What SkyRPG is, how to install the pack and join the server, and what is inside it.

SkyRPG is a 1:1 clone of Hypixel SkyBlock for Minecraft Java Edition 26.3, built on Fabric. You start on your own floating Private Island, level skills, collect resources, build minions, trade on the Bazaar and the Auction House, slay bosses and climb the SkyBlock Level, with Hypixel's items, numbers and look. Every gameplay system is our own mod. Other mods are only used for utilities.
This page tells you what you need to play, how to install it and join, and what the pack adds. Read First steps next.

Your Private Island is yours alone: a small island with a tree, a portal to the Hub and room to build. Everyone starts here, and /is brings you back from anywhere. Place your minions here. See Profiles and islands.
The Hub is the village of Skyhaven, with the shops, the Bank, the Bazaar, the Auction House and Maddox the Slayer, and seven areas on islands around it: the Graveyard, Coal Mine, Farm, Forest, Ruins, Mountain and Wilderness. See Skyhaven and The Hub.
The public islands are shared, and you reach them by launch pads and /warp: the Farming Islands, the Park, the Gold Mine, the Deep Caverns and the Spider's Den. Each needs a skill level to enter. See The Islands.

You play on a profile, and you can keep up to five, each with its own island, inventory, skills and coins. When you die you keep your items and lose half your purse, then wake up on your island. The old survival world is kept only as an archive: nothing in the pack sends you there.

Minecraft Java Edition 26.3 and Prism Launcher (free).
That is all. The SkyRPG instance brings Fabric Loader, Fabric API and every SkyRPG mod, and keeps them current.
The same SkyRPG version as the server. The instance updates itself, so you always match it.

Install Prism Launcher and sign in with your Minecraft account.
Download the SkyRPG instance: SkyRPG-Prism-Instance.zip. Don't unpack it.
In Prism choose Add Instance, then Import, and pick the zip. An instance called SkyRPG appears.
Launch it. The first start downloads the mods, so it takes a moment. A small window shows the progress.

From then on the pack updates itself from GitHub every time you launch. New and changed mods are downloaded, removed ones are deleted. You never need a new zip again. If you are offline, the game starts with the mods you already have.

If you cannot use the instance, the host can give you SkyRPG-<version>.zip. Unpack it. Inside is a mods folder and a HOW-TO-INSTALL.txt. You also need Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer and Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 from Modrinth. You must replace the zip after every update.

Add an instance: Minecraft 26.3, mod loader Fabric (0.19.5 or newer).
Right-click the instance, choose Edit, then Mods, then Add file, and pick every jar from the mods folder.
Launch.

Run the Fabric installer and pick Minecraft 26.3.
Copy every jar from mods into %APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods. Make the folder if it is missing.
Start the fabric-loader-26.3 profile.

Start the game, open Multiplayer and choose Add Server.
Type the address the host gave you.
Ask the host to add your name to the whitelist if you cannot get in.

The SkyRPG title screen and the first-time setup: performance presets, shaders, resource packs, keys and the main settings.

The first time you start the pack, a short setup opens before the main menu. It takes about a minute and tunes the game for your computer. You have to go through every step: on the very first start there is no skip button and Esc does nothing, until you press Finish on the last step. Every step already has a sensible choice picked, so it is just Next, Next, and so on. After that you get the SkyRPG title screen, with a big Play button. Both can be opened again whenever you like, and then the setup can be closed at any time.
The title screen replaces Minecraft's. It shows the world's panorama under a navy tint with slow drifting stars, the SkyRPG name, and these buttons:
Play SkyRPG | Joins the SkyRPG server straight away. If no server address is set, it opens Multiplayer
Singleplayer and Multiplayer | The normal Minecraft screens
Settings | Minecraft's own options (video, sound, controls)
SkyRPG Setup | Opens the first-time setup again
Wiki | Opens this wiki inside the game. If the wiki mod is missing it opens the website instead
Mods | Mod Menu, when it is installed

The footer shows the pack version and the Minecraft version. On wider windows a What's new box lists the latest changes. It is fetched from the website when you start the game, and simply does not appear when you are offline.
It works from a small window to a 4K monitor at any GUI scale. You can press Tab and the arrow keys to move between buttons and Enter to press one, and screen readers read every button.

Play SkyRPG needs the group's Radmin VPN. The server's address starts with 26 and only works while you are connected to the VPN network. If you are not, the game shows "Can't reach the SkyRPG server. Are you connected to the group's VPN (Radmin)?" with Try again and Open Multiplayer buttons.

The address lives in config/skyrpg/welcome.json in your game folder. Edit serverAddress to change where Play joins (for example localhost if you host the server yourself). Leave it empty and Play opens the Multiplayer screen.
If you prefer the plain Minecraft title screen, turn off SkyRPG title screen in K > Settings > Interface.
The setup has six steps. Use Next and Back to move between them. Every choice is applied straight away and saved. When you open it again later you can also close it with Close or Esc at any time.

Welcome. What SkyRPG is: a Hypixel SkyBlock clone, in two lines.
Performance. Pick a preset. The one that suits your computer (from its memory, processor threads and graphics card) is named under the cards, and on the first start it is already applied, so you can just continue. Hover a card to see exactly what it sets.
Visuals. Switch shaders on and choose a shader pack (needs the Iris mod and packs in the shaderpacks folder), and turn resource packs from the resourcepacks folder on or off. The FurfSky Reborn item looks are not in this list: they are always on. Scroll the lists with the mouse wheel. Resource packs reload once when you leave the step.
Controls. The keys that matter: the SkyRPG keys (SkyBlock Menu, map, backpack, wiki lookup), zoom when Zoomify is installed, and movement. Click a key, then press the new one. Esc cancels and Backspace clears. A key shown in red is used by something else too. Open all key bindings opens Minecraft's full Controls screen.
Interface. The settings that matter most: themed chat, message spacing, the HUD, the minimap, the tab list and the SkyRPG title screen. They are the same settings as K > Settings, so they stay in sync.
Done. A summary of what you changed and a Play SkyRPG button.
Potato | Old laptops, integrated graphics | 6 chunks | 5 | Fast | Minimal | Off | 50% | 60 | On
Balanced | Most computers | 10 | 8 | Fancy | Decreased | Fast | 75% | 120 | On
High | Gaming PCs | 16 | 12 | Fancy | All | Fancy | 100% | 240 | Off
Ultra | Strong graphics cards | 24 | 16 | Fabulous | All | Fancy | 150% | Unlimited | Off

Minecraft then shows the graphics mode as Custom, because the preset sets more than the Fast, Fancy and Fabulous buttons. Every preset also sets the biome blend (0, 2, 4 and 6), turns off ambient occlusion on Potato, turns off entity shadows on Potato, and lowers the frame rate when the game is in the background (Potato and Balanced also do that when you are away from the keyboard).
If these mods are installed, the setup also uses them:

Dynamic FPS is switched on.
Dynamic lights (LambDynamicLights) go to off on Potato, fast on Balanced and fancy above.
Sodium and Iris are not changed beyond what the vanilla options already do (Sodium follows the view distance and the other options). Iris is driven for the shader choice.
Without Iris the shader list is hidden.
Zoomify adds its zoom key to the Controls step.
Mod Menu adds the Mods button to the title screen.
Nothing needs them: without any of these mods the setup only changes Minecraft's own options.

On the title screen, press SkyRPG Setup.
In the game, press K, open Settings, and use Show the setup again in the Interface category.
Type /welcome in the chat.
The setup only opens by itself once. It is remembered in config/skyrpg/welcome.json, in the setupVersion entry. Delete that line to see it again at the next start.
Your first hour in SkyRPG: your Private Island, the SkyBlock Menu, the Hub's areas, your first collections and minion, and your first coins.

You start on your Private Island, a small floating island of grass with an oak tree and a portal to the Hub. This page is a route through your first hour: what to open, where to walk, what to collect and where the first coins come from. It follows the same loop as Hypixel SkyBlock: gather, unlock, craft, sell, repeat.

You appear on your island with a welcome in chat. Only you (and the members of a co-op) can build here. Look at the sidebar on the right: it shows the SkyBlock date and time, the area you are in and your purse. The minimap is in the top right corner, and M opens the world map.
Press K to open the SkyBlock Menu. It is the board for everything: Skills, Collections, Recipe Book, Storage, Fast Travel and more. See SkyBlock Menu. Press K again to close it.
/is brings you back to your island from anywhere.

Walk through the portal on the north side of your island. You arrive in the Hub, in the village of Skyhaven, where you walk 60% faster. Nobody can hurt you in the village, and nobody builds here. Take a minute to look at the town: the shops, the Bank, and the NPCs with their names over their heads. See Skyhaven and NPCs.
You can buy a few things right away. Every merchant also buys anything with an NPC price: click an item in the shop's sell panel to sell the whole stack. See NPC Shops.
Sky bridges lead from the village to seven areas, each with something to gather or fight. All of them are in The Hub. The first four are the ones to learn the skills on:
Farm (north-east) | Farming | Harvest Wheat. It grows back
Forest (south-west) | Foraging | Chop Oak. Logs and leaves grow back
Coal Mine (north) | Mining | Mine Coal Ore and Stone. They turn to bedrock for a few seconds, then return
Graveyard (west) | Combat | Kill Graveyard Zombies. Each pays Combat XP and a coin

Every break and kill gives skill XP. The first level of each skill is quick, and it is the key to the launch pads: Farming I, Foraging I, Mining I and Combat I each open the way to a public island (see the Progression guide).
Collections, recipes and your first minion
Collections, recipes and your first minion

Everything you gather counts toward a collection. Open Collections in the SkyBlock Menu to see them: gather enough of an item and you reach the next tier, which unlocks recipes and gives SkyBlock XP. See Collections.
Collections, recipes and your first minion
Open the Recipe Book to see what you can craft. Crafting tables and /craft open a 3 by 3 grid; the Recipe Book fills it for you with Supercraft. See Recipe Book.
Collections, recipes and your first minion

Your first minion is a craft away: a few Cobblestone or Wheat, a few tiers of collection and the recipe from the Recipe Book. Place it on your island, give it room, and come back later to Collect All: it works while you are away. See Minions. Arthur, at the Farm, tells you about them.
Coins sit in your purse, shown in the sidebar. Early on they come from:

Selling. Wheat, logs, ore and mob drops all have an NPC price. Click them in a merchant's sell panel. See NPC Shops.
Mobs. Every kill in the Hub's areas pays a few coins.
Skill levels. Each level pays coins as well as stats.
Minions. What they collect can be sold, or kept for crafting.
The Bazaar, from SkyBlock Level 7: sell materials in bulk at live prices. See Bazaar.
Put coins you will not spend into the Bank, where they are safe when you die. The Banker stands in the middle of the village. See Coins and the bank.
When you die you keep your items but lose half of your purse. Spend or bank your coins before a risky fight.

24 Fairy Souls are hidden around the Hub's islands, and more on the public islands: small glowing pink crystals, on rooftops, under bridges and in tree tops. Click one to collect it. Tia the Fairy, at the Fairy Pond in the Wilderness, turns every five into 10 SkyBlock XP. See The Hub.

Press K and look at the SkyBlock Menu once.
Walk through the portal and meet the village's merchants. Find the Banker and the Bartender.
Cross to the Farm, the Forest and the Coal Mine and gather until each skill is at level 1 or 2.
Kill a few zombies in the Graveyard for Combat XP.
Sell what you gathered, and check the Collections page for new tiers.
Craft your first minion from the Recipe Book and place it on your island.
Go back to the Hub and hunt Fairy Souls on your way to Tia.
Open the Settings page once and glance at the HUD and Map options. See Settings.
Some fights are tougher than they look. The Ruins' wolves attack on sight, and the Hub Crypts' Golden Ghoul has 45,000 health. Stay on the Graveyard and the Farm until your Combat level is up.

The path through SkyBlock, from your Private Island to the Slayers: which island to visit next, which skill levels open the way, and what to build and buy at each stage.

SkyRPG follows Hypixel SkyBlock's loop: gather, unlock, craft, earn, go further. There is no single route, and this page lays out one in six stages: what to gather, which gates open and what to aim for. The levels are the ones the game itself checks: the skill levels on the launch pads, the SkyBlock Level that opens the Bazaar and the Combat levels the slayer tiers need. Everything else is a rough guide.

Gathering gives skill XP, collection progress and coins. Each skill level gives stats, coins and SkyBlock XP. See Skills overview.
Collections count everything you gather. Each tier unlocks recipes, above all your minions, and gives SkyBlock XP. See Collections.
Crafting turns gathered items into enchanted items, minions and gear. The Recipe Book lists every recipe and what unlocks it.
Minions gather while you are away, so your island earns for you. See Minions.
Selling pays for the next step: the NPC shops buy anything with an NPC price, the Bazaar trades materials at live prices and the Auction House trades gear. See NPC Shops.
SkyBlock Level rises with nearly everything you do and opens features along the way. See SkyBlock Leveling.
Every public island is behind a launch pad or gate that asks for a skill level. If you don't have it, you are pushed back and told what is missing.
The Barn | Launch pad on the Hub's Farm | Farming I
The Park | Launch pad in the Hub's Forest | Foraging I
Gold Mine | Gold gate deep in the Hub's Coal Mine | Mining I
Spider's Den | Launch pad behind the Hub's Graveyard | Combat I
Mushroom Desert | Bridge from the Barn | Farming V
Deep Caverns | Lift shaft at the bottom of the Gold Mine | Mining V
Each island you visit also unlocks its /warp.
1. Your island | Learn the menu, place your first minion | Private Island, Skyhaven
2. The Hub | Level each skill to I, meet the merchants | The Hub's areas
3. The first islands | Farm, forage, mine and fight on the public islands | Barn, Park, Gold Mine, Spider's Den
4. The Bazaar | Sell in bulk, grow your minions | SkyBlock Level 7 and up
5. The deep | Mine and farm for rarer goods | Mushroom Desert, Deep Caverns
6. Slayers | Kill the four slayer bosses | Maddox in the Hub
Goal: know where everything is, and have a minion working.

Press K and look through the SkyBlock Menu.
Walk through your island's portal to the Hub, meet Skyhaven's merchants and come back with /is.
Gather the materials for a first minion and craft it from the Recipe Book. Place it on your island.
See First steps and Profiles and islands.
Goal: reach level I in Farming, Foraging, Mining and Combat, which opens the four first launch pads.

Farm: Wheat. Forest: Oak. Coal Mine: Coal and Stone. Graveyard: zombies. See The Hub.
Sell what you don't need, and keep the rest for your collections and recipes.
Find the Fairy Souls on the Hub's islands and bring five at a time to Tia. See The Hub.
Put coins in the Bank. See Coins and the bank.
The Ruins' wolves and the Hub Crypts' ghouls are tough. Come back to them later, for Combat XP and for Sven.
Goal: work each skill where it pays best, and fill your first collections.
Farming | The Barn | Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, Pumpkins and Melons
Foraging | The Park | Birch, Spruce, Dark Oak, Acacia and Jungle wood
Mining | Gold Mine | Stone, Coal, Iron and Gold Ore
Combat | Spider's Den | Spiders, level 2 to 10 around the camp and level 42 on the Mound

The Park's Howling Cave is a good place to fight for wolf drops. The merchants on these islands (the Windmill Operator, Old Shaman Nyko, the Iron and Gold Forgers and Shaggy) sell their own goods. See NPC Shops. New minion recipes unlock as your collections grow.
Goal: SkyBlock Level 7, and a way of making coins that doesn't need you.

SkyBlock Level 7 opens the Bazaar. Sell your materials in bulk, and buy what your recipes need.
Level 5 opens the Wardrobe.
Upgrade your minions: higher tiers work faster and hold more, and fuel and upgrades improve them again. See Minions.
Visit the Blacksmith at Rosetta's forge to reforge your gear. See Reforging.
List gear on the Auction House, or buy it there.
Check the calendar for the day's events.
Minion slots grow with the number of different minions you craft, so craft a new kind before you upgrade an old one.
Goal: Farming V and Mining V, and the rarer ores.

Farming V opens the bridge from the Barn to the Mushroom Desert: Cactus, Sugar Cane, Cocoa Beans and Mushrooms.
Mining V opens the lift from the Gold Mine to the Deep Caverns: six layers, from Coal and Iron down to Diamond and Obsidian. Lift Operators on every layer take you to any layer you have already walked into.
Craft the enchanted versions of what you mine. Collection tiers unlock the recipes for better gear and minions. See Collections.
Talk to Maddox the Slayer in the Hub to start. Each boss is a chain of tiers; a tier needs the one below it beaten, and some also need a Combat level. See Slayers.
Revenant Horror | Graveyard, Hub Crypts | From the start (2,000 coins)
Tarantula Broodfather | Spider's Den | Revenant Horror II beaten
Sven Packmaster | Ruins, the Park's Howling Cave | Tarantula Broodfather II beaten
Voidgloom Seraph | Any area with mobs | Sven Packmaster IV beaten
Slayer levels give stats and SkyBlock XP, and unlock the slayer gear's recipes in the Recipe Book.

Keep every skill moving. Skill levels give stats and coins, and each adds SkyBlock XP.
Fill your collections: they unlock almost everything.
Wear the best gear you have, and reforge it at the Blacksmith. See Weapons, Armour sets and Accessories.
Get a pet for the skill you are levelling. See Pets.
Keep coins in the Bank, because dying costs you half of your purse.
Use the Wardrobe and the Ender Chest to keep your sets and spares. See Storage and Wardrobe.

The extra mods the pack installs for speed and comfort, the zoom key, how to turn shaders on, and performance tips.

Besides the SkyRPG mods, the pack installs a set of well-known Fabric mods. They make the game faster, add a few comfort features and let you use shader packs. All of them are client-side: they change how your own game looks and runs, nothing about the server. The pack keeps them up to date the same way it keeps SkyRPG up to date.
SkyRPG was tested together with every mod on this page (chat, the SkyBlock Menu, HUD and minimap, tab list, effects, 3D item models, the minions, the wiki), also with a shader pack switched on.
Sodium | A much faster renderer. More frames per second and smoother chunk loading.
Sodium Extra and Reese's Sodium Options | More video settings (clouds, animations, fog, FPS counter) in one tidy screen. Find it under Options, Video Settings.
Lithium | Faster game logic, which helps the built-in server and big crowds of mobs.
Entity Culling and More Culling | Skip drawing mobs and blocks you cannot see. A big help in the busy Hub.
ImmediatelyFast | Faster drawing of the HUD, menus and text.
Dynamic FPS | Lowers the frame rate while the window is in the background, so the game stops heating your computer when you tab away.
Zoomify | Hold C to zoom in like a spyglass. Scroll while holding C to zoom further or less.
Mod Menu | A list of the installed mods, with a settings button for those that have one. Open it with the Mods button on the title screen, or the small icon in the game menu.
AppleSkin | Shows how much hunger and saturation food gives, in its tooltip and on the hunger bar.
Mouse Tweaks | Faster inventory handling. Drag with the left or right button to spread or collect items, scroll over a slot to move items, and hold the button to move whole stacks.
Controlling | A search box in the Controls screen, so you can find a key quickly.
Shulker Box Tooltip | Hover a shulker box to see what is inside.
LambDynamicLights | A torch or lava bucket in your hand, and lit mobs and dropped items, light up their surroundings.
3D Skin Layers | Your skin's hat and jacket layers get real depth.
Continuity | Connected glass and other connected textures, for resource packs that use them.
Iris | Shader pack support. See below.
The pack also installs the libraries these mods need (Fabric API, Fabric Language Kotlin, YetAnotherConfigLib, Cloth Config, Placeholder API and Searchables). You never use them directly.

Hold C. The view zooms in smoothly, scrolling changes how far, and letting go zooms back out. Zoomify has its own settings in Mod Menu (change the zoom time, switch between hold and toggle, make zoom move the mouse more slowly). Change the key under Options, Controls, Zoomify. A second key, F6, gives a stronger zoom that also hides the HUD.
Zoom works with a spyglass in your hand too. If you want zoom on the mouse wheel only, set the zoom key in Controls to Unknown.

Shaders add realistic light, shadows, water and clouds. They look beautiful and they cost frames, so they are off by default. The first-time setup (see First launch and setup) can switch them on for you. Three shader packs come with the pack:
Complementary Reimagined | Natural and close to vanilla, with good shadows, water and sky. The one we recommend. | Medium
MakeUp Ultra Fast | Soft light and nicer water for weaker computers. | Light
BSL | Bright, colourful and dramatic. | Heavy
To turn them on in the game:

Press I (Iris: shader pack selection), or open Options, Video Settings, Shader Packs.
Click a shader pack in the list and press Apply.
Press U at any time to switch shaders off and on again without leaving the game. R reloads them.

On the first start the shader takes a few seconds to compile. The game can freeze for a moment.
The Shader Packs screen has Shader Pack Settings for each pack. Lowering the shadow distance and quality is the biggest saving.
Our effects (mob and boss particles, the screen flash and shake) still show with shaders on, and the HUD, the menus and the minimap are not touched.
Shaders ask a lot of your graphics card. If the frame rate drops, choose MakeUp Ultra Fast or switch them off.
More shader packs: drop a .zip into the shaderpacks folder of your game folder (Prism: Folder, Shader Packs) and pick it in the list.

Iris binds "toggle shaders" to K by default, which is the SkyRPG menu key. SkyRPG moves Iris's key to U the first time you start the game with both, so the menu and shaders do not fight. You can change it back in Controls.
SkyBlock items look like Hypixel's because of two extras the pack downloads from Modrinth:
Catharsis | A client mod that reads each item's SkyBlock id, so a resource pack can give every SkyBlock item its own look.
FurfSky Reborn | The resource pack that gives SkyBlock's items, armour and held models their look. Only its item folders load: its menus, hotbar, blocks and fonts never do.
There is no setting for either: they are always on, and they are not in the resource pack list you can toggle. SkyRPG's own screens (the SkyBlock Menu, shops, the Bazaar) are not changed by them.
Two small optional packs sit in your resourcepacks folder. They are not turned on until you choose them in Options, Resource Packs (or in the first-time setup):
Low On Fire | The on-fire overlay sits low on the screen instead of covering it.
Fast Better Grass | Grass blocks show their top texture on the sides, so grass looks fuller.
SkyRPG's own look (menus and icons) comes from its mods and still works with these packs.

Use the Balanced preset in the setup. Open it again with /welcome or K, Settings.
Lower Render Distance first. It is the biggest saving. 10 to 12 chunks is plenty.
Switch Graphics to Fast and set Clouds to Off or Fast on a weak computer.
Give the game memory: 4 GB is the default of the pack and enough for most people. 6 GB helps with shaders. In Prism: Edit, Settings, Java, Memory.
Keep VSync on if you see tearing, off if you want the most frames.
Dynamic FPS only helps while the window is not in front. Alt-tab away when you are idle.
If shaders stutter, lower the shader's shadow distance and use Complementary Reimagined or MakeUp Ultra Fast.
Fancy extras you can turn off in Video Settings (Sodium Extra): animations and particles, and the LambDynamicLights settings.
All of these are files in the config folder of your game folder, and each mod also has a screen in Mod Menu or in the Video Settings:
Iris and the chosen shader pack | config/iris.properties (enableShaders, shaderPack)
The pack only puts its default settings in place the first time. After that your own changes are never overwritten by an update.

First launch and setup
Controls and keys
Settings
The SkyBlock Menu opens everything from one board, as on Hypixel. Fast Travel warps you to your island, the Hub, and each island once you've visited it.
Press the menu key (K unless you changed it in Controls) and the menu opens on the SkyBlock Menu.
On the left is you: your character (it looks at your mouse), your name, the profile you're playing, where you are, the SkyBlock date and time, and your purse.
On the right is everything you can open, in four colour-coded groups. Each tile shows something live about it:
You (gold) | Your Profile, Skills, Collections, SkyBlock Leveling
Gear (purple) | Storage (how many items in how many pages), Wardrobe (the set you wear), Accessory Bag (your accessories, Magical Power), Pets (your pet out), SkyBlock Items
World (aqua) | Fast Travel (warps unlocked), Calendar (today's date), Recipe Book
Account (green) | Profiles (how many of 5), Personal Bank, Settings
The grey Personal Bank tile is still being built (the Banker in the Hub runs the bank for now). Every page is also in the menu's sidebar on the left.
Choose Fast Travel in the SkyBlock Menu, or type /warp <place>. Each warp has a short warm-up: stand still, and you can't warp while you're in combat.

More islands get a warp as they're built. Like on Hypixel, you have to visit an island once before you can warp to it. The first time you arrive, chat says Fast Travel unlocked, and the warp lights up on the Fast Travel page.
Public islands are protected, so you can't break or build on them. The exception is the parts meant to be worked: a farm's crops, a forest's trees, a mine's ore.

In those areas you can break the blocks that belong there. They grow back after a few seconds. Mined ore turns to bedrock until it does.
Monsters keep spawning in fighting areas (like a graveyard), and only there can you fight on a public island.
The sidebar shows which area you're in (for example ⏣ Coal Mine).
Every Hypixel SkyBlock item is in the game with its real name, SkyBlock ID, rarity and stats. With FurfSky Reborn installed, each one looks the way it does on Hypixel.

SkyRPG SkyBlock is being built as a 1:1 copy of Hypixel SkyBlock. The first piece is in: all 5,680 SkyBlock items, from Enchanted Diamond to Hyperion. Each one has Hypixel's name, SkyBlock ID, rarity, category and stats.
Where an item comes from (drops, recipes, shops, minions) arrives with the systems that use it, phase by phase. Until then, admins hand items out with /sbitem.

A SkyBlock item is a normal Minecraft item underneath, like on Hypixel: the Aspect of the End is a diamond sword, and the Summoning Ring is a player head. The item also carries its SkyBlock ID, the same one Hypixel uses.

The pack uses the FurfSky Reborn texture pack, through the Catharsis mod. Both read that ID and give each item its proper look: the Hyperion, Terminator and Necron's armour look like they do on Hypixel. Without the pack you see the base item instead, so a Hyperion is an iron sword. Heads always show their own skin, and leather armour keeps its colour.

FurfSky Reborn belongs to its own team. We never host it; your launcher downloads it from Modrinth along with the pack. It's always on. Only its item and armour looks are used (and its border round the selected hotbar slot); SkyRPG's own screens and menus stay as they are.
SkyBlock items use Hypixel's tooltip layout in SkyRPG's frame:

Rarities run in Hypixel's order: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, Divine (aqua), Special, Very Special, Ultimate and Admin. A Recombobulator (when it arrives) raises an item by one step, up to Divine.
Everything Hypixel puts on items is a SkyRPG stat now, with Hypixel's symbol. On top of the ones SkyRPG already had, these are new:

Combat: Bonus Attack Speed, Ferocity, Ability Damage, True Defense, Swing Range, Health Regen, Vitality and Mending.
Mining: Breaking Power, Pristine, Mining Spread, and Ore, Block, Dwarven Metal and Gemstone Fortune.
Farming and foraging: a Fortune for each crop, plus Fig, Mangrove and Helix Fortune.
Fishing: Double Hook Chance, Treasure Chance and Trophy Fish Chance.
Other: Pet Luck, Bonus Pest Chance, Heat, Cold and Pressure Resistance, Respiration, Fear, Alchemy Wisdom, Tracking and Pull, and the Rift stats.
The skill XP stats are called Wisdom now, as on Hypixel: Farming Wisdom, Mining Wisdom, Foraging Wisdom, Combat Wisdom and Fishing Wisdom.
Some of these stats only do something once their system lands (the Rift, the Garden).

289 items carry Hypixel's ability, shown on the tooltip as Ability: Instant Transmission RIGHT CLICK, with its description, Mana Cost and Cooldown. Using one spends its mana (less with Ultimate Wise) and starts its cooldown (the item greys over while it recharges). Ability damage grows with Intelligence (+1% per point) and Ability Damage.
Instant Transmission | Aspect of the End, Aspect of the Void | Teleports you 8 blocks ahead (stopping before walls), +50 Speed for 3 seconds
Dragon Rage | Aspect of the Dragons | 12,000 damage to every monster in front of you, with big knockback
Ice Spray | Ice Spray Wand | 17,000 damage in a cone, freezing what it hits for 5 seconds
Molten Wave | Midas Staff | 12,000 damage in a wave in front of you
Giant's Slam | Giant's Sword | 100,000 damage to everything near you
Showtime | Bonzo's Staff | A balloon that explodes where it lands for 1,000 damage
Guided Bat | Spirit Sceptre | A bat that explodes for 2,000 damage
Ice Bolt | Frozen Scythe | 1,000 damage and slowness for 5 seconds
Rapid Fire | Jerry-chine Gun | A bullet for 500 damage that knocks you back
Fire Blast | Ember Rod | Fireballs that burst for 30 damage
Speed Boost | Rogue Sword | +100 Speed for 30 seconds
Small / Medium / Big / Huge Heal | Wands of Healing, Mending, Restoration and Atonement | Heals you every second for a few seconds (wand heals don't stack)
Every other ability shows on its item but doesn't do anything yet.

Right-click a Booster Cookie to eat it: 4 days of the Cookie Buff, counted in real time (each cookie adds 4 more days). While it lasts you get +15 Magic Find and +5 Wisdom in every skill, and you keep your coins when you die (normally a death costs half your purse). /cookie says how long it has left. The buff is per profile.
A SkyBlock item doesn't act like the vanilla item it's made from:
Bows, crossbows, fishing rods, ender pearls and wearable items work as normal. Nothing wears out.

The SkyBlock Items page in the K menu has every SkyBlock item in a grid, sorted by rarity. Type to search by name or SkyBlock ID, and hover an item to see its full tooltip. Admins can click an item to get one.
/sbitem <id> [count] | Gives you an item. Type its SkyBlock ID in lower case (/sbitem aspect_of_the_end), with - for a : (wool-6 is WOOL:6).
/sbitem give <players> <id> [count] | Gives items to other players.
/sbitem search <text> | Lists up to 40 items whose name or ID contains the text. Hover to see one, click to get it.
Up to five SkyBlock profiles, each with its own private island, inventory, skills and coins. Switch between them, visit other players' islands, and team up in a co-op.

Like on Hypixel, you play SkyBlock on a profile. Each profile is a separate playthrough: its own private island and its own inventory, ender chest, skills, collections, pets and coins. You can have up to five profiles and switch between them whenever you like.
Every profile gets a fruit for a name, picked at random: Apple, Banana, Blueberry and so on. The first time you join, everything you already had becomes your first profile, so nothing is lost.
Each profile has a small floating island of its own: grass over dirt and stone, an oak tree, and a portal to the Hub on the north side.

Building. Only the profile's members can break and place blocks on an island. Each island has a build area of 160 by 160 blocks around its centre.
The portal. Walk through the portal to warp to the Hub. The Hub's big portal brings you back to your island.
/is (also /island and /warp home) warps you to your island from anywhere, after a short warm-up. You have to stand still, and you can't warp while you're in combat.
Dying on an island puts you back on your own island.
/visit <player> warps you to the island of the profile that player is playing. As a guest you can look around but you can't break, place or open anything.

Open the K menu and choose Profile Management. It lists your profiles, shows which one you're playing, and has a Switch button on each of the others. There's also a Create button while you have fewer than five. Both ask for a second click, because they reconnect you to the server for a moment.
There are commands for the same things:
/profiles | Lists your profiles. Click [Switch] next to one to play it, or [Create a new profile].
/profiles create | Starts a new profile on a new island.
A new profile starts with nothing, on its own island. Your other profiles stay exactly as you left them.
A co-op is a profile shared by several players. They share the island, and each member keeps their own inventory and skills on it.

While playing the profile you want to share, type /coopadd <player>.
The other player clicks [Accept] in chat, or types /coop accept <you>, within 5 minutes.
They get a new profile that's a member of your co-op, and they start on your island.
Every member can build on a co-op island.
Like on Hypixel, you keep your items when you die, but you lose half the coins in your purse. Coins in the bank are safe.
The SkyBlock calendar runs on Hypixel's own clock, so the date here is the date on Hypixel. A day lasts 20 minutes, and the year has twelve months of festivals.
SkyBlock has its own calendar, and it runs on Hypixel's clock: the date in SkyRPG is the same as the date on Hypixel at that moment.
A SkyBlock day | 20 minutes (one Minecraft day)
A year | 12 months (124 hours, about 5 days)
The months are Early Spring, Spring, Late Spring, Early Summer, Summer, Late Summer, Early Autumn, Autumn, Late Autumn, Early Winter, Winter and Late Winter. Year 1 began on June 11, 2019.
The sky follows the calendar: at 6am on the SkyBlock clock the sun comes up, and at 7pm night falls.
The SkyBlock sidebar on the right of your screen shows, from the top:
Move it, resize it or hide it in the HUD editor (K, Settings, HUD, Edit HUD layout).
Open the K menu and choose Calendar and Events. It shows:
Hoppity's Hunt | All spring: Early Spring 1st to Late Spring 31st
Traveling Zoo | Early Summer 1st to 3rd, and Early Winter 1st to 3rd
Jerry's Workshop | All of Late Winter
Season of Jerry | Late Winter 24th to 26th
New Year Celebration | Late Winter 29th to 31st
Jacob's Farming Contest | Every third day, from the 2nd (on the real clock, every hour at :15)
The calendar already shows these events. Each one starts working in game when its system arrives (the Spooky Festival with its mobs and candy, Jacob's contests with the Garden, and so on).
Skyhaven and the areas around it: the Graveyard, Coal Mine, Farm, Forest, Ruins, Mountain and Wilderness, their mobs and resources, and the Fairy Souls hidden on them.

The Hub is where everyone meets: the village of Skyhaven in the middle, with the shops, the Bank, the Bazaar and the Auction House, and seven islands around it, joined to the village by sky bridges. Each island is one of Hypixel SkyBlock's Hub areas, with the same purpose, mobs and resources, built as a floating island. The sidebar shows the area you're in.
Graveyard | west | Combat: Graveyard Zombies, Zombie Villagers at night
Coal Mine | north | Mining: Coal and Stone; the Hub Crypts below
Farm | north-east | Farming: five Wheat fields
Ruins | far west, past the Forest | Combat: Wolves and Old Wolves
Mountain | south | Climbing, a Carrot farm inside, High Level's Skeletons
Wilderness | east | Fishing, the Fairy Pond, the Tavern and the Dark Auction

Breaking blocks is only allowed where an area lets you: the Coal Mine's Coal Ore and Stone, the Farm's Wheat, the Forest's Oak logs and leaves, the Mountain's Carrots. What you break grows back after a few seconds, so there's always more. Everything else in the Hub is protected.

The Hub's mobs have Hypixel's names and stats. Killing one pays its Combat XP and coins straight into your purse, and counts for slayer quests (a Crypt Ghoul adds its 36 Combat XP to a Revenant Horror quest, not a plain zombie's 6). None of them burn in daylight.
Golden Ghoul | Hub Crypts (one at a time) | 50 | 45,000 | 800 | 50 | 100
Old Wolf | Ruins (two at a time) | 50 | 15,000 | 720 | 40 | 40
The Ruins' wolves attack anyone who comes near. Night mobs leave at sunrise.

West of the village, over the bridge from its west edge. A dark island of podzol and moss: rows of graves inside an iron fence, dead trees and cobwebs, and the chapel with the Emerald Altar. In the chapel's west aisle, barred stairs lead down towards the Hub Crypts. Pat, in his house by the gate, sells Flint and Gravel. At the back, a launch pad takes you to the Spider's Den (needs Combat I).
Revenant Horror quests are best done here: the zombies fill the bar and the boss can rise among the graves.

North of the village, reached from the Starwatch islet. A rocky hill with a timber-framed mine entrance. Inside, tunnels and three caverns of Stone and Coal Ore (both become bedrock for a few seconds when mined), with rails, posts and lanterns. A trail climbs to the summit outside.

Stairs from the first cavern lead down to the Hub Crypts: deepslate corridors and burial rooms where Crypt Ghouls roam, and a gilded room where a Golden Ghoul waits. /warp crypt takes you there once you've been to the Coal Mine. Deep in the mine, a gold-trimmed gate opens onto the Gold Mine: walk in (needs Mining I).

North-east, over the bridge from the Bazaar islet's north end. Five fields of Wheat that grow back (floating crystals hang above them), scarecrows, a windmill, a well and the Farmer's shack. Arthur stands by a Wheat Minion on display and talks about minions. A launch pad takes you to The Barn (needs Farming I).

South-west, over the bridge from the village's south-west edge. A thick Oak forest with big old oaks; logs and leaves grow back. The Lumber Jack lives in the log cabin near the path. A launch pad takes you to The Park (needs Foraging I), and a second bridge leads west to the Ruins.

Far west, over the bridge from the Forest. A ruined castle: broken walls and towers, the great hall with its fallen throne, arches and rubble, and a wolf den in the rocks. Wolves and Old Wolves roam the courtyard, so Sven Packmaster quests are done here. The Lonely Philosopher stands on the north-west tower. /warp castle takes you here once you've visited.

South of the village, over the bridge from the Wildgate islet. A snowy peak with a path winding to the top, where Scoop has his cabin. A tunnel at the foot leads into a cave of Carrots that grow back. On the mountainside: the arch to the Dungeon Hub (coming soon) and a hot air balloon with Amelia and Christopher.
Behind the mountain lies High Level: a huge wooden door between two stone knights, where Skeletons come out at night.

East of the village, over the bridge from the Bazaar islet's east end. Meadows and trees, a stream, the Fairy Pond with Tia the Fairy on her rock, and a fishing lake with Fisherman Gerald's hut and dock. Shifty and Lucius are in the Tavern; Sirius stands outside the Dark Auction house next door (the auction itself is coming). /warp da takes you there once you've visited.

24 Fairy Souls are hidden around the Hub's islands (three or four on each): small glowing pink crystals, on rooftops, under bridges, in crypts and tree tops. A soul you haven't found yet sparkles. Click one to collect it: "SOUL! You found a Fairy Soul!", with how many you have on the Hub and in total. Each profile finds its own.
Bring them to Tia the Fairy at the Fairy Pond. She exchanges them five at a time: each exchange gives 10 SkyBlock XP (see SkyBlock Leveling).
On Hypixel some exchanges also unlock Backpack slots; that comes with backpacks. The other islands have their own souls (see The Islands); Tia takes them all.
/warp crypt | the Hub Crypts | the Coal Mine
/warp da | the Dark Auction | the Wilderness
The rest of the Hub is a walk over the bridges. See also Profiles and islands, Slayers and Collections.

Hypixel's Crystal Hollows - a huge generated cave world under the Dwarven Mines. Gemstones, Hard Stone and treasure chests, its five zones and their mobs, the Crystal Nucleus, Commissions, and how to get in.

The Crystal Hollows are a huge cave world under the Dwarven Mines, 512 by 512 blocks of Hard Stone with caverns, a lava sea and veins of gemstones. Unlike everywhere else, what you mine here is gone for good: you dig your own tunnels, as on Hypixel. The whole world is made anew once a week (Hypixel's lobbies close too), with fresh gemstones.

Talk to Gwendolyn at The Lift in the Dwarven Mines. You need Mining XII and Heart of the Mountain IV. She sells a Crystal Hollows Pass: 10,000 coins for 6 hours (real time). With a pass, talking to her sends you down to the Crystal Nucleus. When the pass runs out you're taken back to the Dwarven Mines; the pad in the Nucleus goes back any time.
Jungle | north-west | Amethyst (purple) | Sludge, Thyst | the Jungle Temple (Odawa, the Kalhuiki Door Guardian)
Mithril Deposits | north-east | Jade (lime); Mithril and Titanium | Team Treasurite Grunts | the Mines of Divan (the four Keepers)
Goblin Holdout | south-west | Amber (orange) | Goblins, Knifethrowers, Weaklings | the Goblin Queen's Den and King Yolkar's tower
Precursor Remnants | south-east | Sapphire (light blue) | Automatons | the Lost Precursor City (Professor Robot)
Magma Fields | everywhere under y 64 | Topaz (yellow) | Yogs | Khazad-dûm
Crystal Nucleus | the middle | - | - | where you arrive: Emissary Sisko, Gemma, Geonathan Greatforge
Ruby (red) is in every zone, and Jasper (magenta) turns up in small rare veins.
Hard Stone (all the stone) | 50 | 4 | Hard Stone
Amethyst, Jade, Amber, Sapphire | 3,000 | 7 | its Rough gem, 2 Gemstone Powder
Mithril, Titanium | as in the Dwarven Mines | 4, 5 | Mithril, Titanium, Mithril Powder

Gemstones use Gemstone Fortune, Mithril and Titanium Mining Fortune and Dwarven Metal Fortune. Gemstone Powder only comes from the Hollows (gemstones, treasure chests and Commissions); it pays for the higher Heart of the Mountain perks. Gems go in items' slots: see Gemstones.

Every Hard Stone you mine has a 1 in 500 chance (more with the Great Explorer perk) to uncover a treasure chest right where it was. Only you can open it, within a minute: right-click it for 3 to 6 rolls of Gemstone Powder (200-500 each), Mithril Powder, the zone's Rough and Flawed gems, Treasurite, and now and then an Oil Barrel, Sludge Juice, Ascension Rope, Wishing Compass, Jungle Key, Goblin Egg or, very rarely, a Pickonimbus 2000.

The great cavern in the middle, where you arrive: the five crystal pedestals (Jade, Amber, Topaz, Sapphire, Amethyst), Emissary Sisko with the Hollows' Commissions, Gemma with the Gemstone Grinder, and the pad back to the Dwarven Mines.

Emissary Sisko has the Hollows' own board (the Dwarven Mines' is separate): Hard Stone Miner (1,000), a Gemstone Collector for each gem (100), Chest Looter (3 treasure chests), and slayers for Goblins (13), Automatons (13), Sludges (25), Yogs (13), Thysts (5) and Team Treasurite (13). Each pays 400 HotM XP, 1,500 Gemstone Powder and 10,000 Mining XP; your first four of the day (on either board) pay +900 HotM XP.

Not yet: the crystals and the Nucleus loot, the Jungle Temple's key and parkour, Divan's metal detector, the Goblin Queen and King Yolkar's scent, Professor Robot's parts, Bal, Boss Corleone, Scatha and the worms, the treasure chests' lockpick, and the Fairy Grottos.
Hypixel's Dwarven Mines - a cavern kingdom of Mithril and Titanium under the Deep Caverns. Its areas, mobs and NPCs, Commissions, the Forge, and how to get there.

The Dwarven Mines are a huge cavern kingdom of dwarves under the Deep Caverns, Hypixel SkyBlock's second mining island. It's where you mine Mithril and Titanium, do Commissions for the King, level up your Heart of the Mountain and forge gear at the Forge.

Getting there: the launch pad on the Obsidian Sanctuary floor, at the bottom of the Deep Caverns (Mining XII). You arrive at The Lift, on the east side of the Dwarven Village; a pad there takes you back. After your first visit, /warp mines takes you to The Lift and /warp forge to the Forge.

Dwarven Village | the middle of the north | The square with Emissary Eliza, the bank (Banker Broadjaw), the Blacksmith (reforging), Bubu (pickaxes), Bulvar (minions), the Station Master, Old Man Garry, Don Expresso, Fragilis and Rhys
Dwarven Tavern | the village's north-east | Brynmor's bar (Powder Pie and other food) and the regulars
The Lift | the village's east end | Where you arrive; Emissary Braum, the Lift Operator, the pad back to the Deep Caverns
Upper Mines | the far north-west | A high cavern of Mithril and Titanium, with Treasure Hoarders; Emissary Fraiser
Rampart's Quarry | west | A terraced quarry full of Mithril; Emissary Carlton
Far Reserve | south-west | Mithril veins, wooden platforms and rails
Goblin Burrows | the far south-west | Gold-lined tunnels of Goblins; mineable Gold Ore
Gates to the Mines | south of the village | The great carved gate over the Forge
The Forge | under the gates | The Forger, Fred and Jotraeline Greatforge, around a lava fall
Cliffside Veins | the middle | A deep chasm of Mithril and Titanium; the Cult of the Fallen Star's cave; Emissary Ceanna
Divan's Gateway | south of the Veins | A great bridge-gate over a cavern; Bylma
The Mist | under Divan's Gateway | A foggy ice cavern of Ghosts
Great Ice Wall | the far south | A wall of ice with Pure Emerald in it, and Glacite Walkers
Lava Springs | east | Lava falls and Mithril; Emissary Lilith
Palace Bridge | east | The long bridge to the palace, over the Royal Mines
Royal Mines | under the bridge | Mithril, Titanium, every ore and the Pure Ores (blocks of each); Emissary Wilson, Marigold
Royal Palace | the far south-east | The King and Queen Mismyla, the Grand Library and the Puzzler
Aristocrat Passage | south of the Royal Mines | The corridor down to the Great Ice Wall
There are 11 Fairy Souls in the Mines.

Everything in the Mines uses Hypixel's mining rules (see Mining): Mithril needs a pickaxe with Breaking Power 4, Titanium Breaking Power 5. Mined blocks turn to bedrock and come back after a few seconds.
Mithril | gray wool, cyan terracotta | 500 | 4 | 1 Mithril | 1
Pure Ores | ore blocks (Royal Mines) | 600 | 3 | the ore's item | -

Mithril and Titanium count Mining Fortune and pay 45 and 100 Mining XP. Every Mithril block you mine has a 0.5% chance to turn into Titanium instead of bedrock (more with the Titanium Insanium perk). Mithril Powder only drops here; it's what Heart of the Mountain perks cost.
Goblins sometimes drop a Goblin Egg, Treasure Hoarders Starfall, Glacite Walkers a Glacite Jewel. Ghosts are invisible charged creepers: they never explode, but they hit hard if they touch you.
Talk to the King in the Royal Palace or any Emissary for the Commissions board. Each commission is a task:
Mithril Miner | Mine 350 Mithril anywhere in the Mines
Area Mithril | Mine 250 Mithril in Lava Springs, Cliffside Veins, Rampart's Quarry, the Upper Mines or the Royal Mines
Area Titanium | Mine 10 Titanium in one of those areas
Goblin Slayer | Slay 100 Goblins (Knifethrowers and Fireslingers count)
Glacite Walker Slayer | Slay 50 Glacite Walkers
Treasure Hoarder Puncher | Damage Treasure Hoarders 10 times

When one is done, go back to the King or an Emissary and click it for its rewards: HotM XP (100 at HotM 1, 200 at HotM 2, 400 from HotM 3), 500 Mithril Powder and 5,000 Mining XP. Your first 4 commissions each day also give +900 HotM XP. A new commission takes the finished one's place.
You have 2 slots; a third opens after 100 commissions, and Core of the Mountain level 3 adds a fourth.

The Forger in the Forge (/warp forge) forges Hypixel's 123 Forge recipes: Refined Mithril, Mithril and Titanium pickaxes and drills, Golden Plates, Gemstone gear, Travel Scrolls, pets and more. The Forge opens at Heart of the Mountain 2.

The top row shows your slots: 2 at HotM 2, one more each tier up to HotM 6, and one from Core of the Mountain level 2.
Below are the recipes, each with its materials (green when you have enough), coins and time. Click one to start it in a free slot; its materials and coins are taken.
Forging takes the recipe's time in real time, even while you're offline. You get a message when it's ready; click the slot to take the item.
The Quick Forge perk takes 10.5% to 30% off every forge time.
Some recipes need a higher HotM tier, shown on the recipe.

Not yet: the King's rotation (one King for now), mining events (Goblin Raids, Fallen Stars, 2x Powder, Raffles), Golden and Diamond Goblins, Powder Ghasts, the Puzzler's and Fetchur's daily tasks, the Royal Pigeon. The Crystal Hollows and the Glacite Tunnels have pages of their own.

Hypixel's Glacite Tunnels under the Dwarven Mines - the Dwarven Base Camp, the Cold, Glacite, Tungsten, Umber, four new gemstones, their commissions, the Glacite Mineshafts and the Fossil Research Center.

The Glacite Tunnels are a maze of icy tunnels below the Dwarven Mines, for miners at the top of the Heart of the Mountain. At their north end is the Dwarven Base Camp, a warm outpost around a campfire.

Talk to the Ticket Master at the minecart station in the Dwarven Mines (beside Gwendolyn). You need Heart of the Mountain 7, and the first time a Secret Railroad Pass, which you forge at the Forge (a Flawless Ruby, 2 Refined Mithril and 8 Corleonite). After that the ride is free, and /warp base takes you there once you've been. The Ticket Master at the Base Camp takes you back up.
Ticket Master | Back to the Dwarven Mines
Cold Enjoyer, Dulin, Scout Plinius | Tips about the Cold and the Tunnels
Dr. Stone, Researcher Beryl, Fossil Excavator | The Fossil Research Center
Out in the Tunnels you get colder: 1 Cold every 5 seconds, slower with Cold Resistance (5 x (1 + Cold Resistance / 100) seconds) and four times as fast in water. The sidebar shows it.
over your Cold Resistance | each point takes 0.5% off your Mining Speed
100 | you freeze and wake up at the Base Camp
The Base Camp warms you up at once, and so does leaving the Tunnels. Cold Resistance comes from Cold Resistance potions (Alchemy), pets (the Glacite Golem, Mammoth, Penguin...) and gear.
Everything here needs Breaking Power 9 (Hard Stone needs 4). Blocks become bedrock and grow back after 20 seconds.
Glacite | Packed Ice | 6,000 | 1 Glacite, 2 Glacite Powder
Tungsten | Cobblestone (and its slabs and stairs), Clay | 5,600 | 1 Tungsten (Clay: 3), 1 Glacite Powder
Umber | Terracotta, Brown Terracotta, Red Sandstone | 5,600 | 1 / 2 / 3 Umber, 1 Glacite Powder
Aquamarine, Onyx, Citrine, Peridot | blue, black, brown and green stained glass | 5,200 | 4 Rough gems, 2 Gemstone Powder
Mithril, Titanium | as in the Dwarven Mines |  | as there
Mining Fortune and Dwarven Metal Fortune give more Glacite, Tungsten and Umber; Gemstone Fortune more gems. Glacite Powder is the Heart of the Mountain's third powder.

Emissary Lissandra's board: collect 1,500 Glacite, Tungsten, Umber, Aquamarine, Citrine, Onyx or Peridot, slay 50 Glacite Walkers (in the Dwarven Mines), enter a Glacite Mineshaft, loot 2 Frozen Corpses, find a Suspicious Scrap, or slay 10 Glacite Maniacs. Each pays 400 HotM XP (750 at HotM 10), 1,500 Glacite Powder (3,000 at HotM 10) and 25,000 Mining XP.

Every block you mine in the Tunnels has a 1 in 2,000 chance to open a Mineshaft portal beside you. It can't take forever: each block also counts toward a sure one (2,000 points: Mithril 2, Glacite, Tungsten and Umber 4, gemstones and Titanium 8). The portal stays for 30 seconds; right-click it to go in.

A mineshaft is yours alone: a long tunnel with side rooms, its walls full of one kind of ore. There are 16 kinds: Titanium, Tungsten, Umber, each of the twelve gemstones (Opal only comes from here) and the Fairy mineshaft with every gemstone at once. The kind you mined last comes up more often. Ore you mine in a mineshaft doesn't grow back.

Frozen Corpses (1 to 3) | Right-click to loot: the Lapis Corpse is free, the Umber Corpse needs an Umber Key, the Tungsten Corpse a Tungsten Key, and the Fairy mineshaft's Vanguard Corpses a Skeleton Key. Each gives 3 to 8 picks from Hypixel's loot table (gems, Glacite and keys, enchanted books, Suspicious Scrap...).

Glacite Maniacs (3) | The Glacite Mutt, Bowman, Caver and Mage, level 173 to 177. Only a mining tool hurts them: every hit takes 8% of their health. They drop 50 Glacite Powder, Enchanted Glacite, sometimes a Fine gemstone (5%), a Glacite Jewel (4%) or a Glacite Shard (0.1%).
Suspicious Scrap | 1 in 200 for each block you mine, half as likely after each one you find.

The Cold keeps building in there, and faster the longer you stay (+0.25 vulnerability every 150 seconds). The ladder at the start takes you back to the Base Camp with a Glacite Powder bonus: 1,000, plus 500 for each Suspicious Scrap, 250 for each corpse you looted and 10 for each point of Cold. Freezing takes you back too, without the bonus. A mineshaft nobody is in is gone after a minute.

The Heart of the Mountain's Glacite Powder perks help here: Surveyor, No Stone Unturned, Gifts from the Departed, Dead Man's Chest, Vanguard Seeker, Mineshaft Mayhem, Rags to Riches and Eager Adventurer.
The hut at the west of the Base Camp, with the Fossil Excavator by its door.

The Fossil Excavator (HotM 7) digs for treasure and fossils. You need a chisel (kept) and a Suspicious Scrap (used up). The dig is a 9 x 6 bed of dirt: each click uses one of your chisel's charges and uncovers a tile.

Uncovering plain dirt can highlight a tile (a gold star) with something under it: a treasure, or, once you've found a fossil, more of the fossil. 8 to 11 treasures are buried in each dig: Fossil Essence (10-40), Glacite Powder (1,000-10,000), Enchanted Glacite, Umber or Tungsten, Flawed or Fine Tunnels gemstones, Paleontologist books, and rarely Fossil the Fish. One dig in ten also hides a fossil (Clubbed, Footprint, Spine, Tusk, Ugly or Webbed): uncover all of it to get it; a part of it gives Fossil Essence (half a point for each percent). When the charges run out (or you press Finish) you get everything you uncovered.

Dr. Stone takes one of each kind of fossil (the six above and the Claw Fossil): each gives 25,000 Mining XP, 25,000 Glacite Powder, 5,000 HotM XP and 10 SkyBlock XP, and all seven another 50,000 Glacite Powder and 10,000 HotM XP.
Researcher Beryl sells Suspicious Scrap for 100 Fossil Essence, and salvages a scrap for 5 or a fossil Dr. Stone already has for 50 (the Claw 25). /essence shows your essence.
Not yet: chisel gemstone slots, the Fossil Muncher, the Great Glacite Lake and Grandpa Wolf.
Ender Chest pages of 45 slots each, a Wardrobe for nine armour sets, and Hypixel's Sacks that gathered materials go straight into.

Open the K menu and choose Storage, or type /storage. Using an ender chest anywhere in the world opens it too. It has two parts: your Wardrobe and your Ender Chest pages. Each card shows a peek at what's inside, so you can see which page holds what. Click a card to open it.
Both belong to your profile: each profile has its own pages and its own Wardrobe.
Each Ender Chest page holds 45 slots. You start with 2 pages, and there are 9 in all. More pages will unlock with SkyBlock Leveling once it arrives.
The Ender Chest screen has a tab for every page down its left side. Click one to switch pages without closing the screen; locked pages are greyed out. The tab under them opens the Wardrobe.

/ec opens page 1, and /ec <page> opens any page you have.
Shift-click an ender chest to place things against it without opening Storage.
The first time you use Storage, whatever was in your old 27-slot ender chest moves into page 1.

The Wardrobe saves up to 9 armour sets and lets you swap between them in one click. Open it from the Storage page, the tab in the Ender Chest screen, or type /wardrobe. As on Hypixel, it opens at SkyBlock Level 5 (see SkyBlock Leveling).
Each set is a card with a model of you wearing it. The model turns slowly, and towards your mouse when you point at it. Point at a model to see everything that set gives you, added up.

Under each model are the set's four slots: helmet and chestplate, then leggings and boots. Put armour in to save a set. Each slot only takes its kind of armour, and shift-clicking armour from your inventory puts it in the first free slot.
The button under each card shows its state:
Empty: nothing saved yet.
Wear: click to put this set on.
Worn (the card glows green): you're wearing it. Click again (it says Take off) to take it off.
Wearing another set puts the one you had on back into its own card first.
If what you're wearing didn't come from the Wardrobe, it goes into your inventory, so you need room for it.
The set you're wearing stays on its card, so you can change a piece there and it changes on you too.

Sacks hold materials so they don't fill your inventory. There are Hypixel's 28 kinds: Mining, Combat, Foraging, Fishing, Agronomy, Husbandry, their Enchanted versions, Gemstone, Dwarven Mines, Crystal Hollows, Slayer, Nether, Dragon and more, each holding its own list of items (a Mining Sack holds Cobblestone, Coal, Iron, Gold, Mithril, Titanium...).

Right-click a sack to add it to your Sacks (it's used up). Whatever you're carrying that it holds goes in straight away.
After that, what you gather that a sack holds (mined, farmed, chopped, fished or picked up) goes straight into it instead of your inventory. Every few seconds chat says how much went in: "[Sacks] +128 items. (Last 5s.)"
A sack holds a fixed amount of each item: Beginner 640, Small 2,240, Medium 6,720, Large 20,160 (Gemstone Sacks 128,000 to 2,560,000). When it's full, the rest goes to your inventory. A bigger sack of the same kind replaces the smaller one's size.
/sacks shows every sack you have and what's in it. Click an item to take a stack out, shift-click to fill your inventory with it; Insert inventory puts everything the sacks hold away.
/gfs <item> <amount> takes items out without opening the menu (/gfs coal 64).
Sacks belong to your profile. Gear never goes in a sack, only materials.
/ec [page] | Opens an Ender Chest page (page 1 if you leave the number out).
/storage unlock <players> <pages> | Admins: sets how many Ender Chest pages players have (1 to 9).

Hypixel's Dungeons - the Dungeon Hub and Mort, runs through a new map every time, keys and Wither doors, the Blood room and the Watcher, Bonzo, the score, reward chests, the Catacombs level and the five classes.

The Catacombs are Hypixel SkyBlock's Dungeons: you and your party (up to 5) go down into a crypt that's laid out anew every run, clear its rooms, open the Blood room, beat its boss, and open a reward chest.
/warp dungeon_hub (it unlocks the first time you're there). The crypt at the north end is the way into the Catacombs, and Mort stands in front of it.
Mort | Pick your class and a floor, and in you go
Malik | Adds stars to dungeon items for essence
Croesus | Keeps reward chests you left behind (later)

Party Finder (the button on Mort's screen): a party's leader lists the party for a floor (◀ ▶ to pick it); anyone not in a party can join a listing with room, and the leader is told their class. A listing goes after 30 minutes, when it's full, or when the leader leaves.
Talk to Mort: click a class (Healer, Mage, Berserk, Archer, Tank), then a floor. Your party's leader picks the floor and takes everyone in. Each floor needs a Catacombs level (and a Combat level):
Every run is a new map: a grid of rooms (some long, square or L-shaped) joined by doors. You start in the Entrance (green); the timer starts after 5 seconds.

Rooms: their mobs appear when you first walk in. Mobs with a ✯ before their name are star mobs: kill them all and the room is cleared.
Keys and doors: some doors are black Wither doors. Clearing the right room drops a Wither Key; walk into it, then right-click the door. The Blood room's red door needs the Blood Key the same way.
Secrets: hidden chests, items lying on ledges, and bats. Each holds essence or a dungeon item (Spirit Leaps, Healing Tissue, traps...). They count toward your score.
The Fairy room (pink) is a quiet room; it counts as cleared when you walk in.
Blessings: solving a puzzle, beating a miniboss and one secret chest in five bless the whole party for the rest of the run. Their levels add up (I on Floor I, up to IV on Floor VII, one more in Master Mode). Per level: Life +3% Health, Power +2% Strength and Crit Damage, Stone +2% Defense, Wisdom +2% Intelligence and Speed, Time +2% Health, Defense, Strength and Intelligence.
Minibosses (from Floor II): a room's strongest mob is sometimes a miniboss: the Lost Adventurer, Angry Archaeologist (Floor III+), Shadow Assassin (V+), Frozen Adventurer (VI+) or King Midas (VII). Beating one blesses the party.
Crypts: some rooms hide a Crypt Undead. Each one killed is +1 Bonus score, up to 5. The sidebar counts them.
The Mimic (Floor VI and up): one secret chest is alive. Kill it for +2 Bonus score ("Mimic Killed!").
Puzzles (purple rooms; Floor I has one, later floors more). Solve one and its room is cleared; get it wrong (or leave it) and it costs 14 Skill score:
Three Weirdos: three people before three chests. Talk to each; exactly one of them tells the truth. Open the chest with the reward.
Higher Or Lower: ten blazes float with their health over their heads. Kill them in the order the sign says (lowest to highest, or highest to lowest).
Tic Tac Toe: right-click a white tile on the floor to play. The AI never loses, so a draw is the way to solve it; if it wins, you fail.
The Blood room: opening it wakes the Watcher, who sends his undead in waves. Kill them all and he opens the way to the boss.
The fairy in the Fairy room revives everyone who's dead, once a run, when someone alive walks up to it.
Dying makes you a ghost: you float, unseen, and can't fight or open anything, until the boss room (everyone comes back for the boss). If the whole party is dead, the run fails.
The sidebar shows the run: time, rooms cleared, secrets found, your keys, and your team with their class and health.
Each floor ends with its boss (a health bar shows at the top):
I | Bonzo | 250,000 | Throws balloons that burst around you and calls undead. When he falls he gets back up once ("Oh, I'm not done yet!"), faster.
II | Scarf | 1,000,000 | Shielded while his Undead Warrior, Archer, Priest and Mage live. Then he fights, blinking around, burning his target and calling archers.
III | The Professor | 3,000,000 | Shielded behind four Guardians. At half health he calls two more and speeds up.
IV | Thorn | 4 hits | A floating spirit only the Spirit Bow can hurt. Spirit Wolves and a Spirit Bear come; whoever kills the bear gets a Spirit Bow with one arrow. Four hits and he's done.
V | Livid | 7,000,000 | Nine Livids in nine colours. The real one's colour is the wool block in the middle; hitting a fake hurts you.

VI | Sadan | 40,000,000 | Survive his Terracotta army for a minute, then beat his four Giants (Diamond Giant, Bigfoot, L.A.S.R., Jolly Pink Giant, 25,000,000 each), then Sadan himself. Giants stomp the ground around them.

VII | Maxor, Storm, Goldor, Necron | 100M, 400M, 750M, 1B | Maxor is shielded until both Energy Crystals are carried to their pads (walk into a crystal, right-click a pad). Storm only takes damage for 10 seconds after someone pulls down a Pillar. Goldor hurts everyone every few seconds until all four Terminals are done. Necron can always be hurt, and blasts everything around him at 80% and 5%.
Beat Floor VII and Mort's screen gets a Master Mode switch: the same seven floors, much harder.

Each Master floor needs a higher Catacombs (and Combat) level: 24 for M1, then 2 more a floor, up to 36 for M7.
Mobs are past Floor VII's, and stronger each floor. The bosses have Hypixel's Master Mode health: Bonzo 200,000,000, Scarf 375,000,000, The Professor 600,000,000, Thorn 6 Spirit Bow hits, Livid 600,000,000, Sadan 800,000,000 (his Giants 250,000,000), Maxor, Storm, Goldor and Necron 800,000,000 to 1,400,000,000. Their minions are much stronger too.
The Speed score allows 8 minutes, and every secret counts toward the Explore score.
Chests cost twice as much and drop Master Skulls, the Master Stars (First on M3 ... Fifth on M7) and, on M7, the Dark Claymore. Runs give three times the Catacombs XP.
Master Stars: Malik puts them on an item that already has all five stars, in order (First to Fifth). Each adds 5% stats in Master Mode. They show as ➊ to ➎ after the stars.

Pick one at Mort before the run (hover a class there for what it does). In a run, the drop key (Q) uses your class ability and sneak + drop key your ultimate; nothing is dropped. The class's bonuses grow with its level.
Healer | Allies within 8 blocks heal 1% of their health a second | Healing Circle: allies nearby heal 25% (10 s) | Wish: everyone to full health, +20% absorption (120 s)
Mage | +100 Intelligence (+3 a level), abilities 25% faster | Guided Sheep: a blast 10 blocks ahead (30 s) | Thunderstorm: lightning on mobs around you for 10 s (100 s)
Berserk | +20 Strength (+1 a level) | Throwing Axe: hits the first mob in 15 blocks (10 s) | Ragnarok: +100 Strength and Speed for 15 s (60 s)
Archer | +10 Crit Damage (+1 a level) | Explosive Shot: three blasts where you aim (40 s) | Rapid Fire: five shots a second at your target for 4 s (100 s)
Tank | +100 Health and +50 Defense (more each level) | Seismic Wave: mobs within 7 blocks, more with Defense (15 s) | Castle of Stone: 70% less damage for 20 s (150 s)
Skill | 100 | 20 + 80 for the share of rooms cleared, -2 for each death, -14 for each puzzle failed or left
Explore | 100 | 60 for the share of rooms cleared, 40 for secrets (Floor I counts 30% of them as all of them, Floor VII 100%)
Speed | 100 | full within the floor's time (10 minutes on Floor I), then a little less every few seconds
Bonus | up to 7 | +1 for each Crypt Undead killed (up to 5), +2 for the Mimic

At the end you get Catacombs XP and class XP (the class you played gets it all, the others a quarter), more for a better score. Then the reward chests: right-click the chest in the boss room and pick one.
Emerald | from 100,000 coins | rank A, Floor II+
Obsidian | from 250,000 coins | rank S, Floor III+
Bedrock | 2,000,000 coins | rank S+, Floor V+

Every chest holds Undead Essence (Wither Essence too from Floor III), and each floor has its own drops: Floor I Bonzo Fragments, the Red Nose, Balloon Snake, Bonzo's Mask and Staff; Floor II Scarf Fragments, Scarf's Studies and Thesis, the Adaptive Belt, Stone Blade and Red Scarf; Floor III the Adaptive armour, Suspicious Vial and Scarf's Grimoire; Floor IV Thorn Fragments, Spirit Wing, Bone and Decoy, the Spirit Bow and Sword, Thorn's Boots and Ultimate Rend; Floor V Livid Fragments, the Dark Orb, Shadow Assassin armour, Lethality VI, the Livid Dagger, AOTE Stone, Shadow Fury and Last Breath; Floor VI Giant Fragments, Sadan's Brooch, the Fel Skull, Soulweaver Gloves, Necromancer Sword and Lord Chestplate, Summoning Ring, Giant's Sword and Precursor Eye; Floor VII Wither armour, the Wither Cloak, Blood and Catalyst, Precursor Gear, Auto Recombobulator, Ultimate One For All, the three scrolls, Necron's Handle and the Lords' fish. Any floor can also give a Hot Potato or Fuming Potato Book, a Recombobulator 3000, a Kismet Feather or a Dungeon Chest Key. Better chests and a better rank make the rare ones likelier. Essence goes to /essence.
Dungeon items (most gear from the Catacombs, and others marked as dungeon items) get stronger inside the Catacombs: +1% stats for each Catacombs level, and +10% for each star.

Stars (✪, up to 5) are added by Malik in the Dungeon Hub: hold the item and talk to him. Each star costs essence (Wither Essence for most gear), as Hypixel's item says; some also cost coins or items. A starred item shows its stars after its name.
The other tab of Malik's screen spends essence on perks that work in the Catacombs (click one for its next level):
Health / Defense / Strength / Intelligence Essence | Undead | 5 | +2 Health / +1 Defense / +1 Strength / +2 Intelligence
Forbidden Health / Defense / Strength / Intelligence | Wither | 5 | +1% of that stat
Undead perks cost 1,000 Undead Essence and up (to 50,000); Wither perks 100 Wither Essence and up.
Catacombs XP levels you up to 50 on Hypixel's table (50 XP for level 1 ... 569,809,640 in all); each level gives 20 SkyBlock XP (40 from level 40). Classes level the same way.
Not yet: more puzzles (Water Board, Ice Fill, Creeper Beams, Teleport Maze, Quiz, Boulder...), traps, ghost abilities, the dungeon map, Croesus.

The public islands past the Hub: the Farming Islands, The Park, the Gold Mine, the Deep Caverns, the Spider's Den and The End (the Crimson Isle has its own page). How to get there, what they need, their mobs, resources, NPCs, Fairy Souls and the Ender Dragon.
Past the Hub lie Hypixel SkyBlock's other public islands, each one floating in its own sky. Everyone shares them, like the Hub: you can break the resources they're for, and nothing else.
The Barn | the Farm's launch pad | Farming I | /warp barn | Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, Pumpkins, Melons; Cows, Pigs, Chickens
Mushroom Desert | over the bridge from the Barn | Farming V | /warp desert | Cactus, Sugar Cane, Cocoa, Mushrooms, Sand; Rabbits, Sheep, Mooshrooms
The Park | the Forest's launch pad | Foraging I | /warp park | Birch, Spruce, Dark Oak, Acacia and Jungle wood; the Howling Cave
Gold Mine | the Coal Mine's gold gate | Mining I | /warp gold | Stone, Coal, Iron and Gold Ore
Deep Caverns | the lift shaft at the bottom of the Gold Mine | Mining V | /warp deep | Six layers of ores and their mobs
Spider's Den | the Graveyard's launch pad | Combat I | /warp spider | Spiders, Gravel; the Spider Mound and Arachne's Sanctuary
The End | the Spider's Den's west launch pad | Combat XII | /warp end | Endermen, Zealots, End Stone, Obsidian; the Ender Dragon
Crimson Isle | the Spider's Den's east launch pad | Combat XXII | /warp crimson and four more | Blazes, Magma Cubes, the factions and their minibosses; see its own page
Dwarven Mines | the Obsidian Sanctuary's launch pad (Deep Caverns) | Mining XII | /warp mines, /warp forge | Mithril, Titanium, Commissions, the Forge; see its own page

Launch pads are 3x3 pads of slime blocks with a sign saying where they go. Step on one and you're thrown to the island, if you have the skill level it needs; if not, it pushes you back and says what you're missing. Every island has a pad back to where you came from in the Hub.
Warps open the first time you set foot on an island (see Fast Travel in the SkyBlock Menu). After that /warp <name> takes you straight there. Falling off an island puts you back at its arrival point.

They have Hypixel's names and stats, pay Combat XP and coins on the kill and count for slayer quests: the Spider's Den's spiders for the Tarantula Broodfather, the Howling Cave's spirits for Sven Packmaster, zombies for the Revenant Horror. Neutral mobs (the Howling Cave's wolves, the Deep Caverns' pigmen) attack anyone who comes near.
Pack Spirit | The Park, Howling Cave | 30 | 6,000 | 300 | 22 | 11
Howling Spirit | The Park, Howling Cave | 35 | 7,000 | 450 | 22 | 11
Soul of the Alpha | The Park, Howling Cave (one at a time) | 55 | 31,150 | 1,425 | 50 | 50
Sneaky Creeper | Deep Caverns, Gunpowder Mines | 3 | 120 | 0 | 8 | 3
Lapis Zombie | Deep Caverns, Lapis Quarry | 7 | 200 | 50 | 12 | 5
Redstone Pigman | Deep Caverns, Pigmen's Den | 10 | 250 | 75 | 20 | 12
Miner Zombie | Deep Caverns, Diamond Reserve | 15 | 250 | 180 | 20 | 12
Miner Skeleton | Deep Caverns, Diamond Reserve | 15 | 250 | 150 | 20 | 12
Miner Zombie / Skeleton | Deep Caverns, Obsidian Sanctuary | 20 | 300 | 250 | 20 | 12
Gravel Skeleton | Spider's Den, the gravel pit | 2 | 100 | 35 | 6 | 1
Obsidian Defender | The End, Dragon's Nest | 55 | 10,000 | 200 | 40 | 15
Zealot Bruiser | The End, Zealot Bruiser Hideout | 100 | 65,000 | 2,500 | 300 | 40
Voidling Fanatic | The End, Void Sepulture | 85 | 1,500,000 | 3,500 | 110 | 20
Voidling Extremist | The End, Void Sepulture | 100 | 8,000,000 | 13,500 | 1,000 | 100
Some mobs also drop items straight into your inventory: Endermen and Zealots drop Ender Pearls (Zealots sometimes an Enchanted Ender Pearl), Obsidian Defenders drop Obsidian and Watchers drop Arrows.
The farm animals (Cows, Pigs, Chickens, Rabbits, Sheep, Mooshrooms) wander their pens and fields.

The first farming island, reached by the launch pad on the Hub's Farm (Farming I). A wide green island with a big red barn, a windmill and fields of Wheat, Carrots and Potatoes, a Pumpkin patch and a Melon patch. Crops grow back after you harvest them. Cows graze the pasture, Pigs the mud pen and Chickens the coop's yard. The Farmhand works the fields; the Windmill Operator at the windmill's door sells farming goods.
At the east edge, a gate opens onto the sky bridge to the Mushroom Desert (Farming V).

Over the bridge from the Barn. Sand and red sand dunes with Cactus fields, Sugar Cane along water channels, an oasis whose palms bear Cocoa Beans, and a mycelium field with a mushroom cave full of Red and Brown Mushrooms and Mooshrooms. Plain Sand on the dunes can be dug (it comes back). A desert settlement holds Jake's shop; Trevor the trapper has his den to the north, the Shepherd minds the sheep pen and Farmer Jon keeps the cactus fields.
The foraging island, through the launch pad in the Hub's Forest (Foraging I). A group of forest islands, each with its own wood, all of it choppable and regrowing:

Birch Park (where you arrive): a bright birch wood around a lake. Charlie and Vanessa.
Spruce Woods, to the west: tall spruces and a viking camp with Kelly, Gustave and the Melancholic Viking.
The Howling Cave, north of the Spruce Woods: a dark cavern where Pack Spirits, Howling Spirits and the Soul of the Alpha roam. Old Shaman Nyko keeps a fire at the entrance and sells his wares.
Dark Thicket, east over the bridge: dense dark oak, and the Campfire Cult's clearing with Ryan and the Campfire Adept.
Savanna Woodland: acacia trees and a camp with Melody, Master Tactician Funk (a shop) and Worker Xavier.
Jungle Island: towering jungle trees and an old temple, with Molbert and Juliette. East of their campfire, a launch pad goes to Galatea (Foraging XII).

Through the gold-trimmed gate deep in the Hub's Coal Mine (Mining I). A huge open-pit mine in terraces, ramps winding down to the bottom, with tunnels and caverns off them. Stone, Coal Ore, Iron Ore and Gold Ore turn to bedrock for a few seconds when mined, then come back. The miners' camp at the top has Rusty, the Lazy Miner, the Iron Forger and the Gold Forger (both shops).
At the bottom of the pit, a lift shaft goes down to the Deep Caverns (Mining V).
A mountain of rock with six caverns stacked inside it, each with its own ore and mobs, joined by spiral ramps:
Gunpowder Mines | Coal, Iron, Gold | Sneaky Creepers
Diamond Reserve | Diamond | Miner Zombies and Skeletons
Obsidian Sanctuary | Diamond, Obsidian, Diamond Blocks | stronger Miner Zombies and Skeletons

Walter sells supplies at the entrance at the top. On every layer a Lift Operator stands in the lift cage in the middle: talk to one to ride the lift to any layer you've already walked into. The Lapis Miner, the Redstone Miner and Rhys (at the shrine in the Obsidian Sanctuary) live down here too. A launch pad at the top takes you back to the Gold Mine, and one on the Obsidian Sanctuary's floor goes down to the Dwarven Mines (Mining XII).

Through the launch pad behind the Hub's Graveyard (Combat I). A dark island of cobwebs and dead trees around the Spider Mound, a huge hill that a path winds up. Spiders crawl everywhere; at the top of the mound they're level 42. Gravel can be dug on the slopes and in the gravel pit, where Gravel Skeletons lurk. Under the mound, a stair goes down to Arachne's Sanctuary, a webbed chamber with an altar (Arachne herself is coming). A launch pad on its east edge goes to the Crimson Isle (Combat XXII).
The camp by the arrival has Grandma Wolf, Haymitch, Rick, Shaggy (a shop) and the Archaeologist.
Through the launch pad on the Spider's Den's west edge (Combat XII). A cluster of End Stone islands floating in the dark:

The arrival (where /warp end puts you): the stalls of the Pearl Dealer (End Stone, Obsidian, Silent Pearls, the Remnant of the Eye) and Gregory (a shop), and a pad back to the Spider's Den.
The main island, to the south-east: Endermen roam it in three groups (level 42 near the arrival, 45 and 50 further out) with Endermites. Guber, the Lone Adventurer and Tyzzo live here. Under its east end a stair goes down to the Zealot Bruiser Hideout, a cavern of level 100 Zealot Bruisers.
The Dragon's Nest, north of the arrival: a huge bowl ringed by obsidian pillars, with Zealots, Obsidian Defenders and Watchers on its floor and the altar in the middle.
The Void Sepulture, over the bridge to the west: a dark island with Voidling Fanatics and Voidling Extremists, by far the toughest mobs here.
End Stone and Obsidian can be mined anywhere on the main islands; they come back after a few seconds.
Every Zealot you kill has a 1 in 420 chance (a Zealot Bruiser 1 in 210) to leave a Special Zealot behind: an Enderman carrying an End Portal Frame. Kill it for a Summoning Eye.
