The altar in the middle of the Dragon's Nest has 8 End Portal Frames. Right-click a frame with a Summoning Eye to place it; right-click your own eye to take it back. When the eighth eye goes in, the Dragon Egg spawns, and 8 seconds later one of seven dragons rises:
Its health shows on a boss bar to everyone near the nest. If everyone leaves it alone for two minutes, it flies away (and the eyes are gone).
Loot. When the dragon dies, everyone who hit it or placed an eye gets loot by their Dragon Weight:
Your weight buys one major drop at most: the game goes down this list and gives you the first one you have the weight for that also passes its chance:
Ender Dragon pet (Legendary) | 450 | 0.01% per eye you placed
Aspect of the Dragons (not Superior) | 447 | 3% per eye
Travel Scroll to the Dragon's Nest (Unstable only) | 250 | 35%
What's left of your weight turns into the dragon's Fragments (one per 22 weight, up to 32; the armour is crafted from them, 50 for a helmet), then Enchanted Ender Pearls and Ender Pearls.

Every island hides its own Fairy Souls, four on each part: 8 on the Farming Islands, 8 in The Park, 4 in the Gold Mine, 4 in the Deep Caverns, 4 in the Spider's Den and 4 in The End. Some sit in plain sight; others are on roofs, in tree tops, in caves or behind cobwebs. Nothing needs to be broken to reach them. Tia the Fairy in the Hub exchanges them all.

Hypixel's nether island over a lava sea - Elle, the Mage and Barbarian factions, reputation and daily faction quests, the five minibosses, its mobs, Trophy Fishing with Odger, Kuudra, the Dojo, Vulcan's Crimson stars and the Inferno Demonlord.

The Crimson Isle is a nether island floating in a sea of lava, Hypixel SkyBlock's late-game combat island. Two factions split it: the Mages of Scarleton in the east and the Barbarians of Dragontail in the west, with the Stronghold, the Crimson Fields and the Blazing Volcano between them.

A launch pad on the Spider's Den's east edge, next to its pads to the Hub and The End. It needs Combat XXII. You land at the Crimson Isle's south coast, where a pad goes back to the Spider's Den. Once you've been to them, the warps take you straight there:
/warp crimson | the arrival, at the Crimson Fields
/warp kuudra | the Forgotten Skull, Kuudra's lair
Lava rivers run between the island's three parts; four nether-brick bridges cross them. Fall into the lava sea and it throws you back out at the nearest warp.
Crimson Fields | the arrival; Magma Cubes, Pack Magma Cubes, Magma Cube Riders
Stronghold | Elle; Blazes, Mutated Blazes, Bezal, Wither Skeletons; Bladesoul
Blazing Volcano | Smoldering Blazes, Millennia-Aged Blazes, Flares, Ghasts
Magma Chamber | the cave under the volcano: Kada Knights; the Magma Boss
Dragontail | the Barbarian town: Chief Scorn, Igor, the Barbarian Emissary, a Banker, Auction House and Bazaar
Barbarian Outpost | a camp at the north-west bridge
The Dukedom | Kada Knights; Barbarian Duke X
Smoldering Tomb | Wither Spectres and Wither Skeletons in a crypt
Burning Desert | Flaming Spiders; Red Sand and Sulphur
Forgotten Skull | Vulcan and the Kuudra Gatekeeper (Kuudra)
Scarleton | the Mage town: Queen Nyx, Alwin, the Mage Emissary, a Banker, Auction House and Bazaar
Mage Outpost | a camp at the north-east bridge
Cathedral and Courtyard | the Mage Outlaw
Dojo | Master Tao and his tests
Odger's Hut | Odger and Trophy Fishing, by a pier over the lava
They have Hypixel's levels and health, pay Combat XP and coins on the kill, and the blazes and magma cubes count for the Inferno Demonlord.
Mutated Blaze | 70 | 1,500,000 | 4,000 | 90 | Blaze Rods, Blaze Ashes (35%)
Millennia-Aged Blaze | 110 | 12,000,000 | 10,000 | 1,000 | Blaze Rods, Enchanted Blaze Powder (20%)
Magma Cube | 75 | 400,000 | 2,500 | 50 | Magma Cream, Magma Chunks (25%)
Pack Magma Cube | 90 | 1,500,000 | 4,000 | 120 | Magma Cream, Magma Chunks (35%)
Magma Cube Rider | 90 | 1,200,000 | 4,000 | 110 | Magma Cream, Magma Chunks (35%)
Kada Knight | 90 | 2,000,000 | 6,000 | 150 | Magma Cream, Kada Lead (2%)

Fish the Isle's lava with a lava rod (Starter Lava Rod and up, Fishing X). A bite that isn't a sea creature can be a Trophy Fish: every fish whose conditions you meet gets a try, rarest first, at its chance (more with Trophy Fish Chance, from Odger's teeth and lava rods). Each comes in four tiers: Bronze 73.353%, Silver 24.451%, Gold 1.996%, Diamond 0.2% (the Charm enchantment raises the better ones). Hypixel's pity: catch the same fish 100 times without a Gold and the next is Gold; 600 without a Diamond and the next is Diamond.
Gusher | Common | 20% | the Blazing Volcano, for 10 minutes after it erupts (every 20 minutes)
Steaming-Hot Flounder | Common | 20% | the Blazing Volcano's geysers (the small lava pools on its slopes)
Sulphur Skitter | Common | 30% | within 4 blocks of Sulphur
Flyfish | Uncommon | 8% | the Blazing Volcano, with your bobber 8 blocks below you
Obfuscated-2 | Uncommon | 20% | carrying an Obfuscated-1 (it's used up)
Slugfish | Uncommon | 15% | your bobber out for 20 seconds
Mana Ray | Rare | 5% | with 1,200 Mana or more
Obfuscated-3 | Rare | 10% | carrying an Obfuscated-2 (it's used up)
Vanille | Rare | 8% | a Starter Lava Rod with no enchantments
Volcanic Stonefish | Rare | 4% | the Blazing Volcano
Moldfin | Epic | 2% | the Mystic Marsh or Scarleton
Skeleton Fish | Epic | 2% | the Burning Desert or Dragontail
Golden Fish | Legendary | 5% | after 8 minutes of fishing without a 2-minute break
Odger, at his hut by the lava on the south coast, shows every fish you've caught in each tier, fillets the trophy fish you carry into Magmafish (4 to 1,300 each, by fish and tier), and ranks you:
Novice | Bronze or better of 15 fish | Bronze Hunter armour, Odger's Bronze Tooth, the Bronze Trophy Fishing Sack
Adept | Silver or better of all 18 | the Silver set, tooth and sack
Expert | Gold or better of all 18 | the Gold set, tooth and sack
Master | Diamond of all 18 | the Diamond set, tooth and sack, and Diamond the Fish

The Isle's lava sea creatures (Fishing level): Fried Chicken (10), Magma Slug (27), Moogma (28), Lava Leech (30), Pyroclastic Worm (31), Lava Flame (33), Fire Eel (34), Taurus (35), Thunder (36), Fiery Scuttler (43), Lord Jawbus (45) and Ragnarok (46). See Fishing.
Elle waits just inside the Stronghold's south gate. Before any faction takes you in:

Elle wants 4 Magma Chunks (Magma Cubes), 3 Blaze Ashes (Blazes) and 2 Spectre Dust (Wither Spectres).
Then meet both leaders: Queen Nyx in Scarleton and Chief Scorn in Dragontail.
Talk to the one you choose and join.
You can switch sides any time at the other leader. Your reputation is kept with each faction, so switching doesn't lose it. On the Isle, the sidebar shows your reputation with your faction.
Talk to your faction's leader to see the day's five quests (new ones at midnight UTC) and your rank:
Two hunts: slay 10 to 30 of one of the Isle's mobs | 80-90 each
Defeat one of the minibosses | 120 (the Magma Boss 150)
Two errands for your faction's people | 100 each
Mages | Pablo: 32 Red Mushrooms · Avorius: a Cup of Blood · Mollim: 32 Mycelium
Barbarians | Pomtair: an Enchanted Bone Meal · Sirih: 16 Sulphur · Suus: 16 Magma Cream
Talk to the person with the items in your inventory to hand them over. Every miniboss you help kill also gives +20 reputation.
Each has a spot of its own and comes back two minutes after it dies. When one appears, everyone on the island is told. Anyone who did at least half a percent of its health in damage gets its reward.

They also give Combat XP (2,500 to 3,922) and count for your faction quests. The Magma Boss gives 20-35 Magma Cream, a 50% chance at Enchanted Magma Cream, Compact Ooze and a Rekindled Ember Fragment. Their moves:

Bladesoul and Barbarian Duke X sweep everything around them (5 blocks).
The Mage Outlaw and Ashfang burst into flame, burning everyone within 7 blocks.
The Magma Boss leaps and slams down (9 blocks).

Kuudra, a colossal magma cube, sleeps under the Forgotten Skull. Talk to the Kuudra Gatekeeper there to fight it with your party (up to 4). You must be in a faction, and each tier needs the one before it beaten.
Basic | 100,000 | every 35 s | 60 Crimson Essence | +10 | 20 SkyBlock XP

The fight is in Kuudra's Hollow, a crater of lava with a fortified platform and a ballista in the middle and six islets around it on bridges. Fall in the lava and it throws you back onto the platform.

Supplies. Six supply crates sit on the islets. Right-click one to pick it up (you're slow while carrying it) and bring it to the ballista.
Build. Stand by the ballista to build it: the more of you, the faster.
Kuudra. Kuudra rises in the east. Fuel cells wash up on the islets two at a time; carry them to the ballista. Each one is a shot: right-click the ballista's back to fire. A shot takes a tenth of Kuudra's health and stuns it beside the platform for 10 seconds, and only then can you hurt it.

All through, Kuudra's followers climb out of the lava in waves (Kuudra Followers, Knockers, Magma Followers, Wandering Blazes, and Berserkers from Hot up), and every few seconds Kuudra slams down where someone stands (a ring of fire warns first). From Burning, two tentacles grab the platform after each stun and the ballista won't fire until they're dead. From Fiery, Kuudra heals while it isn't stunned. In Infernal, below a quarter of its health, it slams twice as often. Going down isn't the end: you're back on the platform after 10 seconds, but if everyone is down at once, Kuudra wins.
After the kill, two chests (/kuudra chests reopens them):

Free chest: Crimson Essence.
Paid chest: opened with that tier's Kuudra Key. Twice the essence (plus 2,000 in Infernal), a piece of Crimson, Aurora, Terror, Hollow or Fervor armour of the tier, Kuudra Teeth in Fiery and Infernal, sometimes a Kuudra Chunk or a Kuudra Core.
You're sent back to the Forgotten Skull a minute later (/kuudra leave goes at once).
The Emissary in your faction's town sells them:

Master Tao at the Dojo (south-east, past the Mystic Marsh) tests you in his walled arena, one player at a time. Each test scores points and grades them: S (1,000+), A (800), B (600), C (400), D (200) or F. Tests last a minute (Mastery two). Leaving the arena ends a test early.
Force | knock the helmeted zombies into the walls | iron 10, gold 20, diamond 30; leather zombies -15
Stamina | walls of fire sweep across: stand in their gap | 17 a second; -50 when one catches you
Mastery | shoot the targets on the walls before they go dark (you get a bow) | green 8, yellow 16, red 32
Discipline | hit each zombie with the sword matching its helmet (you get four swords) | +25 right, -10 wrong
Swiftness | stand on the green tiles, never the red | +10 or -10 every half second
Control | keep your eyes on the circling skeleton | 1 every tick you look within 10 degrees
Tenacity | fire rains on marked rings, faster and faster | 17 a second; -100 a hit
Your best score in each test adds up to your belt, which Master Tao gives you with its Combat XP:
Your first S in each test also gives 5 SkyBlock XP. Belts are worn as equipment and take Crimson stars at Vulcan.

Vulcan, at the Forgotten Skull, adds Crimson stars to Kuudra armour (and the Dojo belts) for Crimson Essence: hold the piece and talk to him. Ten stars on Basic to Fiery pieces, fifteen on Infernal ones, at Hypixel's costs (30 to 90 essence a star on Basic armour, up to 265,000 on Infernal; coins, Heavy Pearls and Kuudra Teeth from the fourth star). Each star adds 2% of the piece's stats. Stars past five show as a circled number after the name.
The Blaze Slayer: its quest fills from the Isle's blazes and magma cubes. See Slayers.
Still to come here: Vulcan's Crimson Essence perks, attributes on Kuudra armour, Rollim's and Kaus's duels, the Vanquisher and the Plhlegblast.

Any kill on the Crimson Isle has a small chance (1 in 640, rising the longer you go without one) of calling up a Vanquisher beside you: a Wither with 5,000,000 health that hits for 3,000. Beat it for 3 Corrupted Nether Stars. Vulcan's Wither Piper perk makes them likelier.
Vulcan stars up your Kuudra gear and sells perks for Crimson Essence (Kuudra's chests and the Isle's minibosses drop it):
Fresh Tools | 5 | Build Kuudra's ballista faster
Headstart | 5 | Bonus tokens at the start of Kuudra (with its token shop)
Kuudra Master | 1 | Each ballista shot hurts Kuudra a little more
Fungus Fortuna | 10 | +2 Mining Fortune on Mycelium a level
Harena Fortuna | 10 | +2 Mining Fortune on Red Sand a level
Crimson Training | 3 | Combat Wisdom on the Crimson Isle
Wither Piper | 5 | Vanquishers 2% likelier a level

Rollim (Scarleton) trains Mages and Kaus (Dragontail) Barbarians: one duel a day for seven days, each one tougher (50,000 health on day one, 25,000,000 on day seven). Each win is 25 reputation; the seventh, a Bag of Gold. Watch out: once in each duel they eat a golden apple.
Minions gather for you on your island, even while you're offline. All 61 of Hypixel's minions, with their real speeds, storage and upgrade costs.

A minion is a little helper you place on your island. It works the ground around it and fills its storage with what it gathers, even while you're offline. There are 61 kinds, from the Cobblestone Minion to the Inferno Minion, each with up to 12 tiers. Every number comes from Hypixel: time between actions, storage, what each one collects, and what each upgrade costs.
Hold a minion and right-click the top of a block on your own island. It stands on that block and works the 5 by 5 around it. A minion never puts a block where someone is standing.
Each minion works in its own way:
Mining (Cobblestone, Coal, Iron, Diamond...) | Places its block on the empty spots around it, at the height of the block it stands on, then mines them.
Farming (Wheat, Carrot, Melon...) | Plants on the ground around it, then harvests.
Foraging (Oak, Birch...) | Grows logs on the outer ring around it, then chops them.
Combat and animals (Zombie, Cow, Chicken...) | Spawns its mob next to it, then kills it.

Give a mining minion room: leave the 5 by 5 around it empty (air) at the level of the block it stands on. It fills every empty spot first, then mines one each time and refills the gap, so it harvests on every other action.

A minion keeps time with the real clock. When you come back, it has done everything it would have done while you were gone, up to what its storage holds. When its storage is full it stops, and /!\ My storage is full! :( floats above it.
Right-click your minion to open it:

The minion turning on its stand, with a bar that fills up to its next action and a countdown.
Its speed (time between actions) and how much it has generated in total.
Its storage. Higher tiers hold more, and the locked slots show how much room the next tiers add. Click an item to take it, or use Collect All.
Upgrade: what the next tier costs (the items from its Hypixel recipe), in green when you have enough. A higher tier works faster and holds more. Tier XII is a trade on Hypixel (Bulvar in the Dwarven Mines for mining minions, Tony for farming ones...): coins and materials, for example 2,000,000 coins and 1,024 Enchanted Cobblestone. Until those NPCs are in, the Upgrade button does the trade. Snow and Ice XII need North Stars and farming XII need Pelts, which aren't in the game yet.
Pick Up: puts the minion back in your inventory, with everything it had collected.
Fuel, shipping and upgrades: four slots under the storage, explained below. Shift-click an item from your inventory and it goes into the slot it belongs in.
Only the profile's members can open a minion.

Fuel makes a minion work faster while it burns. Put a stack in and it burns one item after another, in real time, even while you're offline. The screen shows what's burning and how long it has left. Burning fuel can't be taken back out, except fuel that lasts forever. You can only add more of the same fuel.

A Budget Hopper or Enchanted Hopper in the shipping slot sells whatever no longer fits into storage, for 50% or 70% of its NPC price, so the minion never stops. It holds the coins until you press Collect All (or pick the minion up), and they go into your purse.
A minion has two upgrade slots. Speed upgrades add up with each other and with the fuel.
Auto Smelter | Smelts what it makes: Cobblestone into Stone, ores into ingots, logs into Charcoal, Sand into Glass...
Compactor | Turns what it makes into block form: 9 Coal into a Block of Coal, Snowballs into Snow Blocks.

Super Compactor 3000 | Turns what it makes into its enchanted form once there's enough in storage: 160 Cobblestone into an Enchanted Cobblestone, then on into enchanted blocks. A minion needs room for 160 items for this to work.
Dwarven Super Compactor | Smelts first, then does what the Super Compactor does.
Diamond Spreading | 1 Diamond for every 10 items the minion makes, on average.
Potato Spreading | 1 Potato for every 20 items.
Krampus Helmet | A tiny chance at a Red Gift for every item.
Minion Expander | Reaches 1 block further (a 7 by 7) and works 5% faster.
Berberis Fuel Injector | Works 15% faster (farming minions only).
Solar Panel | Works 25% faster during the SkyBlock day.
Enchanted Egg | Chicken Minions only: an extra Egg from every chicken.
Flint Shovel | Gravel Minions only: always Flint, never Gravel.
Enchanted Shears | Sheep Minions only: shears every sheep for extra Wool.
Lesser Soulflow Engine / Soulflow Engine | Halves what the minion makes, but adds a Raw Soulflow every 3 minutes / 90 seconds.

Two of the same upgrade only count twice for the speed ones (Minion Expander, Flycatcher). An upgrade that doesn't fit the minion does nothing. Picking a minion up gives back its fuel (minus the one burning), its hopper and its upgrades.

Minions are crafted. Each one unlocks at tier I of its collection (the Cobblestone Minion at Cobblestone I), and its recipe is in the Recipe Book: a Cobblestone Minion I is 80 Cobblestone around a Wooden Pickaxe. Higher tiers come from the minion's Upgrade button. Admins can hand them out with /sbitem cobblestone_generator_1 (<type>_generator_<tier>).
You can place 5 minions to start with. Every unique minion you make (each type and tier counts once, crafted or upgraded) brings you closer to another place, as on Hypixel:
A new one is announced in chat (NEW UNIQUE MINION!). Unique minions are kept per profile. When you can't place another, the message says how many more unique minions you need.
Gather items to climb Hypixel's collection tiers. Each tier unlocks recipes (minions, enchanted items, gear) and gives SkyBlock XP.

Collections count how much of each item you have gathered. There are 83 of them, the same as on Hypixel SkyBlock: 25 Mining, 20 Farming, 15 Foraging, 12 Fishing and 11 Combat. Each has its own tiers (from 5 up to 12) with Hypixel's amounts, and each tier unlocks what it does on Hypixel.
Open the SkyBlock Menu and choose Collections to see your tiers.
A collection counts items you gather:

Items you pick up from the ground, mine, harvest, chop or fish.
What you collect from your minions (Collect All, taking items out of their storage, or picking the minion up).
Items you buy, craft or get from another player don't count. A collection counts its own item only: an Enchanted Cobblestone is not 160 Cobblestone for your collection.
The Mushroom collection counts both Red and Brown Mushrooms.
Every tier lists its rewards, as on Hypixel:

Recipes. Most tiers unlock something in the Recipe Book: the collection's minion, its enchanted forms, minion upgrades, gear. Until you reach the tier, the recipe is locked.
SkyBlock XP: 4 per tier.
Some tiers list skill experience ("+1,000 Mining Experience").
When you reach a tier you get a notice, a sound and the list of rewards in chat.
Collections are kept per profile. The Rift's collections come with the Rift.
Hypixel's Garden - your own 480 by 480 farm with 24 plots to unlock, Garden levels, crop milestones, visitors and their Copper, the Composter, SkyMart, pests and Jacob's Farming Contests.
The Garden is your profile's own farm, a separate island shared by your co-op. It opens at SkyBlock Level 5: /warp garden (or the Fast Travel menu) takes you there.

The Garden is a 5 by 5 grid of 96 by 96 plots. The middle one holds the Barn: the Desk inside it, the Composter beside it, the SkyMart stall, Pesthunter Phillip's shed, the visitor yard, and Jacob and Anita south of the Barn. The other 24 plots start fenced off. You can't leave the Garden's square; walking off the edge puts you back by the Barn.
You build and farm only on plots you've unlocked (anyone else visiting can look, not touch). The sidebar shows which plot you're on.
Unlock plots at the Desk, in Hypixel's order (the first four around the Barn, then the corners of that ring, then the outer ring). Each costs Compost, later Compost Bundles, and needs a Garden level:

Every plot gives +3 Farming Fortune in the Garden and 5 SkyBlock XP. A fresh plot is overgrown with grass, flowers, rocks and the odd tree: clear it to farm it. Compost and other costs come out of your inventory or your sacks.

Garden XP raises the Garden level, I to XV (Hypixel's table: 70 XP for level II up to 10,000 a level from XI on, 60,120 in all). Each level gives 10 SkyBlock XP and lets visitors ask for more crops. Garden XP comes from crop milestones and visitors.

Harvesting the ten Garden crops on your plots counts toward their milestones: Wheat, Carrot, Potato, Pumpkin, Melon, Sugar Cane, Cactus, Cocoa Beans, Mushrooms and Nether Wart. Each broken crop counts as Hypixel's base drop (Carrots and Potatoes 3, Melons 5, Cocoa 3, Nether Wart 2.5, the rest 1) times your Farming Fortune. Milestones go up to level 46, on Hypixel's thresholds (Wheat 30 for the first level, Carrots 100, Melons 150...). Each milestone level gives 10 Garden XP times the level and 1 SkyBlock XP. The Desk's Milestones tab shows them all.

The Desk's Crops tab shows every crop's milestone bar and its crop upgrade: nine tiers for 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1,000, 2,000 and 4,000 Copper, each giving +5 of that crop's Fortune (Wheat Fortune, Carrot Fortune...) and 1 SkyBlock XP. Crop Fortune adds to your Farming Fortune whenever you break that crop, anywhere, not only in the Garden (so do the Turbo enchantments).

A visitor arrives every 15 minutes while you're online, up to five waiting in the yard by the Barn. Right-click one to see their offer: one or two of your Garden crops (raw, or enchanted for bigger orders), the more the higher your Garden level. Accept to hand them over for Copper, Garden XP and Farming XP; decline and they leave. Rarer visitors pay more:
Mythic | 2%, from Garden XIV | five times as much
Copper runs from 2 to 100 an offer. Every visitor you serve for the first time gives 1 SkyBlock XP.
Right-click the Composter by the Barn. It turns 4,000 Organic Matter and 2,000 Fuel into one Compost every 10 minutes, also while you're away.

Organic Matter: your crops (Wheat 1 each, Pumpkins and Mushrooms 1, Sugar Cane and Cactus 0.5, Potatoes, Cocoa and Nether Wart 0.33, Carrots 0.29, Melon Slices 0.2; enchanted crops 160 times that). Add crops puts in every crop you carry.
Fuel: Biofuel (3,000), Oil Barrels and Volta (10,000). Add fuel puts in every fuel you carry.
Collect takes the Compost.

Five upgrades, 25 tiers each, for Copper (100 at tier 1 up to 4,000 at tier 25) and enchanted crops: Speed (+20% a tier), Multi Drop (+3% chance of an extra Compost), Fuel Cap (100,000 + 30,000 a tier), Organic Matter Cap (40,000 + 30,000 a tier) and Cost Reduction (-1% Organic Matter and Fuel a tier).

The SkyMart NPC (and the Desk's SkyMart tab) sells Hypixel's Garden gear for Copper (and a few things for coins): the Garden Scythe, gardening hoes and axes, the Lotus accessories, Copper Talisman and Ring, the Mk. I crop tools for each crop, vacuums, the Sprayonator and Pest Repellent, Biofuel and more.
From Garden V, farming can stir up pests. Each crop you break has a 0.2% chance to bring that crop's pest, at most one every 5 minutes per Garden:
Fly, Cricket, Locust, Rat, Mosquito | Wheat, Carrot, Potato, Pumpkin, Sugar Cane | V

Pests float over your plots, glowing, with 600 health. Swords and bows don't touch them: only a vacuum does (SkyMart sells them). Hold right-click and aim at a pest within 10 blocks; the vacuum's Damage hurts it every second. A pest you vacuum up gives 1,000 coins, 1,500 Farming XP and an enchanted crop of its kind (one more for every 50 Farming Fortune).

Leave them be and they cost you: with 4 or more pests alive in your Garden, your Farming Fortune there drops by 5%, then 15%, 30%, 50% and at worst 75% (every 100 Bonus Pest Chance lets you carry one more before that, though it also brings pests more often). Pest Repellent halves the chance of pests for an hour; Pest Repellent MAX quarters it.

From Garden Level 5, the Sprayonator (SkyMart, 25 Copper) sprays the plot you're standing on: right-click to spray, sneak + right-click to pick the material. For 30 minutes the plot draws pests: +25 Bonus Pest Chance, half again as many pests, and the material's own pests far more often.
Pests sometimes drop the materials. The Juicy Sprayonator lasts 45 minutes and doubles the pests.

Ten Garden Chips make you better at the Garden. Right-click a chip to redeem it (sneak to redeem the stack): the first unlocks it, five make it Epic and 21 Legendary, and each rarity makes its levels worth more. Level chips up with Sowdust, which you earn harvesting Garden crops; open them with /chips.
Vermin Vaporizer | +3 Bonus Pest Chance | pests
Overdrive | +5 Farming Fortune in Jacob's Contests | Anita, 2 Gold Medals
Hypercharge, Mechamind, Evergreen, Rarefinder | (coming with what they boost) | visitors, Anita, the Greenhouse, crops
Phillip stands by his shed next to the Barn. Every pest you vacuum up is one to spend with him:
Pesthunter's Necklace, Cloak, Belt, Gloves | 40 each

Every third SkyBlock day (once an hour) Jacob runs a 20-minute contest on three of the ten Garden crops (the calendar and Jacob's menu show the next one). You need Farming X. The first contest crop you harvest on your Garden is the one you compete in; the sidebar shows the time left, your crop, your score and the bracket you're in.

At the end, everyone with at least 100 crops gets a reward. With ten or more players in a crop, the brackets go by standing (Hypixel's: Diamond top 2%, Platinum 5%, Gold 10%, Silver 30%, Bronze 60%). With fewer, they go by score (counted in Wheat; Carrots and Potatoes count 3 times as much, Melon 5, Nether Wart 2.5):
Rewards wait for you at Jacob, south of the Barn: right-click him and Claim.

Anita, next to Jacob, sells farming gear for Jacob's Tickets and medals (Hypixel's prices): the InfiniDirt Wand, Prismapumps, the Hoes of Great, Greater and Greatest Tilling, the Basket of Seeds and Nether Wart Basket, and Anita's Talisman, Ring and Artifact (each upgrade takes the one before it). She also changes medals down: 1 Gold for 2 Silver, 1 Silver for 2 Bronze.
Not here yet: Garden Chips, the Greenhouse, Barn skins and plot presets.
Moonglade Marsh, Galatea's first island - Fig and Mangrove trees with Sweep and Tree Gifts, the Hunting skill, critters to lasso and net, shards, the Hunting Box and attributes.

Galatea is the foraging archipelago from Hypixel's 2025 Foraging update. Its first island is Moonglade Marsh: woods and fig groves in the north, and the great Murkwater Loch with its mangroves in the south. Galatea also brings a new skill, Hunting: catch the critters that roam the island for their shards, then syphon the shards into attributes that give you stats.

You need Foraging XII. The launch pad on The Park's Jungle Island, just east of Molbert and Juliette's campfire, takes you to Tangleburg, the island's town. A pad in Tangleburg takes you back. Once you've been, /warp galatea works too.
Tangleburg | the town: Hina, the Hunting Lodge, the Fusion House, the Bank, shops
Evergreen Plateau | high ground covered in fig groves; Chillblades
North and West Reaches | woods, figs and critters
Dragon's Lair | the Jade Dragon's ledge
Murkwater Loch | the lake, its mangroves, the long pier and Agatha's pavilion
Murkwater Shallows | a sunken ruin under the water; Nemo's dock
Murkwater Outpost | huts on stilts; Rosemary
South Reaches and South Wetlands | channels, mud and mangroves; Bogged, and Phanpyres at night
Squid Cave | a flooded cave full of Lumisquids
SwampCut Inc. | the logging camp; Amaury sells axes
Galatea's trees are chopped differently from the rest of SkyBlock. Hit a log with an axe and you take it, plus extra logs if your Sweep is high enough for the tree's toughness:
Fig | 10 | trunk, then branches | 15 | Tender Wood
Mangrove | 50 | branches, then trunk, then roots | 20 | Vinesap
Cut out of order and your Sweep only counts for half. Fig Fortune and Mangrove Fortune (on top of Foraging Fortune) give extra logs.

When the last log falls, everyone who cut at least a tenth of the tree gets a Tree Gift: Forest Essence, Foraging XP and a chance of Tender Wood or Vinesap. If you cut a fifth of the tree the gift is 1.5 times bigger, and if you cut a third it's doubled, so chopping together pays. The tree grows back a minute later.

Critters wander Galatea's woods and swim its water. Each one is named after the shard it carries, and the name's colour shows how rare it is. Every shard you catch goes into your Hunting Box and gives Hunting XP (75 for a Common shard, up to 1,000 for a Legendary one).
Auryon, outside the Hunting Lodge, gives you your first Abysmal Lasso.

Right-click a critter within 14 blocks. The lasso catches it and its stamina bar starts draining.
Keep looking at it. If you look away, or it gets more than 16 blocks from you, it slips free.
When REEL! shows on your screen, right-click again within two seconds.
If you reel too early or too late, the critter escapes. Rarer critters have more stamina, and better lassos (Vinerip, Entangler, Everstretch) and Pull wear them down faster.

Jaeger gives you your first Basic Fishing Net. Look at a critter in the water and right-click it. Better nets reach further (8, 12, 16 or 20 blocks) and catch more often. Quick critters (Lumisquids, Salamanders, Bullfrogs, Joydives, Sepialots and Water Snakes) slip through a Basic net: you need a Medium net or better.
Galatea's mobs carry shards too. Kill a Bogged, a Chillblade, a Phanpyre or a Lumisquid, and your Charm Chance is the percent chance that its shard lands in your box.
Hunting Fortune gives extra shards on every catch. Each 100 is one more shard for certain, and anything left over is a chance of one more.

Open the box with /huntingbox, with the barrel in the Hunting Lodge, or from David Hunterborough's menu. Every shard has an attribute, for example Grove's Nature Elemental (+2 Health a level). Syphon shards into an attribute to level it up. Each level costs more shards, following Hypixel's levelling. Rarer shards need a higher Hunting level before you can syphon them: Uncommon needs Hunting 5, Rare 10, Epic 15 and Legendary 20.
Attributes that give a plain stat (Health, Strength, Speed, Fortune, Wisdom...) work right away. The others are listed with their effect and will be wired in later parts.
Each Hunting level gives +1 Hunting Fortune and +0.04% Charm Chance.
Hina | Tangleburg square | welcomes you; tips on trees and hunting
David Hunterborough | Hunting Lodge | your Hunting Box, your Hunting level, the Hunting Toolkit
Auryon | by the Lodge | your first lasso; lasso tips
Jaeger | the pond | your first fishing net; net tips
Banker Bonsai | the Bank | the bank
Sawyer | lumber yard | the Foraging Fortune Booster
Amaury | SwampCut Inc. | axes and Canopy armour
Nemo | the Shallows' dock | snorkeling armour
Agatha | the pavilion | prizes for Agatha Coupons
Kysha, Dax, Kiara, Oden, Alan, Jade Dragon, Rosemary | around the island | talk to them (their features are coming)

Rosemary's Forest Essence shop and perks, Agatha's Starlyn contests, the Heart of the Forest, Kysha's shard fusion, Dax's Huntraps, the Pocket Black Hole, the Forest Temple and the second island, Torrhus.
Every Hypixel SkyBlock recipe (2,468 of them), what unlocks each, crafting straight from your inventory, and the crafting table.

SkyBlock has 2,468 crafting recipes, all from Hypixel SkyBlock, with the same grids and amounts: an Enchanted Cobblestone takes 160 Cobblestone, a Cobblestone Minion I takes 80 Cobblestone around a Wooden Pickaxe. Most recipes are unlocked by a collection tier. Some need a slayer level, and 965 (tools, basic blocks and the like) have no requirement at all.
Open the SkyBlock Menu and choose Recipe Book. Its tile shows how many recipes you have unlocked.

Every item that has a recipe is in the grid. Type to search by name or SkyBlock id.
Show: switches between All, Unlocked (what you can make once you have the materials) and Craftable (what you can make right now).
Locked items are dimmed. Hover one to see what unlocks it ("Requires Coal Collection II").
Items you can craft right now glow green at the bottom.
Click an item to see its recipe on the right:

The 3 by 3 grid with how many of each ingredient a cell takes. A green line under a cell means you have enough of that ingredient; red means you don't. Hover a cell for the ingredient's tooltip and how many you have.
What unlocks it, and your tier in that collection while it's still locked.
Items with more than one recipe show Recipe 1 of 2: click the arrows to switch.
Craft makes it from the materials in your inventory (Hypixel's Supercraft). Shift-click to craft as many as you can, up to 64 at once.
Right-clicking a crafting table opens SkyBlock's crafting screen (sneak to place blocks on it instead). You can also type /craft.

Put the ingredients in the 3 by 3 grid as on Hypixel. A smaller pattern can sit anywhere in the grid, and mirrored. As soon as the grid makes something, the result shows on the right with its rarity's glow:

Craft makes one. Craft all makes as many as the grid holds (shift-click does the same).
A locked recipe shows what unlocks it.
The Recipe Book link at the top opens the Recipe Book.
What you make goes into your inventory. Whatever is left in the grid comes back to you when you close the screen.
Crafted items don't count for collections. Crafting a minion for the first time counts as a new unique minion (see Minions).

Hypixel's Rift - a timed dimension behind the Wizard Tower's portal, with Rift Time, Motes, Enigma Souls, Timecharms, the Leech Supreme, the Wyld Woods, the Black Lagoon, West Village, the Dreadfarm, the Village Plaza and beyond.
The Rift is a strange dimension you can only visit for a while. It opens at SkyBlock Level 12.
Go to the Wizard Tower (/warp wizard, the island south of the Wilderness) and climb to the top floor. Walk into the portal next to the Wizard. You need a Dimensional Infusion:

You get one free every 4 hours, up to 3 stored.
The Wizard sells one for 32 Grand Experience Bottles.
It's used when you leave the Rift's own Wizard Tower, so a look around the tower costs nothing.

Inside, your health bar becomes Rift Time (ф). You start with 8:00, plus the Rift Time your gear gives (Wyld armour, the Enigma Cloak). It runs down a second at a time everywhere except inside the Rift's Wizard Tower.

At 10 seconds the Rift starts collapsing; at 0 you're sent back to the Hub's Wizard Tower.
To leave early, walk into the portal on the Rift tower's ground floor.
Nothing hurts you in the Rift. A monster's hit takes Rift Time instead.
Falling off the edge sends you back to the tower and costs 10 seconds.
Mote orbs (pink, floating near the ground) give 25 Motes and 2 seconds each.
Your weapon doesn't matter here: every hit deals your Rift Damage, 20 plus your gear's.
Motes are the Rift's money. The sidebar shows them instead of your purse. You get them from:

Rift monsters.
Mote orbs.
The Motes Grubber, who eats Rift items: Shy Crux, Deadgehog Spines, Lil' Pads, Muted Bark and more.
Violet Enigma Souls are hidden all over the Rift: on branches, in a grotto, behind a cage, at the end of a trail of flower pots. Right-click one to take it. A couple come from people:

Tel Kar gives one if you hear his whole story.
Roy sells one for 4,000 Motes and 8 Deadgehog Spines.

Enigma, outside the Rift's Wizard Tower, sells the Enigma Cloak for 100 Motes. With it, every soul you've found gives +20 Rift Time. Every 4 souls he sells a cloak upgrade: +2 Speed and +4% Mana Regen in the Rift.
The woods around the Wizard Tower are giant trees joined by rope walkways, with treehouses high up.
Argofay Traffickers (4 treehouses) | Wyld Boots 50, Wyld Leggings 1,000, Wyld Helmet 1,000, Wyld Chestplate 2,000 Motes
Argofay Threebrothers | Wyld Sword: 333 Motes + 3 Shy Crux
Argofay Bugshopper | Larva Hook: 6 Shy Crux
Shifted (the Shifted Tavern) | Speed, Jump and Strength Elixirs
West of the woods is a swamp of channels, giant mushrooms and the Lagoon Hut. Kay sells Lil' Pads for 10 Motes, and Roy sells his Enigma Soul.
The channels are rough: right-click the water with a Lil' Pad to put down a lily pad you can stand on for 10 seconds.
The Leeches Lair lies under the lagoon, reached by the tunnel past Dr. Edwin. Its boss, the Leech Supreme, has 800 health and four phases:

Slime Pound: a shockwave around it (-8 seconds; get off the ground).
Wicked Bombs: red circles that blow up after 2 seconds (-10 seconds).
Leech Swarm: small leeches.
Mortiferous Lazer: a beam; sneak to duck under it.
It drops 8 Leech Supreme Fragments and 3,000 Motes to everyone who fought it, and comes back 40 seconds later.

Once Elise has your Supreme Timecharm, the glowing pad beside her takes you to the Rift Gallery: eight glass cases, one per Timecharm, each showing the ones you've secured. Rift Time stands still there.

Timecharms open the rest of the Rift. Craft them or earn them, then bring them to Elise in the Rift's Wizard Tower to secure them: +100 SkyBlock XP each, and your first earns the Rift Necklace. In the Rift its stats grow with every Timecharm you've secured: from +60 Rift Time with one to +380 Rift Time, +6 Speed, +10 Intelligence, +25 Mana Regen, +1 Rift Damage and +1 Heart with all eight.

The first is the Supreme Timecharm: 4 Bottled Odonata, 32 Lil' Pads, 24 Deadgehog Spines and 4 Leech Supreme Fragments. To bottle an Odonata (the dragonflies over the woods' ponds), hold an Empty Odonata Bottle (the Bugshopper sells them) and look at one for 3 seconds.
West Village | the Supreme Timecharm, 3:00 left
The Mirrorverse | the Supreme Timecharm, 3:00 left
Village Plaza | the mrahcemiT esrevrorriM and the Chicken N Egg Timecharm, 8:00 left
Barrier Street | the Globulate Timecharm, 10:00 left
West Village, the Dreadfarm and the Village Plaza
West Village, the Dreadfarm and the Village Plaza

West Village: north of the lagoon, across a rope bridge. Crooked houses, walkable rooftops, the Cake House, the Infested House and the Mirrorverse's door. Shadows drop 150 Motes and Shadow Crux.
The Dreadfarm: a wilted mirror of the Hub's farm, with the Great Beanstalk to climb. Volts drop 155 Motes and Volt Crux.
The Village Plaza: the town square, Barry and his protesters, Barrier Street and the floating islets of Deja Vu Alley. Scribes drop 100 Motes and Scribe Crux.
Cryptosis sells an Enigma Soul for 15,000 Motes and 10 Scribe Crux.
Seymour sells the Exceedingly Comfy Sneakers.

Gunther stands at the banner arch in West Village. Race through his ten glowing checkpoints and back to the start line: under a minute earns a Dark Pebble, under 35 seconds his Gunthesizer Lichen, which turns Wyld Boots (and 8 Shadow Crux) into Gunther's Sneakers (+30 Rift Time, +4 Speed).
Ask the Chef to start it: for 60 seconds his stall flings hot dogs over the counter. Grab them and right-click Joey McPizza to hand them over. Fifty in the minute earns an Enigma Soul.
Shania gives you a Wand of Farming. Hold it to farm:
Agaricus Cap | Look at a brown mushroom until it turns red, then click it.
Caducous Stem | Click a rose bush's top, then its bottom.
Wilted Berberis | Break the dead bushes that sparkle purple; the sparkle moves to another bush.
Twenty of a crop make a bunch. Bring Shania two bunches of each for a Proto-Chicken. Her task ends when you wear Chicken Leggs.

The Berberis Blowgun (60 Wilted Berberis, Wilted Berberis II) shoots arrows that only hurt chickens and Puffs. Punch a Not Chicken into the air and shoot it while it floats down: it drops a Metaphoric Egg and 50 Motes. Eggs make Chicken Leggs (32) and the Chicken N Egg Timecharm (8, with the Proto-Chicken and a bunch of each crop). The Blowgun also pops the balloons and presses the buttons some Enigma Souls hide behind.

The door in West Village's courtyard leads into Dr. Emmett's Mirrorverse: eight rooms, each split by a glass mirror. Your side hides something; the reflection shows it. Rift Time stands still inside and nothing can hurt you.
1 | Flip your levers to match the mirror's.
2 | Your floor is blank; the mirror shows the lava and the iron path through it. A wrong step sends you back.
3 | The mobs are invisible on your side and visible in the mirror. Their drops (written backwards) craft the remmaH yniT, which opens the door. The crafting table is invisible too.
4 | Only the platforms in the mirror are safe; the others drop you into the lava.
5 | Click the mirror to step through it; walls and lava block one side or the other. A pocket on the mirror's side, past the last lava pit, hides the Big Brain Talisman.
6 | Dance: do what Dr. Emmett calls (Move, Sneak, Stand, Jump, Don't jump, Punch). Seven steps open the door; all twelve earn the Tiny Dancer.

7 | Climb an invisible staircase the mirror shows. Dr. Emmett lends you his Emmett Pointer, whose lazer marks the invisible steps. The levers at the bottom take you back to checkpoints; climbing without them earns the Miniaturized Tubulator.
8 | Dr. Emmett pays 60,000 Motes once. His reflection, ttemme .rD, sells the mrahcemiT esrevrorriM (10,000 Motes and 10 Shadow Crux), which opens the Village Plaza with Chicken N Egg.
A Dr. Emmett in every room takes you back to any room you've reached.
The Living Cave (and the frozen Living Stillness below) | north of the Plaza, past Deja Vu Alley's islets | the SkyBlock Citizen Timecharm, 5:00 left | Autonull, Frozille
The Colosseum | east of the Living Cave | the Living Timecharm, 15:00 left; Rift Time runs at half speed inside | Autoboots
The Photon Pathway | east of the Plaza, across a bridge of light | nothing | none
Stillgore Château | east of the Pathway | talk to Deer at the Pathway's end | Thrall, Fledgling, Splatter
The Mountaintop | south of the Plaza | the Vampiric Timecharm, 9:00 left; the Time Chamber runs double | Puffs

In Stillgore Château, monsters take Hearts (you have 10) instead of Rift Time. Run out and you're dragged to the Oubliette, the castle's prison. Vampires drop Vampiric Melons; Healing Melons heal 7 Hearts there (Juicy 9, Luscious 12). The Fairylosopher, atop his tower, sells an Enigma Soul.

Porhtal (at the Broken Cage in the Wyld Woods) has seven eyes scattered across the Rift: The Intruder, The Gill-Man, The Baba Yaga, The Bankster, Gooey, The Prince and The 7th Sin. Hit an eye until you've dealt 300 Rift Damage to calm it. Each calmed eye gives Rift Time for good (+10 for the first, up to +70 for the seventh) and becomes a stop on Porhtal's fast travel (5 seconds of Rift Time a trip).

Sad Jacquelle's cat Montezuma lost his soul in nine pieces all over the Rift: under a tree, on a rooftop, behind a cracked wall, under the snow... Right-click a piece to take it, then bring it to her. Every piece back gives +15 Rift Time; from six on, each also gives Mana Regen in the Rift.

Kat (West Village) lends you her Turbomax Vacuum Cleaner. Hold right-click at the flies, spiders and silverfish in her house to suck them up (the bag holds 8), then empty it into the Vermin Bin (the composter in the front room). What you've deposited unlocks her trades:
Disinfestor Gloves (+30 Rift Time) | 4 flies, 4 spiders, 4 silverfish | 12 Shadow Crux
Vermin Belt | 15 flies (and the gloves) | a Leech Belt
Rift Ferret pet | 20 flies, 10 spiders, 20 silverfish | 12 Riftwart Roots, 3,000 Motes
Key to the Infested House Soul | 40 silverfish | 500 Motes
Fake Neuroscience Degree | 30 flies, 40 spiders, 60 silverfish | 10 Volt Crux, 10 Shadow Crux, 5,000 Motes
With the key, press the button by the iron door to reach the locked room and its Enigma Soul.
Reed in the Black Lagoon's hut needs five parts, in order. Each one is permanent Rift Time:
Living Anchor | a Living Metal Anchor | +30s
Then he sells you the finished Rift Boat for 25,000 Motes.
Cowboy Nick and the Half-Eaten Cave
Cowboy Nick and the Half-Eaten Cave

Cowboy Nick (by the rabbit pen in the Village Plaza) lends you his Horsezooka: right-click to launch a horse that clears hay out of its way. The Half-Eaten Cave east of the Plaza is packed with hay that grows back after half a minute. Don't be standing there when it does: you get squashed (-60 seconds of Rift Time) and land back at the mouth.
Cowboy Nick and the Half-Eaten Cave

Clear 3,000 bales and Nick gives you a rabbit. It follows you; take it to the carrot patches at the back of the cave and it nibbles them into Half-Eaten Carrots (you can pick them by hand too). Eighty make a Nearly-Whole Carrot; bring Nick seven, one for each of his bunnies. An Enigma Soul hides behind the hay at the very end.

Damia on Barrier Street runs Shen's Auctions: a new one every SkyBlock year, with bids in Motes. Each lot goes to its top bidders: Dead Cat Food (60), Flex Helmet (15), Placeable Fairy Soul (15), Punchcard Artifact (25), Rift Prism (25) and Ancient Elevator (15). Your bid is paid when you make it; when the year ends, collect what you won (or your Motes, if you were outbid) from Damia.
SkyBlock Citizen | Talk Barry's seven protesters down outside the Barry Center. He gives you his Montgray Pen; bring it with 16 Scribe Crux and he signs you in.

Living | Mine the Living Cave's lapis with a Self-Recursive Pickaxe for Living Metal (twice as much in Living Stillness, and more the longer you keep mining). Craft it from 160 Living Metal and 20 Frosty Crux.
Globulate | Beat Bacte in the Colosseum for Bacte Fragments; craft it from 8 of them and 20 Shy Crux.
Vampiric | Craft it from Bloodbadges, which open at Vampire Slayer 3.
Celestial | Buy Shen's Ringalia, get past Obo into the Cerebral Citadel and light Shen Citrinitas' sequence on the Hive Mind (below).

Youngite ore (light blue glass) grows round the Mountaintop's Continuum and on the Time-Torn Isles. Hold a Time Gun (a Berberis Blowgun and 32 Youngite) on an ore for 2 seconds and it ages into Timite (blue); age it again for Obsolite (purple). Aged ore turns back after 30 seconds.
Youngite | Anti-Sentient Pickaxe (Chipper McPickaxe, 24,999 Motes), Eon or Chrono | 1 Youngite
Timite | Eon Pickaxe (Timite I) or Chrono Pickaxe (Timite III) | 1 Timite and +2s Rift Time

Madame Eleanor Q. Goldsworth X (the summit) sells Shen's Ringalia for 25,000 Motes, 64 Puff Crux, 20 Youngite, 20 Timite, 20 Obsolite and the Disinfestor Gloves. Obo only lets its wearers into the Cerebral Citadel.

Inside, Shen's Hive Mind fills the west wall: seven lamps over seven buttons. The oak button on the left picks the sequence (one per Shen), the one on the right resets it. Each button flips its own lamp and, in every sequence but the first, some others. Light all seven and that Shen will see you: Shen Citrinitas gives the Celestial Timecharm, Shen Magnum Opus the Golden Belt (+100 Rift Time, +10 Intelligence, +4 Speed).

Oruo the Almighty (by the Time Chamber's door, inside the mountain) lets you fight the Sun Gecko for 5,000 Motes (you need 2:00 of Rift Time left; it runs twice as fast in there). It has 250 health and you have 10 Hearts.

Instant Transmission: it appears right behind you. Move away.
Perfect Volley: it throws you into the air, unless your combo is 3 or more.
Extreme Speed: three clones charge round the room. Don't hit the wrong one.
Spirit Beam: it rises and fires where you stood: a second of Rift Time if you're still there.
Keep your combo going: every hit before the timer runs out keeps it, and every third hit raises it (more damage each level). Lose it and you lose 4 Hearts.

A win is 5 Sun Gecko Essence. After two, Oruo shows you seven modifiers (Revival, Combo Maniac, Time Sliced, Buffantics, Collective, Brand New Dance and Culmination); each one you turn on makes the fight harder and pays 5 more essence. Spend it in his shop: Combo Mania (a longer combo timer), Extremely Real Shurikens, Grandma's Knitting Needle, Super Leech Modifiers, an Enigma Soul, and the Blessing of Time (three tiers of Speed, Rift Time, Mana Regen, Strength, Health, Intelligence and Defense in the Rift).
Ubik Von Neumann (the Continuum) hides an Enigma Soul in each game:

Ubik's Boxes: pick one of three boxes; he opens an empty one. The prize is an IQ Point; switch, and explain why, for the soul.
Ubik's Averages: pick a number from 1 to 100 each SkyBlock year. The closest tenth to half the average of everyone's picks win Free Will and the soul.
Tit for Tat: 5 to 9 rounds of split or steal (both split: 3,000 Motes each; both steal: 1,000; a steal against a split: 5,000 for the stealer). Split first, then copy his last move every round, for Ubik's Cube and the soul.

Walk into the Colosseum's arena and Bacte, a giant slime with 1,000 health, oozes out. Each phase it raises tentacles (one, then two, three, four and six); it can't be hurt while any is up. Watch for spikes (stand clear of the green circles), its slice (jump) and, at the end, a floor that bounces. It drops 8 Bacte Fragments and 6,000 Motes.
Maddox, in Stillgore Château's great hall, starts the Riftstalker Bloodfiend for Motes:
IV | 7,000 | 2,400 | 1 | 120 | a tier III kill, Combat 15
V | 10,000 | 3,000 | 1.5 | 150 | a tier IV kill, Combat 25

Kill the Château's vampires to fill the quest, then the Bloodfiend rises beside you. It drains your Hearts every second. From tier II it also slashes with Twinclaws (don't stand in front of it) and goes into Mania (it can't be hurt for 8 seconds). Below a fifth of its health only a Steak Stake (Maddox sells them) finishes it. Rewards are Coven Seals, rare drops (Bubba Blister, Guardian Lucky Block, McGrubber's Burger, Unfanged Vampire Part) and Motes. Slayer levels (20, 75, 240, 840 and 2,400 XP) give Rift Time and SkyBlock XP.
Not here yet: the Living Metal snakes, the Wizardman Trials and the other area quests.
Hypixel's Museum - donate 973 items and armor sets in eight categories for SkyBlock XP; a better item counts the ones it replaces.

The Museum collects Hypixel's 973 donations: weapons, tools, accessories and armor sets, in eight categories (Combat, Farming, Mining, Fishing, Foraging, Dungeoneering, Hunting, Special). Open it with /museum.

The tabs show each category and how many you've donated. In a category, an item you have with you is outlined in gold and comes first: click it to donate it. Donated ones are green; ones you haven't found show ?.
An armor set is donated whole: bring every piece.
A donation goes to the Museum for good (it's taken from your inventory).
Each donation pays Hypixel's SkyBlock XP for it (1 to 20+; Special items pay nothing but count).
A better item also counts the ones it replaces: a Refined Mithril Pickaxe counts the Mithril, Bandaged and Fractured Mithril Pickaxes too, with their XP.
Hover a donation for its SkyBlock XP and its game stage (Starter to Master).
Not yet: borrowing donated items back, the Museum's milestones and rewards, the Curator and the Museum building, and the Special items' display.
Your SkyBlock Level: 100 SkyBlock XP a level, +5 Health every level, +1 Strength every 5, prefix colours and the features levels open.

Your SkyBlock Level is the number in brackets next to your name in chat and in the tab list. It goes up as you play: every 100 SkyBlock XP is a level, as on Hypixel. Open the SkyBlock Menu and choose SkyBlock Leveling (or type /sblevel) to see your level, the bar to the next one, what your levels give you, the features they open up, the prefix colours and where SkyBlock XP comes from.
A skill level | 5 (levels 1 to 10), 10 (11 to 25), 20 (26 to 50), 30 (51 to 60)
A new unique minion | 1 (tiers I to VI), 2, 3, 4, 6, 12, 24 (tier XII)
Fairy Souls, slayers, the bestiary and more come later. Every gain shows above your hotbar ("+4 SkyBlock XP (54/100)").

+5 Health every level.
+1 Strength every 5 levels.
A new prefix colour every 40 levels: grey, then white at 40, yellow at 80, green at 120, dark green at 160, aqua at 200, cyan at 240, blue at 280, pink at 320, purple at 360, gold at 400, red at 440 and dark red at 480.
A level up shows as one panel in chat with everything it gives.
6 | Auto-pickup of block and mob drops
50 | A daily coins trading limit of 1B
100 | A daily coins trading limit of 10B
The Wardrobe is the first of these that's locked here; the others come with their features.
Hypixel's merchants and what they sell, selling anything for its NPC price, and buying back what you sold.

Merchants sell what they sell on Hypixel SkyBlock, at Hypixel's prices: the Farm Merchant's 3 Wheat for 7 coins, the Mine Merchant's pickaxes, the Bartender's drinks. All 88 of Hypixel's shops are in the game's data; the Hub's merchants are open now, and the rest come with their islands.
Farm Merchant | Crops, seeds, Enchanted Bone Meal, the Rookie Hoe
Fishing Merchant | Rods, bait and fish
Mine Merchant | Ores, stone and pickaxes
Combat Merchant | What an adventurer needs
Wool Weaver | Wool, glass and clay in every colour
Librarian | Books (enchanted books come with enchanting)
Right-click a merchant to open their shop.
The shop shows its offers in a grid. Hover one to see what it costs: coins, and sometimes items too, each with how many you have. What you can't afford is dimmed.

Click to buy one.
Shift-click to buy a stack's worth.
Every merchant buys anything that has an NPC price. Hover an item in your inventory to see what it sells for, and click it to sell the whole stack.
Your last 9 sales sit in the Buyback row above your inventory. Click one to buy it back for what you got for it. Buyback is kept until you log out.
Buy and sell over 1,000 SkyBlock items instantly, or place buy orders and sell offers. Opens at SkyBlock Level 7.

The Bazaar is the market for SkyBlock's materials: over 1,000 products, from Wheat to Enchanted Diamond Blocks. It opens at SkyBlock Level 7 (see SkyBlock Leveling). Open it from the SkyBlock Menu's Bazaar tile, or type /bz (or /bazaar).

Products are sorted into Hypixel's five tabs: Farming, Mining, Combat, Woods & Fishes and Oddities. Each tab has a group per collection (Cobblestone, Wheat, Ender Pearl...), and the products in a group go from the raw item to its enchanted forms. Every row shows what buying one instantly costs and what selling one instantly pays. Type in the search box to find a product in any tab.
Click a product to trade it.
Buy instantly | Buy 1, a stack, or as many as your purse allows, at the cheapest sell offer.
Sell instantly | Sell all of it in your inventory to the best buy order.
Buy Order | Type an amount and a price each (or take the best order and add 0.1). The coins are paid now; the items arrive as people sell to you.
Sell Offer | Type an amount (all of yours if empty) and a price each (or one tenth under the cheapest offer). The items are handed in now; the coins arrive as people buy from you.

Orders never trade with each other: they fill when someone else buys or sells instantly, as on Hypixel. The order book under the trading panels shows the best offers and orders, with how much and how many orders sit at each price.
Selling costs 1.25% tax: on instant sales, and on the coins a sell offer earns.

So the Bazaar always trades, even with few players online, a market maker quotes every product at Hypixel's own prices from a snapshot: it always sells at the Hypixel buy price and buys at the Hypixel sell price. It's the line marked Market in the order book. Player orders that beat it trade first; nobody trades past it.

Manage Orders (top right) lists your orders: what they are, how much has filled, and what's ready to Claim. Claim one, or Claim all. Cancel an order to get back what hasn't traded yet: the coins of a buy order, or the items of a sell offer. You get a message when one of your orders fills completely. Orders belong to your profile.
Sell items to other players as Buy It Now or by bidding, browse what's for sale, and collect what you sold or won.
The Auction House is where players sell items to each other: weapons, armour, accessories, anything. Open it from the SkyBlock Menu's Auction House tile, or type /ah.

Auctions are sorted into Weapons, Armor, Accessories, Consumables, Blocks and Tools & Misc (or All). Search by name, sort by Ending soon, Lowest price or Highest price, and switch on BIN only to see only Buy It Now items. Each card shows the item, its price and how long is left; hover it for the full tooltip and the seller. Click it to buy or bid.

Buy It Now (BIN): click Buy and it's yours, straight into your inventory (or to collect, if your inventory is full).
Auction: type a bid (at least the shown amount: the starting bid, or 15% over the top bid) and click Bid. If someone outbids you, your coins come back: to your purse if you're online on that profile, or to collect in Manage. When the auction ends, the top bid wins.
You can't bid on or buy your own items.

Click Create, pick an item from your inventory, choose Buy It Now or Auction, type the price (or starting bid; 25k, 2.5m work), and pick how long it runs: 1, 6, 12, 24 or 48 hours. The listing fee is shown before you create it:
Listing | 1% of the price (2% from 10M, 2.5% from 100M)
Collecting what you sold | 1% of it, when it's over 1M
You can have up to 14 auctions at once. An auction with no bids can be cancelled from its page; the fee isn't paid back.

Manage lists your auctions and the auctions you bid on: what's still running, what sold (coins to collect), what ended unsold (item to collect) and what you won (item to collect). Collect one at a time or Collect all, which also collects coins from bids you lost while away. You get a message when your item sells or you win an auction.
Maddox's slayer quests, Hypixel's five bosses, their drops and odds, slayer levels and the gear they unlock.

Slayers are SkyBlock's boss quests. Maddox the Slayer stands in the Hub. Pay him for a quest, earn Combat XP from the right mobs, and the boss rises next to you. Beat it for slayer XP, Combat XP and its drops. Slayer levels give stats and SkyBlock XP, and unlock the crafting recipes for slayer gear. Everything here (bosses, costs, health, drops, odds and levels) comes from Hypixel SkyBlock.
Talking to Maddox opens the quest screen. The Slayers page in the menu shows each boss, your level, every tier and what each level unlocks.

Pick a boss and a tier at Maddox and pay the cost.
Kill that boss's mobs. Each kill adds its Combat XP to the quest bar: a zombie gives 6, a wolf 10, an enderman 12.
When the bar is full, the boss rises next to you, with a boss bar and a clock.
Kill it before the clock runs out: 3 minutes for tiers I and II, 4 minutes above.
If the clock runs out or you die, the quest fails and the coins are gone.

Bosses only rise where there are mobs to fight: in a Hub area with mobs, or out in the world, but never on your island. The boss follows you around that area. If you leave it, log off or change dimension, the boss goes away and comes back with the time that was left.
Revenant Horror | zombies, husks, drowned, zombie villagers (6), zombified piglins (8)
Tarantula Broodfather | spiders and cave spiders (5)
Inferno Demonlord | blazes (60), magma cubes (50): the Crimson Isle's
Each tier needs the tier below it beaten, and some need a Combat level. The next boss opens once you have beaten a tier of the previous one:

Tarantula Broodfather opens when you've slain a Revenant Horror II.
Sven Packmaster opens when you've slain a Tarantula Broodfather II.
Voidgloom Seraph opens when you've slain a Sven Packmaster IV.
Inferno Demonlord opens when you've slain a Voidgloom Seraph III.
The Slayers page shows what a locked tier still needs.
A slain boss sends one SLAYER QUEST COMPLETE message that lists everything it dropped, the Combat XP and the slayer XP with your progress to the next level.
Every drop the tier has rolls its own chance:

Guaranteed drops always come.
Drops under 5% get more likely with your Magic Find.
A drop that needs a slayer level only rolls once you have it. The level counts this kill's slayer XP, so a first Tier I kill (5 XP, level 1) already gets the Revenant Flesh that needs level 1.

Rare drops are announced with Hypixel's banners: RARE DROP!, VERY RARE DROP! (Extraordinary) and CRAZY RARE DROP! (Pray RNGesus and RNGesus Incarnate). An RNGesus Incarnate drop is announced to everyone online.

Each boss has its own slayer level, 1 to 9. A level gives a stat for good and SkyBlock XP (see SkyBlock Leveling), and unlocks recipes. A recipe that needs one shows Requires Zombie Slayer 3 (Spider, Wolf or Enderman for the others) in the Recipe Book. It crafts once you reach that level.
Difficulty | Beginner | Strong | Challenging | Deadly | Excruciating
II | 7,500 | 1,440 | 20,000 | 25 | 70 | Combat 5, Revenant Horror I slain
III | 20,000 | 2,400 | 400,000 | 120 | 310 | Combat 10, Revenant Horror II slain
IV | 50,000 | 4,800 | 1,500,000 | 400 | 610 | Combat 15, Revenant Horror III slain
V | 100,000 | 6,000 | 10,000,000 | 2,400 | 1,580 | Combat 25, Revenant Horror IV slain

Each level gives Health: +2 at levels 1 to 3, +3 at 4 and 5, +4 at 6 and 7, +5 at 8 and +6 at 9. Level 1 unlocks the Wand of Healing, 2 the Zombie Ring and Revenant Viscera, 3 the Revenant Falchion, Wand of Mending and Crystallized Heart, 4 the Revenant Leggings and Boots, 5 the Revenant Chestplate, Devour Ring and Revenant Minion, 6 the Reaper Falchion and Wand of Restoration, 7 the Reaper Scythe, Reaper Mask and Zombie Artifact, and 8 the Axe of the Shredded, Reaper Orb and Warden Helmet.
V | 100,000 | 6,000 | 10,000,000 | 3,500 | 2,012 | Combat 25, Tarantula Broodfather IV slain

Each level gives Crit Damage: +1% at levels 1 to 4, +2% at 5 to 7 and +3% at 8 and 9. The recipes go from the Spider Ring (level 1) and Recluse Fang (2) through the Tarantula armour and Tarantula Fang (4), the Spider Shortbow (5) and Scorpion Foil (6) to the Mosquito Shortbow and Primordial armour (7) and The Primordial (8).

Sven's levels alternate Speed (+1 at levels 1, 3 and 8), Health (+2 at 2 and 4, +3 at 6, +5 at 9) and Crit Damage (+1% at 5, +2% at 7). The recipes include the Red Claw Talisman (1), Shaman Sword (3), Mastiff armour (4), Red Claw Ring and Weird Tuba (5), the Pooch Sword and Armor of the Pack (6), and the Overflux Power Orb (7).
Exceedingly Rare Ender Artifact Upgrade | 6 | RNGesus Incarnate |  |  |  | 1 (0.03%)

Voidgloom's levels alternate Health (+1, +2, +3, +4, +5 at levels 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9) and Intelligence (+2 at 2 and 4, +5 at 6, +4 at 8). The recipes include the Voidwalker Katana (1), Null Ovoid and the Soulflow items (2), the Voidedge Katana and Final Destination armour (3), the Vorpal Katana and Juju Shortbow (5), the Aspect of the Void, Atomsplit Katana and Sinseeker Scythe (6), and the Terminator (7).
The Blaze Slayer. Its quest fills from the Crimson Isle's blazes and magma cubes.
Blaze Rod, Glowstone, Magma Cream and Nether Wart Distillate (each) | 3 | Rare |  | 2 (5.08%) | 6-10 (4.86%) | 16-24 (4.57%)
High Class Archfiend Dice | 7 | Pray RNGesus |  |  |  | 1 (0.25%)

Blaze's levels alternate Health (+3, +4, +5, +6, +7 at levels 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9), Strength (+1 at 2, +2 at 6) and True Defense (+1 at 4, +2 at 8). The recipes include the Firedust and Twilight Daggers (2), the Burststopper Talisman and the Inferno Minion (3), the Kindlebane and Mawdredge Daggers and the Demonslayer Gauntlet (4), the Destruction Cloak (5), the Pyrochaos and Deathripper Daggers (6), and the Burststopper Artifact and Annihilation Cloak (7).
The daggers and the Hellion Shield
The daggers and the Hellion Shield

From tier II the Demonlord wears a Hellion Shield attuned Ashen, Spirit, Auric or Crystal (the boss bar names it, and a ring of its colour circles the boss). Only a melee hit from a dagger attuned the same way does full damage; anything else does 1%. Right-click a dagger to swap its attunement (the tooltip shows it): the Firedust, Kindlebane and Pyrochaos Daggers swap between Ashen and Auric, the Twilight, Mawdredge and Deathripper Daggers between Spirit and Crystal. Carry one of each. Every 8 hits that get through, the shield picks a new attunement.
Each boss hits for its tier's damage per second, about once a second, and every tier keeps the abilities of the tiers below. The Slayers page and Maddox's screen list each tier's abilities.

Regeneration: a boss that hasn't hurt anyone for 5 seconds heals 2% of its health a second, until it hits someone again.
Slam-dunk: stand in one block for 6 seconds without the boss reaching you, and the Revenant, Tarantula or Sven pulls you in for True Damage (twice its damage per second). Keep moving.

Undead: arrows heal it instead of hurting it. It gets a burst of speed when it hits you.
Life Drain (I): every 5 seconds, within 12 blocks, it drains one and a half times its damage per second from you and heals 1%.
Pestilence (II): everyone within 5 blocks takes a quarter of its damage per second every second, and loses 25% of their Defense for 3 seconds.
Enrage (III): after 40 seconds it gets MAD, and 5 seconds later ENRAGED for 12: 30% faster and three times as hard-hitting. Then it starts over.
The Atoned Horror (V): a different boss in netherite. Redemption: it heals a thousandth of its health a second, and 5% whenever its TNT hits you. Explosive Assault: every second a circle marks the ground under you, and a moment later TNT lands there, taking 15% to 60% of your health as True Damage (more near the middle); twice as often below a third of its health. Thermonuclear: every 30 seconds it stops for 5 ("Boom!") while a bedrock ring grows around it, then blasts everything within 7 blocks dead.
A cave spider rides it. Hits on the rider go to the Broodfather.

Backstab (I): every 7 seconds it leaps behind you. Its hits from behind deal +50% damage (+75%, +100%, +125%, +150% at II to V).
Noxious Paralysis (II): while it lives, everyone fighting it heals 25% less (50%, 75%, 99% at III to V), and every fifth hit lowers your Speed a little more (0.5% of the 400 cap a stack, 1% at III and IV, 2% at V).
Web of Lies (III): at 66% and 33% health it leaps away, webs the ground around it and lays egg sacs above itself: 2 sacs of 3 hits at III, 3 of 6 at IV, 4 of 9 at V. Smash them within 12 seconds or each hatches two cave spiders.
Bat Barrage (IV): from 66% health, magic can't hurt it and it releases 5 bats every 20 seconds. Each bat alive takes 1% of your health a second as True Damage (2% at V).
Till Death Do Us Part (V): the Primordial Broodfather doesn't stay dead. It fuses into the Conjoined Brood, at full health with twice the toughness and twice the damage, keeping only Backstab and Noxious Paralysis. Kill that to finish the quest.

Agile (I): a small, fast wolf.
True Damage (II): its bites also deal 10 True Damage (50 at III, 200 at IV).
Call the pups! (III): at half health it slows to a crawl and calls a pup every second for 5 seconds. Each pup has a tenth of its health and a quarter of its damage. While any pup lives it is Protected and takes no damage, and it doesn't regenerate.

Malevolent Hitshield (I): when it spawns, and at two thirds and a third of its health, it raises a shield of 15 hits (30 at II, 60 at III, 100 at IV). Every hit takes one off, whatever it deals; until it breaks, nothing gets through. From II the shield also makes it hit 3,000 harder every 3 seconds it stays up.
Dissonance (I): it teleports behind or beside you every 8 seconds, every 4 if you stand still. From II it also deals half its damage per second to everyone within 6.5 blocks, every second.
Yang Glyphs (II): from half its health (two thirds at III and IV), and never while its shield is up, it holds a beacon for 2 seconds and throws it nearby. Stand on or right next to it within 5 seconds to break it, or it kills everyone fighting (a thousand times their health as True Damage).
Nukekubi Fixations (III): from a third of its health, a floating head appears near you every 6 seconds (up to 5). Look straight at one for half a second to destroy it. Together they deal heads x 800 x 2^(heads - 1) damage a second (2,000 a head at IV), and if that outdoes the boss's own damage, the boss itself stops hitting.
Broken Heart Radiation (IV): at 5/6, 1/2 and 1/6 of its health it sits still for 8 seconds, can't be hurt, and sweeps four beams around it. A beam takes 25% of your health as True Damage and cuts your healing by 12% for 90 seconds.

Immolate (I): every second, everyone within 8 blocks takes 100 + a share of their max health as True Damage: 5% (8% below 66% of its health, 12% below 33%) at I; 5% / 10% / 15% at II and III; 15% / 25% / 35% at IV.
Demonsplit (I): at half health (at 66% and 33% from III) it vanishes and two demons rise, Quazii and Typhoeus (500,000 health and 2,500 damage a second each at I; 1,750,000 / 8,000 at II; 5,000,000 / 15,000 at III; 10,000,000 / 30,000 at IV). Immolate burns from them meanwhile. When both are dead, the Demonlord comes back.
Hellion Shield (II): see the daggers above.
Fire Pillars (II): below 66% health a pillar rises next to you every 20 seconds. Hit it 8 times within 7 seconds, or it blows up for more than your whole health.
Apocalypse (III): below 33% health, fire pits open around it every 7 seconds (one under you): smoke first, then fire. Standing in one burns 950 True Damage a second (2,865 at IV).
Not here yet: the runes, enchanted books and dyes these bosses drop (they arrive with enchanting).

Collections
Hypixel's gemstones - mined in the Crystal Hollows in five tiers, set into the gemstone slots of 499 items at the Gemstone Grinder for Health, Mining Speed, Strength and more.

Gemstones come from the Crystal Hollows: every gemstone block (stained glass) you mine drops a Rough gem of its kind. Many items (499 of them, Hypixel's) have gemstone slots; a gem set into one gives the item its stat.
Ruby | Health | Everywhere in the Crystal Hollows (red glass)
Jade | Mining Fortune | The Mithril Deposits (lime glass)
Amber | Mining Speed | The Goblin Holdout (orange glass)
Sapphire | Intelligence | The Precursor Remnants (light blue glass)
Topaz | Pristine | The Magma Fields (yellow glass)
Jasper | Strength | Small rare veins anywhere above the Magma Fields (magenta glass)
Opal | True Defense | not mined here yet
Onyx, Aquamarine, Citrine, Peridot | Crit Damage, Fishing Speed, Foraging Fortune, Farming Fortune | not mined here yet

Rough → Flawed → Fine → Flawless → Perfect. 80 of a tier craft one of the next (Recipe Book). A better gem gives more, and so does a rarer item: a Fine Ruby is +4 Health on a Common item and +14 on a Mythic one. Hypixel's whole table is used (from NEU).

An item's slots show under its stats as a row like  [❤] [⸕] [✦]: the symbol is the slot's gem (or kind: ⚔ Combat, ☤ Defensive, ✦ Mining, ❂ Universal), the brackets the gem's tier (gray empty, white Rough, green Flawed, blue Fine, purple Flawless, gold Perfect), dark when the slot is locked. A gem's bonus shows on the stat line in pink: Mining Speed: +300 (+40).

A slot for one gemstone takes only that gem; a Combat slot takes Ruby, Amethyst, Sapphire, Jasper or Onyx, Defensive Ruby, Amethyst or Opal, Mining Jade, Amber or Topaz, Universal any.
Some slots are open from the start; the others cost coins and gemstones to unlock (Hypixel's costs: 50,000 coins and 20 Fine Jade for a drill's first Jade slot, up to 250,000 coins and Flawless gems for Combat slots).
Gemma in the Crystal Nucleus runs the Gemstone Grinder. Put an item in:

Click a locked slot to unlock it (its coins and gems are taken).
Click an open, empty slot to set your best gem from your inventory that fits it.
Right-click a full slot to take its gem back out, for Hypixel's price: 1 coin for Rough, 100 Flawed, 10,000 Fine, 100,000 Flawless, 500,000 Perfect.
Not yet: Perfect gems' Gemstone Crystals, Gemstone Chambers, chisel slots and Fossils, and the Divine rarity's column.
The Blacksmith's reforges, reforge stones, and the anvil's Recombobulator 3000 and Hot Potato and Fuming Potato Books.

Every weapon, armour piece, tool and piece of equipment can be made better than it came: a reforge in front of its name gives it bonus stats, a Recombobulator 3000 raises its rarity, and Potato Books add flat stats. All of it stays on the item, as on Hypixel, and shows on its tooltip.
The Blacksmith works at Rosetta's forge in the Hub village. Talk to him to open Reforge Item: put the item in the top slot and press Reforge.
With nothing in the second slot he gives the item a random reforge that fits it (never the one it already has), for coins from your purse by the item's rarity:

There are 50 of his reforges, each for one kind of item: swords (Epic, Fair, Fast, Gentle, Heroic, Legendary, Odd, Sharp, Spicy...), bows (Awkward, Deadly, Fine, Grand, Hasty, Neat, Rapid, Rich, Unreal...), armour (Clean, Fierce, Heavy, Light, Mythic, Pure, Smart, Titanic, Wise...), equipment, pickaxes, axes, farming tools and fishing rods. Their stats grow with the item's rarity.

Hypixel's 86 reforge stones each carry one special reforge (Warped for the Aspect of the End, Ambered for pickaxes, Ancient, Necrotic, Spiritual, Renowned...). Most of them are on the Bazaar. Put the stone in the Blacksmith's second slot: the card shows the item with its new reforge and the price, and Reforge applies it and uses the stone. A stone only fits the items its reforge is for; the card says so when it doesn't.
Some stone reforges have a special bonus as well as stats ("Ambered Bonus: find Goblins from mining 40% more often"); the tooltip shows it.
The special bonuses are shown but don't work yet; the stats do.
Any anvil (in the Hub or on your island) opens Combine Items: the item in the top slot, the upgrade in the second, and Combine.

Recombobulator 3000 | One rarity up (Common to Uncommon... Mythic to Divine, Special to Very Special), once per item. A reforge's stats follow the new rarity. | Weapons, armour, equipment, accessories, tools and wands
Hot Potato Book | +2 Damage and +2 Strength on weapons and fishing rods, +4 Health and +2 Defense on armour. Up to 10 per item. | Weapons, fishing rods, armour
Fuming Potato Book | The same, past the tenth book: up to 15 in all. | Weapons, fishing rods, armour
All three are on the Bazaar.

A reforged item's name starts with its reforge ("Fierce Aspect of the End"). Each stat line shows the total, then what the Potato Books add in yellow and what the reforge adds in blue, as on Hypixel. A recombobulated item's rarity line has flickering marks at both ends. An item that can still be reforged says "This item can be reforged!" above its rarity line.
A tour of the Hub village: the plaza, the Bank, the merchants, the Grand Bazaar, the Arcane Library, Starwatch and the Hub's gate to your island.

Skyhaven is a floating town above the clouds: the village at the centre of the Hub, where you shop, bank, reforge and start slayer quests. You reach it through the portal on your Private Island. The village is a safe place. This page walks round it by area, with coordinates so you can find things on the map. The islands around it are on The Hub. North is the negative Z direction, and the Skyheart plaza is at 0, 0.

The Hub is its own dimension. Your Private Island and the public islands are separate from it.
Everyone walks 60% faster in the Hub, so getting from one merchant to the next is quick. The boost ends the moment you leave the Hub.
In the village nobody can fight, break blocks, place blocks or take damage, and nobody gets hungry. The seven areas around it let you break what they are for (Wheat, Oak, Coal and so on, which grow back) and fight the mobs that live there. See The Hub.
You can use doors, trapdoors, fence gates, buttons, levers and bells. Other blocks, such as chests, cannot be used.
Fields cannot be trampled.
If you fall off the island you land back at spawn.
Block items, buckets and spawn eggs cannot be used here.
/hub brings you here from anywhere, after a few seconds of standing still. /is takes you to your Private Island.

The bridges from the village lead on to the Graveyard, Coal Mine, Farm, Forest, Ruins, Mountain and Wilderness: see The Hub. Every NPC also shows up on your minimap and world map with their face, name and role. See NPCs.

The plaza is the middle of the town. A golden beacon fountain rises under the floating Skyheart, a spinning amethyst crystal ringed with purple shards. Eight runestones with banners stand round the edge, between four avenues, with cherry planters and benches facing the fountain. Hidden lights keep it bright at night.
The plaza is where you arrive when you use /hub, a little south of the fountain. Hypixel's other Hub spots (the Museum, the Fashion Shop and so on) are not built yet.
The avenue north of the plaza climbs to the raised Crown Terrace.

Skyhaven Bank, with a copper dome. The Banker keeps your bank balance and pays you interest. See Coins and the bank.
The Emberforge, where Rosetta sells armour sets and the Blacksmith reforges your weapons, armour and tools. See Reforging.
The Mason's Guild, where the Wool Weaver sells wool, glass and clay in every colour.
The windmill, with turning sails, on the north-west edge. The Mine Merchant stands near it, selling ores, stone and pickaxes.
Greenhollow is a working farm with fields, and the Farm Merchant sells crops and seeds there. Further west the Mistfall waterfall pours from the island onto a small pond islet below.
Timberline Lodge sits among great trees. The Lumber Merchant buys logs and sells wood and axes.

Just off the south avenue, on the lawn in front of the gazebo, stands the brainrot podium: statues of the three best brainrot collectors on gold, silver and copper pedestals, with their scores. See Brainrots.
The tavern, with a beer garden and a gazebo, is where the Bartender sells drinks. The build calls the building the Gilded Gull. A bridge from the beer garden leads to the Arcane Library.
The east: the Bazaar Promenade and the Grand Bazaar
The east: the Bazaar Promenade and the Grand Bazaar

The east avenue is a tree-lined promenade with benches, flower planters, banner posts and a koi garden with a brook. It ends at the Bazaar Gate, a great arch with a hanging "GRAND BAZAAR" sign, and a wide dark-oak bridge leads from it to the Grand Bazaar islet.
