Seraphine Vael's enchanting hall stands on an islet to the south-east. Inside, a giant open book floats under a crystal. Talk to her to open the enchanting table. See Enchanting.

On its own islet to the south stands a great stone ring with a shimmering purple veil. A sign on it sends you home: walk through and you are on your Private Island. The portal on your island brings you back.

Starwatch is a small observatory islet in the north-east, reached from the terrace. Right-click the telescope and you get a short stargazing show: fireworks burst into stars over the observatory, a field of sparkles fills the sky, and you get Night Vision for 15 seconds.
The first time you look through it you earn the Stargazer advancement and 500 coins. Only one person can use the telescope at a time.

The minimap in the top right shows the town and its NPCs. The map opens zoomed in when you are in the hub.

Your purse and your bank: where coins come from, what dying costs, and how the Banker's daily interest works.

Coins are the currency of SkyRPG, as on Hypixel SkyBlock. You carry them in your purse and can keep them in the bank in Skyhaven. Everything that costs coins, from a pickaxe to a slayer quest to an Auction House bid, comes out of your purse. This page explains the purse, what happens to it when you die, and how the bank and its daily interest work.
Your purse is the coins you carry. It is saved with your profile, so each profile has its own.

The SkyBlock sidebar shows your purse. The SkyBlock Menu shows it too, next to your character.
/coins shows your purse and your bank in chat. /coins <player> shows someone else's.
Large numbers are shortened to fit, for example 1.23B. Hover to see the full number.

Selling to NPC shops: every merchant buys anything that has an NPC price. See NPC Shops.
Trading: the Bazaar for materials and the Auction House for gear.
Monsters: each kill in the Hub's areas and on the islands pays a few coins, and slayer bosses pay more. See The Hub and Slayers.
Skill levels, which pay coins as well as stats. See Skills overview.
Minions, whose output you sell. See Minions.
Like on Hypixel, you keep your items when you die, but you lose half the coins in your purse. Then you wake up on your Private Island. Coins in the bank are safe.

The Banker keeps the Skyhaven Bank, in the middle of the north side of the village. Right-click him to open the bank screen. You must be at the Banker to use it, because the server checks that you are still talking to him.
The screen has a card for each direction.
All (deposit) | Moves your whole purse into the bank
Half (deposit) | Moves half your purse into the bank
All (withdraw) | Moves your whole bank balance into the purse
Half (withdraw) | Moves half the bank balance into the purse
Deposit and Withdraw with a typed amount | Move exactly that many coins
You can type an amount in the box. Letters work as shorthand: 2.5k is 2,500, 1m is 1,000,000 and 1b is 1,000,000,000. Press Enter to deposit, or Shift+Enter to withdraw.
The screen also shows your last ten deposits and withdrawals with their times. Interest payments appear in that list as deposits.
Coins in the bank are not lost when you die, and they earn interest. Spend what you need, and put the rest in the bank before a risky fight.
Your first login each day pays interest into the bank.
When | The first time you log in on a new calendar day
Where it goes | Into the bank, not the purse

The 1% hits the cap at a balance of 500,000 coins. Keeping more than that earns the same 5,000. You need at least 100 coins in the bank to earn a whole coin. Your very first login, with an empty bank, pays nothing. You get a chat line when interest arrives: "Your bank paid N in interest today (1%, up to 5,000)."
Interest is paid only when you log in, so missing a day costs you that day's interest. It does not stack up.
Hypixel pays 2% every 31 hours, with higher caps and upgrade accounts. That is not built yet: the bank here pays the simple daily rate above.
A balance of 100,000 earns 1,000 a day. Put coins you are saving for something expensive into the bank at the end of each session.
Lost on death | Half the purse
Auction House listing fee | 1%, 2% or 2.5% by price

Hypixel SkyBlock's nine skills, their XP curve and what every level gives: a perk, stats, coins and SkyBlock XP.

Skills are how your character grows. You gain XP in a skill by doing what it is about, and every level gives permanent stats, coins and SkyBlock XP. The skills, their XP curve and their rewards are Hypixel SkyBlock's. Open the SkyBlock Menu and choose Skills, or type /skills. Hover a skill to see your perk, everything it gives you so far, and what the next level adds.

Mining | 60 | Spelunker: +4 Mining Fortune | Defense: +1 (1 to 14), +2 (15 on)

Foraging | 50 | Logger: +4 Foraging Fortune | Strength: +1 (1 to 14), +2 (15 on)

Farming, Mining, Combat, Foraging, Fishing and Enchanting earn XP by doing them. Two more earn XP alongside:

Carpentry: crafting (the Recipe Book or a crafting table) gives 3% of what the ingredients sell for to an NPC, as on Hypixel. 160 Cobblestone into an Enchanted Cobblestone is 4.8 Carpentry XP.
Taming: whatever XP your active pet earns, you earn in Taming too.
Alchemy earns XP from brewing potions (see Alchemy).
Every skill uses Hypixel's curve. The table shows the XP needed to reach each level in total.
Every XP gain shows above the hotbar ("+4 Mining (54/125)").
Every level of every skill gives:

The perk's next tier and the skill's stats (above). They are permanent and stack with your gear.
Coins: 100 at level 1, 250, 500, 750, 1,000 at level 5, then more each level, up to 1,000,000 for each level from 45 on. A skill to 50 pays 17,259,100 coins; to 60, 27,259,100.
SkyBlock XP: 5 a level up to 10, 10 a level from 11 to 25, 20 from 26 to 50, and 30 from 51 to 60.

Harvest the Farm, the Barn and the Mushroom Desert for Farming XP, crops and collections; Farming Fortune, the Farm Merchant and farming minions.

Farming levels by harvesting crops. The Farming skill is Hypixel SkyBlock's: 60 levels, the Farmhand perk (+4 Farming Fortune a level, 240 at level 60) and bonus Health every level. See Skills overview for the XP curve and what each level pays.
Crops only break in the farming areas, and every crop you harvest grows back after a few seconds.
The Barn | the Farm's launch pad (Farming I) | Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, Pumpkins, Melons
Mushroom Desert | over the Barn's bridge (Farming V) | Cactus, Sugar Cane, Cocoa Beans, Red and Brown Mushrooms, Sand
Mountain | Hub, south | Carrots, in the cave at its foot
Crops pay XP only when fully grown. The Barn and the Mushroom Desert also hold farm animals (Cows, Pigs, Chickens, Rabbits, Sheep, Mooshrooms); killing them pays Combat XP, not Farming.
Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, Melon, Sugar Cane, Cactus | 4
Blocks you placed yourself never pay XP, and neither do minions: only what you harvest with your own hands counts.

What you harvest fills the Farming collections: Wheat, Seeds, Carrot, Potato, Pumpkin, Melon Slice, Sugar Cane, Cactus, Cocoa Beans, Mushroom and the rest of the 20. Each tier unlocks recipes in the Recipe Book: Wheat I opens the Wheat Minion, and higher tiers open the enchanted forms. Items you collect from your minions count too.

Farming Fortune | Each full 100 drops the crop's items one more time, and the rest is the chance of one more. It works on fully grown crops, Melons, Pumpkins, Sugar Cane, Cactus and Cocoa, not on Mushrooms. The Farmhand perk gives +4 a level.
Wheat Fortune and the other crop fortunes | Listed on gear, but have no effect yet.

The Farm Merchant in Skyhaven and the Windmill Operator at the Barn sell the same goods: Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, Melons, Sugar Cane, Pumpkins, Cocoa Beans, Mushrooms, Sand, Cactus, Enchanted Bone Meal and the Rookie Hoe. Click any crop in your inventory to sell it (see NPC shops). Jake, in the Mushroom Desert, trades animal axes.
Farming minions work on your island: Wheat, Carrot, Potato, Pumpkin, Melon, Mushroom, Cactus, Cocoa Beans, Sugar Cane, Nether Wart, Flower and the animal minions. See Minions.
A reforge and Potato Books make a farming tool better: see Reforging.
Not built yet: the Garden, Jacob's contests and Visitors, and crop-specific Fortune.
Hypixel's Heart of the Mountain - HotM tiers 1 to 10, Tokens of the Mountain, the 46-perk tree bought with powder, Core of the Mountain and Pickaxe Abilities.

Heart of the Mountain (HotM) is Hypixel SkyBlock's second mining progression, next to the Mining skill. It grows with HotM XP, mostly from Commissions in the Dwarven Mines, and opens a tree of perks that you buy with Tokens of the Mountain and level up with powder. Open it with /hotm. It's per profile.
Each tier opens the next row of the tree. HotM 2 opens the Forge, and every tier up to 6 gives it one more slot.
The tree is Hypixel's: 46 perks on a grid, tier 1 at the bottom, tier 10 at the top. In the menu:

Coal: locked. Emerald: unlocked. Diamond: maxed. Blocks are Pickaxe Abilities; the red block in the middle is Core of the Mountain; redstone is a perk you switched off.
A perk can be unlocked with a Token of the Mountain once its tier is open and it's next to a perk you already have (Mining Speed, at the bottom, is the first).
Click an unlocked perk to level it up with powder (shift-click: ten levels). Each level costs more: Mining Speed's level 2 costs 27 Mithril Powder, level 50 over 130,000.
Right-click a perk to switch it off (it keeps its level) or back on.
Hover any perk for what it gives at its level and the next, and what the next level costs.
Lower perks are paid with Mithril Powder (from the Dwarven Mines), higher ones with Gemstone Powder (Crystal Hollows) and the top three tiers with Glacite Powder (Glacite Tunnels).

What works now: Mining Speed (+20 Mining Speed a level), Mining Fortune (+2 a level), Titanium Insanium (a bigger Titanium chance), Powder Buff (more powder), Quick Forge (shorter forging), Great Explorer (better treasure chests in the Hollows), Core of the Mountain (below) and the Mining Speed Boost ability, and the Glacite Powder perks below. The other perks show what they do but don't do it yet.
Warm Heart | Up to +20 Cold Resistance
Metal Head | Up to +100 Dwarven Metal Fortune
Miner's Blessing | +30 Magic Find on the mining islands
Strong Arm | Up to +500 Mining Speed on Dwarven Metals (Mithril, Titanium, Glacite, Tungsten, Umber)
Rags to Riches | Up to +200 Mining Fortune in the Glacite Mineshafts
Eager Adventurer | Up to +400 Mining Speed in the Glacite Mineshafts
Surveyor | Up to +15% chance to find a Glacite Mineshaft
No Stone Unturned | Up to +25% chance to find Suspicious Scrap in the mineshafts
Gifts from the Departed | Up to a 20% chance at one more item from a Frozen Corpse
Dead Man's Chest | Up to a 25% chance of one more Frozen Corpse when you enter a mineshaft
Vanguard Seeker | Up to +50% chance that a mineshaft is the Fairy mineshaft (Vanguard Corpses)
Mineshaft Mayhem | A random buff each time you enter a mineshaft: +5% scrap chance, +100 Mining Fortune, +200 Mining Speed, +10 Cold Resistance or -25% Pickaxe Ability cooldown
Daily Grind | Your first commission each day on each mining island gives 500 powder for each HotM level
Not yet: Steady Hand (Gemstone Spread), Crystalline (crystals in mineshafts), and the Gemstone Infusion and Sheer Force abilities.

The perk in the middle of the tree, levelled with powder (50,000 Mithril Powder for level 2 up to 1,250,000 Glacite Powder for 10). Its levels give a Forge slot (2), a Commission slot (3), +1 Mithril Powder per Mithril block (4), Tokens of the Mountain (+1 at 5 and 7, +2 at 10), and make the Pickaxe Abilities stronger from level 2.
Unlocking a Pickaxe Ability perk selects it; click another unlocked one to switch. Right-click with a pickaxe, drill or gauntlet in a SkyBlock world to use it (2 minute cooldown):
Mining Speed Boost: +200% Mining Speed for 10 seconds (+250% for 15 seconds with Core of the Mountain 2).
Mithril Powder | Mining Mithril in the Dwarven Mines (1, 2 or 5 a block), 500 per Commission
Gemstone Powder | Gemstones in the Crystal Hollows and the Glacite Tunnels, treasure chests, Hollows Commissions
Glacite Powder | Glacite, Tungsten and Umber in the Glacite Tunnels, Tunnels Commissions, the Glacite Mineshafts, the Fossil Excavator, Dr. Stone
Admins: /sbhotm xp|powder|reset, /sbhotm perk <player> <perk> <level> (free, for testing) and /sbhotm stats <player> (mining stats).

Mine the Coal Mine, Gold Mine, Deep Caverns and Dwarven Mines for Mining XP, ore and collections; Hypixel's block strength, Mining Speed and Breaking Power; Mining Fortune; merchants and mining minions.

Mining levels by breaking stone and ore. The Mining skill is Hypixel SkyBlock's: 60 levels, the Spelunker perk (+4 Mining Fortune a level) and +1 Defense a level (+2 from level 15). See Skills overview for the XP curve and what each level pays.
Stone and ore only break in the mining areas. A broken block turns to bedrock for a few seconds, then comes back, so the ore never runs out.
Coal Mine | Hub, north | Stone, Coal Ore
Gold Mine | through the Coal Mine's gold gate (Mining I) | Stone, Coal Ore, Iron Ore, Gold Ore
Deep Caverns | the Gold Mine's lift shaft (Mining V) | Stone and the ore of each layer
Dwarven Mines | the Obsidian Sanctuary's launch pad (Mining XII) | Mithril, Titanium, every ore and Pure Ores
The End | the Spider's Den's west pad (Combat XII) | End Stone, Obsidian
The Deep Caverns' six layers each have their own ore:
Obsidian Sanctuary | Diamond, Obsidian, Diamond Blocks

The rarer the block, the longer it takes to grow back: Stone and Coal Ore 4 to 6 seconds, Gold Ore and Diamond Ore 8, Obsidian 20, Diamond Blocks 30. Your own island has no ore to mine, but a minion can mine for you there.
Deepslate versions pay the same. Sand, Gravel and Diamond Blocks pay nothing. Blocks you placed yourself never pay XP, and neither do minions: only what you break with your own hands counts.

What you mine fills the Mining collections: Cobblestone, Coal, Gold Ingot, Iron Ingot, Redstone, Diamond, Emerald, Obsidian, Gravel, Sand and the rest of the 25. Each tier unlocks recipes in the Recipe Book: Cobblestone I opens the Cobblestone Minion, Cobblestone IV the Enchanted Cobblestone. Items you collect from your minions count too.

On the mining islands (the Gold Mine, the Deep Caverns, the Dwarven Mines, The End; not the Hub or your own island) blocks break by Hypixel's rules. Every block has a Block Strength and needs a Breaking Power:

A pickaxe with less Breaking Power than the block needs can't break it at all ("You need a tool with a Breaking Power of 4 to mine Mithril!").
Otherwise it takes 30 × strength ÷ Mining Speed ticks (a tick is 1/20 of a second), never less than 4 ticks, unless your Mining Speed is over 30 × the strength (60 × for ores, Pure Ores, Obsidian, Mithril and Titanium): then it breaks at once.
Iron, Gold, Lapis and Redstone Ore | 30 | 2
Pickaxes have Hypixel's numbers: a Wooden Pickaxe has Breaking Power 1 and 70 Mining Speed, Stone 2 and 110, Iron 3 and 160, Diamond 4 and 220, the Mithril Pickaxe 5 and 300.
Mining Speed | Breaks blocks faster (see above). Pickaxes, Heart of the Mountain perks and some armour carry it.

Mining Fortune | Each full 100 drops the ore's items one more time, and the rest is the chance of one more. It counts for ores, Mithril and Titanium, not for Stone or Obsidian. The Spelunker perk gives +4 a level.
Breaking Power | Which blocks your pickaxe can break at all (see above).

The Mine Merchant in Skyhaven sells Coal, Iron and Gold Ingots, Torches, Cobblestone, Stone and Gravel, the Rookie and Promising Pickaxes, and a Gold Pickaxe for 3 Gold Ingots. The Iron Forger and the Gold Forger in the Gold Mine's camp sell ingots, armour and pickaxes. Right-click a merchant to buy, and click any item in your inventory to sell it (see NPC shops).
Mining minions work on your island: Cobblestone, Coal, Iron, Gold, Lapis, Redstone, Emerald, Diamond, Obsidian, Gravel, Sand, Quartz, Glowstone and more. See Minions.
A reforge and Potato Books make a pickaxe better: see Reforging.
The Dwarven Mines go further: Mithril and Titanium, Commissions, the Heart of the Mountain and the Forge.
Not built yet: the Crystal Hollows and Glacite Tunnels, Gemstones, Mining Spread and Pristine.
Chop the Hub's Forest and The Park for Foraging XP, logs and collections; Foraging Fortune, the Lumber Merchant and foraging minions.

Foraging levels by chopping trees. The Foraging skill is Hypixel SkyBlock's: 50 levels, the Logger perk (+4 Foraging Fortune a level) and +1 Strength a level (+2 from level 15). See Skills overview for the XP curve and what each level pays.
Logs and leaves only break in the forests. What you chop grows back: logs after 20 seconds, leaves after 15.
Birch Park | The Park, where you arrive (Foraging I) | Birch
Spruce Woods | The Park, west | Spruce
Dark Thicket | The Park, east | Dark Oak
The Howling Cave in the Park is for fighting, not chopping.
Every log pays 6 XP, whatever the tree. Leaves pay nothing. Blocks you placed yourself never pay XP, and neither do minions: only what you chop with your own hands counts.

What you chop fills the Foraging collections: Oak, Birch, Spruce, Dark Oak, Acacia and Jungle Log. Each tier unlocks recipes in the Recipe Book: the wood's minion, then its enchanted form. Items you collect from your minions count too.
Foraging Fortune | Each full 100 drops the log one more time, and the rest is the chance of one more. The Logger perk gives +4 a level.

The Lumber Merchant in Skyhaven sells logs (25 coins each), the Rookie Axe (12 coins), the Promising Axe (35), the Sweet Axe and Efficient Axe (100) and basic wooden tools. Click any log in your inventory to sell it (see NPC shops). Master Tactician Funk in the Savanna Woodland has a shop too.
Foraging minions work on your island: Oak, Birch, Spruce, Jungle, Dark Oak, Acacia and Flower. See Minions.
A reforge and Potato Books make an axe better: see Reforging.
Not built yet: Hypixel's newer foraging island with its trees, and the Foraging collections that come from them (Fig, Mangrove, Helix and others).
Hypixel's fishing - sea creatures, Good to Outstanding treasure, baits, lava fishing in the Crystal Hollows and on the Crimson Isle, Trophy Fish, and Fishing XP from catches and kills.

Fishing levels by catching things with a rod and killing the sea creatures that come up. The Fishing skill is Hypixel SkyBlock's: 50 levels, the Treasure Hunter perk (+0.1 Treasure Chance a level) and bonus Health every level. See Skills overview for the XP curve and what each level pays.
Any water you can reach works: the Hub's Wilderness has a lake with Fisherman Gerald's hut and dock, and Birch Park in The Park has one too. Cast, wait for the bobber to dip, and reel in.

Lava: in the Crystal Hollows, any rod's bobber floats on the Magma Fields' lava sea, for the Hollows' lava sea creatures and lava catches. On the Crimson Isle you need a lava rod (Starter Lava Rod, Polished Topaz Rod, Magma Rod, Inferno Rod, Hellfire Rod, Elle's Lava Rod), and its lava brings up Trophy Fish too.
Each time you reel in a bite, in this order:

A sea creature, at your Sea Creature Chance (20% to start; rods, armour and baits add to it). On your private island it's a quarter of that.
On the Crimson Isle's lava, otherwise maybe a Trophy Fish (see Crimson Isle).
Otherwise treasure (in water), at your Treasure Chance (your Fishing level gives it). Treasure is a Good Catch (89%), a Great Catch (10%) or an Outstanding Catch (1%), each with its own message.
Otherwise a fish: Raw Cod, Raw Salmon, Tropical Fish or Pufferfish (in lava: Netherrack, Magma Cream, Blaze Powder, Glowstone Dust, Quartz or Nether Wart).
Everything goes straight into your inventory.
Good Catch | 16 Raw Cod or Raw Salmon, 12 Tropical Fish or Pufferfish, 32 Clay, 16 Sponges, 8 Prismarine Shards or Crystals, 4 Grand Experience Bottles, 25,000 to 50,000 coins
Great Catch | 3 to 4 enchanted fish, an Enchanted Sponge, Clay or Ink Sac, a Titanic Experience Bottle, a Common Squid pet, 100,000 to 250,000 coins
Outstanding Catch | 24 to 32 enchanted fish, 8 Enchanted Sponges or Prismarine Crystals, an Epic or Legendary Squid pet, 500,000 to 1,000,000 coins

A sea creature surfaces at your bobber and comes for you, with Hypixel's name, level, health and catch message ("You caught a Sea Walker."). Fishing rods hit sea creatures twice as hard. Whoever kills one gets its coins, its drops (rare ones are announced with their odds) and its Fishing XP, which is where most Fishing XP comes from. Sea creatures killed on a private island give no Fishing XP.
Which one comes up depends on your Fishing level and where you fish; rarer ones are much less likely:
Squid | 1 | 50 | 25 | Ink Sacs, Lily Pads, Squid Boots

Hypixel's enchanting - the Enchantment Table, enchanted books and the anvil, ultimate enchantments, and the Enchanting skill.

Enchanting makes your weapons, armour and tools stronger with Hypixel's 145 enchantments: Sharpness, Critical, Protection, Growth, Efficiency, Life Steal, the ultimate enchantments and the rest. Enchantments are paid for with experience levels (the green number above your hotbar), and every level you spend levels up the Enchanting skill.

Use any enchanting table (there's one in the Hub, and you can place your own on your island), or talk to Seraphine Vael in the Hub. Put the item in the slot: the list shows every enchantment it can take. Pick one to see what it does and a button for each level the table can give (up to V for most, less for some), each with its XP cost.

Click a level to put it on. Most enchants cost 10 to 50 levels at the top table level; some cost more.
An enchantment that conflicts comes off: Sharpness replaces Smite and Bane of Arthropods, Protection replaces the other Protections, Life Steal replaces Syphon and Mana Steal.
Click the level the item already has to take it off (it costs the same).
Levels above what the table gives (Sharpness VI and VII, Growth VI...) only come from books.
Enchanted books carry an enchantment, often at a level the table can't give. Most of them are on the Bazaar, in the Oddities tab, one group per enchantment.
Use any anvil to open Combine Items (see Reforging):

Book on an item: the enchantment goes on (if it fits the item) for the XP levels of that level.
Book on a book: two books of the same enchantment and level make one of the next level, for free. They combine up to the table's top level (two Sharpness IV make V, but two V don't make VI); enchantments the table doesn't have combine up to their highest book.
The higher level always stays: a Sharpness III book does nothing on a Sharpness V sword.
Ultimate enchantments (One For All, Ultimate Wise, Soul Eater, Swarm, Legion...) only come as books and show in bold pink. An item can hold one: putting on another replaces it.
Each enchantment's tooltip says what it does at its level. They work as on Hypixel:

Damage (added to the Combat skill's bonus) | Sharpness, Power (bows), Smite (undead), Bane of Arthropods, Ender Slayer, Cubism (creepers and slimes), Impaling (sea mobs), Smoldering, Gravity, Dragon Hunter, First Strike (first hit), Triple Strike (first three hits), Execute, Prosecute, Giant Killer, One For All, Swarm
Stats while worn | Protection (Defense), Growth (Health), True Protection, Big Brain, Smarty Pants (Intelligence), Sugar Rush (Speed), Rejuvenate (Health Regen)

Stats while held | Critical (Crit Damage), Vicious (Ferocity), Divine Gift (Magic Find), Efficiency (Mining Speed), Harvesting and Cultivating (Farming Fortune), the Turbo enchants (their crop's Fortune), Angler (Sea Creature Chance), Luck of the Sea, Expertise, Compact
On a hit | Life Steal (heals 0.5% of your health a level), Syphon (heals on crits), Mana Steal, Fire Aspect, Knockback, Thunderlord (every third hit), Cleave (hits mobs around)
On a kill | Scavenger (coins by the mob's level), Vampirism (heals your missing health)
Abilities | Ultimate Wise (less mana for the item's ability)

The others show on the item but don't do anything yet: Looting, Luck, Experience, Venomous, Lethality, most fishing and farming upgrades (Lure, Caster, Replenish...) and most ultimate enchantments. Bookshelf Power and the Enchanting level some enchants need are coming. For bonus Enchanting XP and high-level books, see the Experimentation Table.
Spending experience levels at the table or the anvil gives Enchanting XP: 3.5 × levels^1.5 (spending 30 levels gives 575). See Skills for what each level gives.
Hypixel's Experimentation Table - Superpairs, Chronomatron and Ultrasequencer for Enchanting XP, enchanted books, bottles and the Guardian pet.
The Experimentation Table runs Hypixel's three enchanting experiments. They pay Enchanting XP, and Superpairs also gives enchanted books, Experience Bottles, the Guardian pet and more.
Its recipe unlocks at Enchanting X: 8 logs around an Experience Bottle (see the Recipe Book). It's furniture: place it on your island and right-click it. Break it to take it back.
Every experiment comes in stakes. A stake needs an Enchanting level and costs XP levels (the green number above your hotbar) to start.

A board of face-down tiles. Each click turns one over; turn two of the same prize in a row and you win it. A wrong pair turns back after a moment, so remember where things are. When your clicks run out (or the board is cleared), the board is shown and you get everything you won.
Two tiles are power-ups: the Feather gives 3 more clicks, and the Diamond makes the next tile you turn find its pair by itself.

Books are a random table enchantment at the table's top level (Sharpness V, Growth V...). An ultra-rare book is a level above that (Sharpness VI).
Charges: each Superpairs uses one of your 3 charges. A charge comes back 24 hours after you used it. You can buy one back early for 50, then 100, then 200 XP levels (three a day).

Right-click to drink it: each dose makes every add-on milestone one step shorter (a chain of 4 gives what 5 did). Up to 3 doses.

How crafting works in SkyBlock: the crafting table, the Recipe Book, what unlocks a recipe, and the Carpentry XP every craft pays.

Crafting turns what you gather into better things: enchanted materials, minions, tools, armour. SkyBlock has 2,468 recipes, all from Hypixel, and two ways to use them: the crafting table and the Recipe Book. The Carpentry skill levels as you craft. The Recipe Book and Crafting page has the screens in full; this page is how it all fits together.

Crafting table | Right-click any crafting table (sneak to place blocks on it instead), or type /craft | Opens SkyBlock's 3 by 3 grid. Lay the ingredients out as on Hypixel; the result shows on the right. Craft makes one, Craft all as many as the grid holds.
Recipe Book | SkyBlock Menu, Recipe Book | Every recipe in a grid with search and filters. Craft makes the item straight from your inventory, with no table. Shift-click makes up to 64.
Both check the same rules. A locked recipe says what unlocks it, and crafting it is refused. Vanilla's crafting recipes are not used: only SkyBlock's.
Nothing | 965 | the basics you start with
A collection tier | 1,348 | Cobblestone I: Cobblestone Minion. Cobblestone IV: Enchanted Cobblestone
A slayer level | 140 | gear from the Revenant Horror, Tarantula Broodfather, Sven Packmaster and Voidgloom Seraph
A boss from the dungeons | 15 | stays locked for now

Collections fill as you gather: see Mining, Farming, Foraging and Fishing, or Collections. Slayer levels come from Slayers. A recipe that needs Inferno Demonlord or Riftstalker levels can't be unlocked yet, since those slayers aren't built.

Every craft pays Carpentry XP: 3% of what the ingredients sell for to an NPC, as on Hypixel. 160 Cobblestone into an Enchanted Cobblestone is 4.8 XP. It is quiet XP: no line above the hotbar, but your level-ups show as usual.
Carpentry has 50 levels on Hypixel's curve and gives +1 Health a level (see Skills overview). It has no perk.

The first time you craft a minion tier it counts as a new unique minion, which brings you closer to another minion slot (see Minions). Crafted items never count for collections: only what you gather does.

Crafting makes the item; reforging improves it afterwards with the Blacksmith's reforges, the Recombobulator and Potato Books. Merchants sell the basic tools and ingredients (see NPC shops), and the Bazaar sells the rest.

Place a Brewing Stand on your island and right-click it: three bottle slots at the bottom, the ingredient on top. Every brew takes 20 seconds and needs no fuel, and it keeps going with the stand closed.

Water Bottles + Nether Wart make Awkward Potions.

Right-click a potion to drink it. A splash potion gives its effect to every player within 8 blocks, you too. You get a "BUFF!" message, and /effects lists your effects with their time left.

Hypixel's swords, longswords, bows and wands: what each kind is, how Damage and the other stats work today, reforges, and where to get them.

Every weapon in SkyRPG SkyBlock is a Hypixel SkyBlock weapon, imported with its real name, rarity and stats. This page covers what the weapon kinds are, what works today, and how to get one. For the maths behind a hit, see Stats.
Sword | 156 | Fancy Sword, Aspect of the End, Pooch Sword, Hyperion
Bow | 44 | Death Bow, Hurricane Bow, Juju Shortbow, Terminator
Every one has its own page, and the SkyBlock Items page in the menu lists them all. See SkyBlock items and Items: weapons.

A weapon's tooltip is Hypixel's layout: the name in its rarity colour, then its stats in Hypixel's order (Damage, Strength, Crit Chance, Crit Damage, Bonus Attack Speed, Intelligence...), its lore, and the rarity line in bold, such as LEGENDARY SWORD. Weapons from the dungeons carry their requirements in the data, but the dungeons are not built yet.

Hypixel's own item data has stats and a little lore, but no ability text and no set bonuses. So abilities such as Instant Transmission, Wither Impact or a wand's blast, and the gemstone slots, stars and Power Scrolls some items list, do not exist in the game yet. A weapon is its stats.

The held weapon's stats count while it is in your main hand. A sword's Damage is its base hit, on the same scale as mob health: a 100 Damage sword hits for 100 against a mob with 100 health (internally 5 Damage is 1 vanilla damage point). Then:

Damage is multiplied by 1 + Strength / 100.
Roll Crit Chance. A crit multiplies by 1 + Crit Damage / 100.
The Combat skill's Warrior perk multiplies it again against mobs: +4% a Combat level, +1% more a level after 50.
A hit you swing before the weapon has recharged is weaker, as in vanilla. Hits show a damage number: grey for a normal hit, gold and bold for a crit.

This is close to Hypixel's damage but not identical. Hypixel adds 5 to the weapon's damage and part of your Strength before multiplying, and other bonuses add together. SkyRPG multiplies Damage by Strength and crits only. Ferocity, Bonus Attack Speed, Ability Damage and Swing Range are shown on items but do nothing yet.

Bows draw and shoot like vanilla bows. Hypixel's bow stats are on the item, but a Hypixel bow does not use them for its arrows yet: its Damage, Strength and Crit Damage do not change how hard an arrow hits. Held, a bow still adds its non-damage stats to you.

Wands are on the list with their stats (mostly Intelligence and Weapon Ability Damage), but their abilities are not built, so a wand has no attack. Mana and the Intelligence stat work, and the mana bar shows on the HUD, but nothing in SkyBlock spends mana yet.

Every weapon can be improved without changing what it is. The Blacksmith in the Hub gives a weapon a random reforge for coins (swords, bows and the others each have their own reforges), reforge stones give a chosen one, and the anvil takes a Recombobulator 3000 (one rarity up) and Hot Potato and Fuming Potato Books (+2 Damage and +2 Strength each, up to 15 books). All of it is on Reforging.
SkyBlock weapons never break and never need repairing. They are always unbreakable, as on Hypixel.
There is no loot from dungeons or world bosses to find them in yet. What works today:

NPC shops sell 36 weapons, the starter ones such as the Fancy Sword. See NPC shops.
Crafting makes 119 weapons from Hypixel's recipes. They show in the Recipe Book, with what unlocks each (a collection tier or a slayer level).
Slayers drop the items that the slayer weapon recipes need. See Slayers.
The Auction House lets players sell weapons to each other. See Auction House.
Admins can give any item with /sbitem.
Together, 150 of the 232 weapons have a shop offer or a crafting recipe; the rest need sources that arrive with later systems.

Talismans, rings, artifacts and relics in the Accessory Bag, Magical Power and Maxwell's Accessory Powers, and the four equipment slots.

Accessories (talismans, rings, artifacts and relics) give their stats just by being yours. Keep them in the Accessory Bag, where they also give Magical Power, which powers up the Accessory Power you pick at Maxwell. Equipment (necklaces, cloaks, belts, gloves and bracelets) is worn in its own four slots.

Open it from the Accessory Bag tile in the SkyBlock Menu, or with /accessories. It unlocks at Redstone collection II and grows by 6 slots with every Redstone tier after that (see Collections). Only accessories go in.
Every accessory you have counts for its stats, in the bag or in your inventory, with two rules:

Each accessory once: two Speed Rings give one Speed Ring's stats.
Only the highest of a line: with a Speed Ring, the Speed Talisman stops counting; with a Speed Artifact, both do.
Each accessory in the bag (once, and the highest of its line) gives Magical Power by its rarity. A Recombobulator 3000 raises it.
The bag's title shows your total.

Maxwell stands beside Seraphine in the Hub (the bag's crystal tab opens him too). He shows every power with what it gives you at your Magical Power. Click one to make it your power: its stats are multiplied by your Magical Power, 29.97 × ln(0.0019 × MP + 1)^1.2 (about ×0.44 at 16 Magical Power, ×9.6 at 250 and ×26 at 750).

Starter powers (Fortuitous, Pretty, Protected, Simple, Warrior) are yours from the start; the others (Commando, Disciplined, Inspired, Ominous, Prepared) need Combat XV.
Stone powers (Bloody, Silky, Sweet, Shaded, Forceful, Adept, Bizarre and 14 more) are learned by giving Maxwell 9 of their Power Stone. They also have a unique bonus that doesn't scale (Bloody: +10 Bonus Attack Speed). All of them are on the Bazaar.

Necklaces, cloaks, belts, gloves and bracelets go in the four equipment slots next to your armour in the inventory: Necklace, Cloak, Belt and Gloves (gloves or a bracelet). Their stats count while worn, with their reforge and Potato Books. Equipment takes the Blacksmith's equipment reforges (Astute, Blended, Brilliant...).

Not yet: Tuning Points, enrichments, the Redstone Miner's and Jacobus's extra bag slots, and the special accessories (Hegemony Artifact, Abicases, dungeon double Magical Power). Accessory abilities from Hypixel's lore (the Zombie Talisman's damage cut and the like) show on the item but aren't built.
The three backpack slots and five pack sizes still work, but nobody can get a pack in SkyBlock yet. Hypixel's backpacks will live in Storage.
Backpacks give you more room to carry things. You carry up to three at once, each in its own slot, and you open them on the move without putting anything down.

This is the survival game's backpack system, kept as a stand-in. Hypixel's backpacks (70 items, from Small to Jumbo, in many colours) are in the game as items, and the Recipe Book shows their recipes, but they do nothing yet: they will live in Storage when that part is built. The five packs below can no longer be crafted, sold or upgraded, so only an admin can hand you one.

Three backpack slots sit in a strip to the right of the inventory in the E screen (and on the creative inventory's Survival Inventory tab). Like the accessory strip, it hides while the recipe book is open.

Put a backpack in a slot: click it in, or shift-click it from your inventory.
Right-click the slot to open that backpack. Press B to open the first one (you can rebind the key under SkyRPG in Controls).
Backpacks cannot go inside backpacks.
A pack's contents are stored on the pack item, so it keeps them wherever it goes. Backpacks you carry are stored with you, so you keep them on death. The tooltip shows how full a pack is.
Each pack holds a number of stacks:

Hypixel's Quiver - where your arrows live, which one your bows shoot, arrow damage, the Arrow Swapper and Infinite Quiver.
Your arrows live in your Quiver, not your inventory. Arrows you pick up, buy or are given go into it by themselves (45 slots). Type /quiver to see it, take arrows out or put them in.

A bow shoots from your quiver: one arrow a shot, of the type you picked (or the first type in the quiver). Hold an Arrow Swapper and right-click to pick the next type, sneak and right-click for the one before. The Quiver screen shows which type your bows shoot.
Infinite Quiver on a bow saves the arrow 3% of the time per level.
A SkyBlock bow's arrow hits for 5 + the bow's Damage + the arrow's Damage, less if the bow wasn't fully drawn, then your Strength and crits count as for a melee hit.
Icy Arrow | +24 | Slowness I for 3 seconds
Glue Arrow | +15 | stops the target walking for 1.5 seconds
Bouncy, Armorshred, Explosive, Nansorb Arrows | +3 to +5 | their passives aren't in yet
Not yet: arrow requirements (Combat level, Target Practice), the Bouncy/Armorshred/Explosive/Nansorb passives, arrow poisons, and the hotbar's ninth slot showing the quiver.
Every stat in SkyRPG SkyBlock, which ones do something today, where they come from and the formulas for damage, crits, defense and mana.

Stats are the numbers that make your character stronger. Gear, skill levels, slayer levels, pets and your SkyBlock Level add to them, and the game adds them up twice a second. This page lists the stats, what each does in the game today, and the maths behind combat. Open Stats in the menu to see your own totals; hover a stat to see how much each source adds.

Every player starts with a base value for each stat (the tables below). Sources add to it.
Stats come from your worn armour and held item, from your skill levels, slayer levels and SkyBlock Level, and from an active pet. See Skills overview, Armour sets, Weapons, Slayers and SkyBlock Leveling.
Most stats are plain numbers. Crit Chance is a percentage.
Health and damage use SkyBlock's scale: 5 SkyBlock health is 1 vanilla health point. 100 Health is 20 vanilla points, which is 10 hearts. Damage numbers, mob nameplates and boss bars all use the same scale.
Hypixel's items carry about 70 stats, and all of them exist here with Hypixel's symbols. Only some have a gameplay effect so far; the tables say which.
Health | 100 | Your maximum health. 100 Health is 10 hearts.
Defense | 0 | Cuts the damage you take. 100 Defense halves it.
Strength | 0 | Each point adds 1% to your melee damage.
Crit Chance | 30% | The chance that a melee hit is a critical hit.
Crit Damage | 50% | The extra damage a critical hit does.
Speed | 100 | How fast you walk. 100 is normal.
Intelligence | 0 | Each point adds 1 to your maximum mana.
True Defense | 0 | Cuts True Damage the way Defense cuts the rest.
Vitality | 100 | How much healing you get. 100 is normal; 50 heals half as much.
Damage | none | Only weapons have it. It is the weapon's base damage.
Only your own melee hits use Strength and crits. Arrows and abilities do not (see Weapons).

Start with the weapon's Damage stat. A weapon with 120 Damage deals 120 on a fully charged swing (internally, 5 Damage is 1 vanilla damage point). If you swing before your weapon has recharged, the hit is weaker, as in vanilla.
Multiply by 1 + Strength / 100. Strength 100 doubles the hit.
Roll for a crit. If a random number from 0 to 100 is below your Crit Chance, multiply by 1 + Crit Damage / 100. Crits show a gold, bold number between two sparkles and play a crit sound.
Against mobs, multiply by the Combat skill's Warrior bonus: 1 + (4% x Combat level, +1% a level after 50).
Other multipliers apply on top, such as the damage reductions slayer bosses have. See Slayers.
Worked example: a 120 Damage weapon, 100 Strength, 30% Crit Chance and 50% Crit Damage, against a mob (Combat level 0).
Average over many hits | 240 x (1 + 0.30 x 0.50) = 276

This is simpler than Hypixel's formula. Hypixel adds 5 to the weapon's damage and part of your Strength before multiplying, and adds its other bonuses together. Here Damage is only multiplied by Strength, crits and Warrior, so the numbers will not match Hypixel's exactly.
Crit Chance above 100% is wasted: you already crit every time. Crit Damage is then worth more than more Crit Chance.
Crit Chance and Crit Damage multiply each other, so the lower one is worth more per point. With the starting 30% and 50%, a point of Crit Chance is the better buy.
Every time something hurts you, the damage is multiplied by 100 / (100 + Defense).

So "effective health" is Health x (1 + Defense / 100). Defense applies to mobs and bosses. It does not apply to damage that ignores invulnerability, such as the void. Armour pieces give Defense directly (they have no vanilla armour points).

Some boss attacks deal True Damage, which Defense does nothing against: Sven Packmaster's bites, the slam-dunk every slayer boss does to a player who stands still, the Atoned Horror's TNT and blast, and the Voidgloom Seraph's glyphs and beams. Only True Defense cuts it, by the same 100 / (100 + True Defense). See Slayers.
Every bit of healing you get is multiplied by Vitality / 100. It starts at 100. The Tarantula Broodfather's Noxious Paralysis and the Voidgloom Seraph's beams lower it during the fight.
Speed 100 is normal walking. Walking speed is multiplied by Speed / 100, so 150 Speed walks 50% faster.

You have 100 + Intelligence maximum mana. Mana regenerates by 2% of your maximum every second, so an empty bar takes about 50 seconds to refill whatever its size. The mana bar is on your HUD. Nothing in SkyBlock spends mana yet, because Hypixel's item abilities are not built. If your maximum drops (you take off a piece of gear), your current mana is cut to fit.
Mining Speed | 0 | How fast you break blocks. 100 makes it twice as fast.
Mining Fortune | 0 | Extra drops from ores.
Farming Fortune | 0 | Extra drops from crops.
Foraging Fortune | 0 | Extra drops from logs.
Fishing Speed | 0 | Fish bite sooner: the wait is cut by Fishing Speed / 300, so 300 makes them bite straight away.
Sea Creature Chance | 20% | The chance a bite is a sea creature.
Treasure Chance | 0% | The chance a bite that isn't a sea creature is treasure. Every Fishing level adds 0.1%.
Double Hook Chance | 0% | The chance a second sea creature comes up with the first.

When you break a block that counts (ores, grown crops, logs), it drops its normal drops again once for every full 100 Fortune, plus a chance for one more from the remainder. With 250 Fortune you get 2 extra copies and a 50% chance of a third. Crops only count when fully grown. See Mining, Farming and Foraging.
Farming Wisdom | Each point is 1% more Farming XP.
Mining Wisdom | Each point is 1% more Mining XP.
Foraging Wisdom | Each point is 1% more Foraging XP.
Combat Wisdom | Each point is 1% more Combat XP.
Fishing Wisdom | Each point is 1% more Fishing XP.
Alchemy Wisdom | Each point is 1% more Alchemy XP.
Magic Find | Better odds for rare drops.
Wisdom multiplies the XP you earn by 1 + Wisdom / 100. Magic Find multiplies the chance of rare drops by 1 + Magic Find / 100; for slayer bosses it helps drops under 5%. See Slayers.
Hypixel's items list many more stats. They show on tooltips and add up in your totals, but the game has no code for them yet:

Combat: Bonus Attack Speed, Ferocity, Ability Damage, Weapon Ability Damage, Swing Range, Sweep, Health Regen, Mending, Fear.
Mining: Breaking Power, Pristine, Mining Spread, and Ore, Block, Dwarven Metal and Gemstone Fortune.
Farming and foraging: the crop Fortunes (Wheat, Carrot, Potato, Pumpkin, Melon, Mushroom, Cactus, Sugar Cane, Nether Wart, Cocoa Beans) and Fig, Mangrove and Helix Fortune.
Fishing: Fishing Fortune (it only boosted the survival world's Tidescales) and Trophy Fish Chance.
Other: Pet Luck, Bonus Pest Chance, Heat, Cold and Pressure Resistance, Respiration, Tracking, Pull, and the Rift stats.
They start working as their systems land.

Skills give a fixed amount per level. The full table is on Skills overview; in short, Farming gives Farming Fortune and Health, Mining gives Mining Fortune and Defense, Combat gives Crit Chance and the Warrior perk, Foraging gives Foraging Fortune and Strength, Fishing gives Health, and Enchanting and Alchemy give Intelligence.

SkyBlock Level: +5 Health every level and +1 Strength every 5 levels. See SkyBlock Leveling.
Slayer levels: a small stat per level for each boss. See Slayers.
Gear: the armour you wear and the item in your hand, with their reforges and potato books. See Reforging.
An active pet. Hypixel's pets are not built; see Pets.
Weapon Damage is not a player stat. Only the weapon you hold carries it, and nothing can add to it.

Zone mobs with Hypixel levels and stats, what you see in a fight, how damage and defense work, the combat tag, and what a kill pays: Combat XP, coins and slayer progress.

You fight in the zones of the Hub's areas and the public islands. Their mobs have Hypixel's names, levels, health and damage. A kill pays Combat XP and coins, and the right mobs fill a slayer quest. This page covers what you see in a fight and what a kill gives you. For the maths of a hit, see Stats.

Mobs only spawn in a zone's fighting areas, up to a cap, and keep coming back. They do not burn in daylight, and neutral ones (the Ruins' wolves, the Deep Caverns' pigmen) attack anyone who comes near. Private Islands have no monsters.
Coal Mine (Hub) | Crypt Ghoul (30), Golden Ghoul (50)
Spider's Den | Splitter, Weaver, Dasher and Voracious Spiders (2 to 10), Gravel Skeleton (2); in the Spider Mound, level 42 spiders
The Park, Howling Cave | Pack Spirit (30), Howling Spirit (35), Soul of the Alpha (55)
Deep Caverns | Sneaky Creeper (3), Lapis Zombie (7), Redstone Pigman (10), Emerald Slime (15), Miner Zombies and Skeletons (15 and 20)

Every mob with its health, damage, Combat XP and coins is listed on The Hub and The Islands. The Barn's and the Mushroom Desert's cows, pigs, chickens, rabbits and sheep are farm animals, with a level but no attack and no reward.
What you see in a fight
What you see in a fight

Nameplates. A mob within 20 blocks shows [Lv 30] Crypt Ghoul with its health, on the same scale as your own. The level is green below 10, yellow below 20, gold below 30, red below 40 and dark red from 40. Switch them off in Settings under HUD ("Mob nameplates").
Damage numbers. Each hit pops a number over the mob for under a second. Normal hits are grey, critical hits are bold gold between two sparkles.
Boss bars for slayer bosses, with their timer.
What you see in a fight
The level on a zone mob is for show: its health and damage are Hypixel's own numbers, not scaled by level.

A melee hit is the weapon's Damage, times 1 + Strength / 100, times 1 + Crit Damage / 100 when it crits (Crit Chance is the chance), times the Combat skill's Warrior bonus against mobs (+4% a Combat level, +1% more a level after 50). Worked examples are on Stats. Bow damage and abilities are not built for Hypixel items yet; see Weapons.

A mob's damage is its Damage number, reduced by your Defense: the hit is multiplied by 100 / (100 + Defense), so 100 Defense halves it. Some slayer boss attacks are true damage, which only True Defense cuts. See Stats. All healing you get is multiplied by your Vitality.
If you die you keep your items, lose half your purse and respawn, as on Hypixel.

Fighting puts you in combat for 10 seconds. A red In combat box with the seconds left shows at the top of the screen, and you cannot teleport (Fast Travel, /warp, /hub, /is, /visit) while it lasts. You are tagged when you deal damage to or take damage from a hostile mob or another player (an arrow counts for whoever fired it). Each hit restarts the 10 seconds. Fall damage, fire, the void and hitting passive animals do not tag you, and dying clears it.

Combat XP: the mob's own number (a Graveyard Zombie 6, a Crypt Ghoul 36, a Golden Ghoul 50, a Spider Mound spider 36), raised by your Combat Wisdom. It levels the Combat skill, which gives Crit Chance, the Warrior perk, coins and SkyBlock XP. See Skills overview.
Coins straight into your purse (a Graveyard Zombie 1, a Crypt Ghoul 13, a Golden Ghoul 100, a Soul of the Alpha 50).
The mob's normal drops. Hypixel's mob drop tables are not imported yet.
Slayer progress. Each kill adds its Combat XP to a running slayer quest when the mob is one the boss wants.
Mobs from a spawner give only a quarter of the Combat XP and do not count for slayers. The zones' own mobs are natural spawns, so they count in full.

Maddox the Slayer in the Hub sells boss quests: Revenant Horror, Tarantula Broodfather, Sven Packmaster and Voidgloom Seraph, in up to five tiers. Kill the right mobs to fill the bar, then the boss rises. Its drops roll with Magic Find, rare ones are announced, and slayer levels give stats and unlock recipes. See Slayers.

Hypixel's Bestiary - 255 mob families on 19 islands, their kill tiers, and the SkyBlock XP and Milestone Health they give.

The Bestiary counts every mob you kill, by family: Hypixel's 255 families on 19 islands (Hub, The Farming Islands, Spider's Den, The End, Deep Caverns, Dwarven Mines, Crystal Hollows, The Park, your Private Island, and islands still to come). Open it with /bestiary (or /be).

A kill counts for the family named like the mob: a Crypt Ghoul for Crypt Ghoul, a Zealot Bruiser for Zealot, a Knifethrower for Goblin, any of the dragons for Dragon. Vanilla mobs with no name of their own (on your island) count for the Private Island's families: Zombie, Skeleton, Spider and the rest.
Each family has Hypixel's tiers: kill counts that get bigger each tier, up to the family's top tier (5 to 25). A common mob needs thousands of kills for its last tier, a boss only a handful.

Every new family tier: +1 SkyBlock XP.
Every 10 family tiers (all families added up): a Bestiary Milestone, +2 Health each, for good.
A panel in chat shows each tier up ("BESTIARY Goblin II → III").

The islands are down the left with how many of their families you've found; click one to see its families. Each card has the family's head, its tier (out of its top tier) and a bar to the next tier; families you've never killed show as ???. Hover a card for its kills and the kills its next tier needs. The header shows your Milestone and your tiers in all.
Not yet: Hypixel's per-family bonuses (damage and coins against the family), Magic Find from milestones, and the families of islands that aren't here yet.
Load a schematic or a village house, place its hologram, deliver the materials and watch it build itself from the ground up.

The Builder Station turns a blueprint into a real build. Pick a blueprint (one of Minecraft's village houses, or your own schematic file), place its glowing hologram where you want it on your island, deliver the materials it lists, press Build, and it rises from the ground up, layer by layer, in front of you.

In SkyBlock a Builder Station can only be given by an admin (/give @s skyrpg_builder:builder_station). Its only recipe was an Artisan Bench recipe, and the Artisan Bench is switched off, so players cannot craft one and no shop sells it.

With a Builder Station in hand, place it on your Private Island, inside your build area. It does not work in the Hub, and the public islands are protected, so you cannot place one there. Its crystal lens faces you, and new blueprints first appear behind it. Right-click it to open the builder menu.
Press Choose blueprint (or Blueprint... later). The picker has two tabs and two views:

Library: every blueprint on the server. Minecraft's own buildings are always there: the houses and town centres of all five village types (plains, taiga, savanna, desert, snowy), the igloo, the pillager outpost watchtower and the ruined portals. Schematics anyone has uploaded are listed first, with who uploaded them. You can delete your own uploads.
My schematics: the schematic files on your computer, in the schematics folder of your game (the same folder Litematica uses; Open folder opens it). Clicking one uploads it to the server's library and loads it. Uploaded blueprints are shared with everyone on the server.
Cards shows each blueprint as a card with a turning 3D preview and its size underneath. List is a compact list. Both have a search box.
Picking a blueprint closes the menu and goes straight to placing it in the world (below).

Supported files: .litematic (Litematica, every region), .schem (WorldEdit / Sponge, versions 1 to 3) and .nbt (vanilla structure block files). Old MCEdit .schematic files are not supported: save them as .litematic or .schem first. A blueprint can be at most 128 blocks on each side, 120,000 blocks in all, and the file at most 2 MB. Files from older Minecraft versions are updated as they load, and the card says why a file can't be read before you upload it.

A blueprint is placed in the world, not in a menu. Its hologram (see-through blocks with a cyan outline) follows where you aim: the side nearest you sits on the block you look at and the build stretches away from you. Walk around and aim until it's where you want it. A strip at the bottom of the screen shows the keys:
Aim | Move it (it follows the block you look at, up to 64 blocks away)
Scroll, or R | Turn it 90° (Shift+R: the other way)
↑ ↓ ← → | Nudge it one block away, towards you, left or right of where you look (Shift: 5 blocks). This locks it in place
Page Up / Page Down, or Shift+scroll | Raise or lower it
G | Lock it in place, or let it follow your aim again
Left-click, or Enter | Place it here
Esc, Backspace, or right-click | Cancel (it goes back to where it was)

While you place, clicks and those keys only move the hologram: you won't break or place blocks by accident. It turns red when it's more than 64 blocks from its station (or would cover the station), and then it can't be placed. To move a placed blueprint later, sneak + right-click the station (whatever you're holding), or open it and press Move in world. Moving one that's already placed starts locked where it is, so the arrow keys fine-tune it; press G to make it follow your aim again. You can place it from anywhere up to 64 blocks from the station.
Once placed, everyone nearby sees the hologram. Blocks that are already in place disappear from it, and blocks that are in the way glow red. Hologram on/off in the menu hides it.
The left side of the menu shows the blueprint four ways:

3D: a model that turns by itself; drag (or scroll) to turn it yourself. Real shows every block as it looks (torches, flowers, glass, water); Simple shows plain coloured cubes.
Top: seen from above, north up, higher blocks brighter.
Side: seen from the south.
Layers: one layer at a time; scroll for the others. Hover a block to see what it is.
While it builds, the parts not built yet are faded (in 3D they're cyan hologram), and the Layers view follows the layer being built.
The right side lists everything the build needs, how much you've delivered and a bar for each. Blocks already standing in the right place don't need materials.

Deliver all takes everything the build still needs from your inventory and backpacks (never more than it needs). Click one material to deliver just that one.
List or Grid: a list with names and bars, or a grid of bigger icons that fits many more at once.
Each material shows how many you carry (green: enough for what's missing, gold: some). Hover one for the details; Deliver all's tooltip says how much you could deliver now.
Shift-click a row, or press Take back, to get delivered materials back (not while it is building).
In creative mode delivering is free.
Anyone can open the station and deliver, so friends can chip in. The menu shows who delivered how much ("Delivered by").

Most blocks cost their own item. Doors, beds and tall plants are paid for once; double slabs cost two slabs; candles, sea pickles, turtle eggs, petals and snow layers cost one item per piece.
Crops cost their seeds (wheat seeds, carrots, potatoes...), and a potted plant costs a flower pot plus the plant.
Grass blocks, dirt paths, farmland and mycelium take plain dirt.
Water and lava sources cost a full bucket; the empty bucket comes back in the leftovers.
Some blocks are never built and are left out of the cost ("skipped" in the menu): spawners, bedrock, barriers, portals and portal frames, command and structure blocks, budding amethyst, infested blocks, player heads, the dragon egg, and blocks from other mods.
Chests, barrels and the like are built empty. Signs keep their text, banners their patterns and heads their owner.
When everything is delivered the status turns READY TO BUILD. Press Build (or Enter). The menu closes so you can watch.

The station's lens lights up and the build goes up layer by layer from the ground, sweeping out from the station, with a beam from the lens to each new block and a glowing plane at the layer being built. Each layer is cleared first, then its solid blocks go in, then the things that hang on them (torches, doors, carpets). It takes its time so you can watch it: about 12 seconds plus a little per block and per layer, with a short rest after each layer. A small village house takes about 45 seconds, bigger builds a few minutes (3 at most).

Everyone within 64 blocks gets a build panel in the bottom-right corner: a big 3D model of the build (built part in colour, the rest as hologram), its name, a progress bar, the layer, blocks placed and about how long is left. It says FINISHED! when it's done.
The 3D previews (blueprint cards, the station, the build panel) have two settings under K menu → Settings → Builder:

Preview style: Real (default) or Simple. The Real / Simple button in the station and the blueprint picker switches it too.
Preview quality: Low, Medium or High (default). Lower is lighter on slower computers.

Stand clear: the build waits for anyone standing where a block goes.
If it runs out of a material (someone took a block away, for example), it pauses and says what it's waiting for. Deliver more and it carries on.
Stop pauses the build. Press Build again later and it carries on where it left off.
When it's done you get a burst of fireworks and a message. Build again plans the same blueprint again (move it first); New blueprint picks another.

With Clear site on (the default), blocks that are in the way are removed as the layers go up, so the build comes out exactly like the blueprint, air included. What they drop goes to the station's leftovers, but only blocks you could break by hand drop anything: dirt, sand, plants, logs and planks come back, while stone and ores just vanish. Items inside containers that are cleared away go to the leftovers too. Bedrock and other unbreakable blocks are never touched.
With Clear site off, nothing that's already there is touched: blocks in the way are simply left out of the build.
Press Collect leftovers to take them.
Break the station with an axe to move it. Everything delivered to it, and its leftovers, drop on the spot. A build in progress stops.

Put a schematic you made with Litematica (or downloaded) in your schematics folder and it shows up under My schematics, with a preview, right away.
Use Turn before moving: it turns about the middle, so the build stays roughly where you put it.
Turn Clear site off when building into an existing build, so nothing of yours is removed.
Fifteen Italian brainrot creatures to catch for your album. They only appear in the old survival world, so they cannot be found in SkyBlock today.

Brainrots are fifteen silly creatures: Tung Tung Tung Sahur with his bat, Tralalero Tralala in his sneakers, Bombardiro Crocodilo circling overhead, and twelve more. Walk up to one and it shouts its own name. Right-click it to catch it, and it goes into your album, where you can look at it and hear it again whenever you like.

Brainrots only spawn in the old survival world, which is now an archive. In the Hub and on the islands none appear, so there is no way to catch one in SkyBlock today. The album, the catch cards and the leaderboard podium still exist; where brainrots will turn up in SkyBlock is not decided yet.
This is how they behave in the survival world, where they still spawn:

They appear on the surface, 20 to 44 blocks from you, never in caves or other dimensions.
They're not common: about one every five or six minutes while you're out exploring, and only one near you at a time. They don't stay long either: after 6 minutes (or once you go far away) a brainrot vanishes in a puff.
Some like certain places (see the table) and are much more common there: beach brainrots on beaches, desert ones in deserts. Cappuccino Assassino mostly comes out at night, and La Vaca Saturno Saturnita comes out only at night.
When one is within 10 blocks it says its name, with music notes over its head, so listen out.

They move in their own ways: most walk, some hop, Ballerina Cappuccina spins, La Vaca Saturno Saturnita floats just off the ground, and the two fliers (Bombardiro Crocodilo and Bombombini Gusini) circle high above you. Fliers swoop down to head height every half a minute or so (sooner while you're close) and fly slowly for a few seconds: that's when you catch them.
Right-click a brainrot to catch it. It shouts its name one last time and vanishes in a puff, and you get coins:

Catching one for the first time shows NEW BRAINROT! on your screen. Brainrots can't be hurt (hitting one just makes it jump), and whoever right-clicks first gets it. Catch all fifteen and you're a Brainrot Master: the whole server hears about it.

When anyone catches a brainrot, a card slides in at the top left for everyone on the server: the catcher and the brainrot side by side, both turning in 3D, who caught what (NEW BRAINROT! if it was their first of that kind, or how many they have now) and its rarity. The brainrot shouts its name for everyone else too. If several come at once, they queue up.
Move or resize the card in the HUD editor ("Brainrot catches"). In Settings → Brainrots, choose Card and voice, Card only or Off.

The top three brainrot collectors stand on a podium in the Hub, on the lawn just south-east of spawn (around 12, 25), facing the plaza. Nobody can catch brainrots at the moment, so the ranking does not change:

Statues of them with their skins, 1st on the gold pedestal in the middle, 2nd on silver to its left and 3rd on copper to its right. They turn their heads to watch you walk past, and #1 sparkles.
A plate on each pedestal shows their name, how many of the fifteen they've found, how many catches they've made in all, and how many kinds of each rarity they have, coloured by rarity.
The ranking is by kinds found, then total catches, then whoever got there first. It updates as people catch, and a new #1 gets a burst of colour.
Players who caught brainrots before the leaderboard existed are added the next time they join.
Press J (or open the menu and pick Brainrots) to open your album.

A card for each brainrot, coloured by rarity. Ones you've caught show their 3D model (it turns to follow your mouse) and how many times you've caught it. Ones you haven't are a ? with their rarity.
Click a card to see it up close on the right, with its description, where it's found and when you first caught it. Clicking a caught one plays its voice, and ▶ Hear it plays it again.
The bar at the top shows how many of the fifteen you have.
Your album is saved with your character and stays with you when you die. J can be changed in Controls, under SkyRPG.

The Hallow's Crate opens on a spinning reel for candy, coins, the Hallowed Harvest set, scythes and the Jack o'Lantern pet. It only drops in the old survival world, so nobody can get one in SkyBlock today.

Crates are opened with a key: a long reel of prizes spins past a gold marker, ticking as it goes, slows down and stops on what you win, from blue (common) up to the gold ★ prizes. The first crate is the Hallow's Crate, for Halloween, which was meant to run until November 8.

Crates only dropped from monsters in the old survival world, which is now an archive, and the shop that sold keys is gone. In SkyBlock there is no way to get a Hallow's Crate or a Hallow's Key, so nothing in this page can be won today. An admin can still hand them out.
Each crate needs a Hallow's Key to open. Your first crate comes with a free key.

Right-click a crate (or a key) to see everything inside, with the chance of each tier. Press Open Crate (or Enter): it uses one crate and one key, and the reel spins for about 7 seconds. You get the prize when the reel stops (even if you close the screen or log off). Open Another spins again straight away.
The rarer tiers get a bigger fanfare, and Cursed and better prizes are announced to everyone on the server. Gold ★ prizes stay hidden on the reel as ★ Rare Special Item until one lands.
Treat (blue) | 64% | 8 Candy Corn, 4 Toffee Apple, a Pumpkin Pouch with 1,000 coins, or (half as likely) one with 2,500
Trick (purple) | 25% | One piece of the Hallowed Harvest set
Cursed (pink) | 8% | Reaper's Scythe, or the Jack o'Lantern pet (Epic)
Haunted (red) | 2.5% | The full Hallowed Harvest set, all four pieces
★ Hallowed (gold) | 0.5% | ★ Soulreaper, or the Jack o'Lantern pet (Legendary)

Candy is eaten for a 3-minute boost (a new candy replaces the last one; meals are separate): Candy Corn gives +25 Speed and +20 Farming Fortune, a Toffee Apple +30 Strength and +40 Health. A Pumpkin Pouch empties into your purse when you right-click it.
A Legendary set for Farming and Combat at once, only from crates. These are the survival game's items, not Hypixel's, so their stats and bonuses follow the survival rules:
Jack's Grin | 70 Health, 55 Defense, 18 Strength, 15 Crit Damage, 35 Farming Fortune
Hallowed Harvest Coat | 105 Health, 90 Defense, 26 Strength, 50 Farming Fortune
Scarecrow Trousers | 90 Health, 75 Defense, 20 Strength, 45 Farming Fortune
Gravewalk Boots | 55 Health, 45 Defense, 14 Strength, 8 Speed, 30 Farming Fortune

Witching Hour (all four pieces): +40 Farming Fortune and +20 Strength, and rare crop finds are 50% more likely. After dark in the old survival world it adds +60 Farming Fortune, +40 Strength and +30 Crit Damage more.
Both work as a weapon and as a scythe: they harvest an area of crops (replanting them) when you break one, and their right-click ability swings all the way round you.

Reaper's Scythe (Epic): 90 Damage, 50 Strength, 6% Crit Chance, 70 Farming Fortune; harvests a 3x3. Reap (35 Mana, 8 s): 55 damage to every monster within 4.5 blocks, and harvests the grown crops around you.
★ Soulreaper (Mythic): 200 Damage, 120 Strength, 12% Crit Chance, 50% Crit Damage, 160 Farming Fortune; harvests a 5x5, 15% chance to harvest twice. Soul Sweep (70 Mana, 14 s): 130 damage to every monster within 7 blocks, sets them on fire, heals you 3% of your health for each one hit, and harvests the grown crops around you.

A floating, grinning pumpkin that levels with Farming: +1.4 Farming Fortune and +0.6 Strength per level (at Common; Epic and Legendary give more). At level 25 rare crop finds are 25% more likely; at level 50 it heals you 2% of the melee damage you deal. It has no egg: crates are the only way to get one, which makes it unobtainable in SkyBlock for now. See Pets.
Hypixel's 87 pets - the Pets menu, levels 1 to 100, stats by rarity and level, pet XP from your skills and the Taming skill.

Pets float at your shoulder and give stats. Every one of Hypixel SkyBlock's 87 pets is in the game (Bee, Ender Dragon, Rock, Golden Dragon...), at the rarities Hypixel has them in, with their stats and abilities. A pet levels from 1 to 100 (the Golden Dragon to 200) as you gain skill XP.
A pet is an item: a head with the pet's face. Right-click it to add it to your pets; if you have none out, it's summoned straight away.

25 pets can be crafted (Bat, Blaze, Chicken, Endermite, Horse, Ocelot, Pigman, Rabbit, Sheep, Silverfish, Skeleton, Spider, Wither Skeleton, Wolf, Zombie and more): find them in the Recipe Book by name. A crafted pet starts at level 1. Pets can also be traded on the Auction House.
Open the Pets menu from the SkyBlock Menu or with /pets:

The pet you have out is on the card at the top. Put away sends it back.
Every other pet is in the grid below. Click one to summon it (the one out swaps places with it). Right-click one to take it back out as an item, to trade or sell.
Hover a pet for everything about it.
The pet you have out floats beside your shoulder, for everyone to see.

A pet's name shows its level: [Lvl 48] Bee. Its stats and its abilities' numbers grow in a straight line from level 1 to level 100, and a rarer pet has more of them. Its tooltip shows them at its level, and the progress to the next level.
A rarer pet needs more XP for each level: a Legendary pet starts further up Hypixel's pet XP table than a Common one.
Your summoned pet gets a share of all the skill XP you gain:
Its own skill (a Farming pet and Farming XP) | all of it
Its own skill, for a Mining or Fishing pet | one and a half times it
Taming: whatever your pet gets is also your Taming XP, and every Taming level gives your pets 1% more XP (Zoologist). See Skills.

Right-click a pet item while a pet is out to give it to that pet. A pet holds one item; the one it held before comes back to you. Its tooltip shows Held Item and what it does. Hypixel's pet items work the way their text says:
Stats | Big Teeth (+5 Crit Chance), Hardened Scales (+25 Defense), Sharpened Claws (+15 Crit Damage), Lucky Clover (+7 Magic Find), Saddle (+30 Speed), Spooky Cupcake (+30 Strength, +20 Speed)
More of the pet's own stats | Textbook (+100% of its Intelligence), Iron Claws (+40% of its Crit Damage and Crit Chance)
More pet XP | Skill Exp Boosts (+20% to +50% for one skill), All Skills Exp Boosts (+10% to +30% for all)
Rarity | Tier Boost: the pet's stats count as one rarity higher
A few (Flying Pig, Quick Claw, Exp Share...) show their text but don't work yet.
A pet's abilities work while it's out, with their numbers at its level and rarity (a Tier Boost counts). About a quarter of Hypixel's pet abilities work so far, on 48 of the 87 pets:
Stats | Black Cat's Magic Find and Pet Luck, Dolphin's Sea Creature Chance, Squid's Fishing Wisdom, Lion's Damage, Monkey's Foraging Fortune

Stats in a place or at a time | Chicken's Farming Fortune on public islands, Mithril Golem's Magic Find and combat stats on the mining islands, Monkey's Speed and Sweep in The Park, Bal's Pristine in the Magma Fields, Bat's Intelligence and Speed at night
Stats that grow | per player near you (Bee's Hive, Dolphin's Pod Tactics), per skill level (Rose Dragon, Ammonite), per digit of your Gold collection (Golden Dragon)
A share of your stats | Blue Whale's Max Health, Turtle's Defense, Tiger's Ferocity, Ender Dragon's combat stats and Magic Find, Griffin's Strength above 85% Health
Stats from other stats | Elephant's Defense per 100 Speed and Health per 10 Defense, Blue Whale's Defense per 20 Health, Ankylosaurus' Defense as Strength, Golden Dragon's Strength per 5 Magic Find

More damage | Ender Dragon to Ender mobs, Zombie to Undead, Wither Skeleton to Wither mobs, Magma Cube to slimes, T-Rex up close, Giraffe from afar, Megalodon to hurt enemies, Tiger to lone enemies, Pigman to Level 50+ and 100+ mobs, Skeleton's arrows, Golden Dragon per million coins in the bank
Less damage taken | Enderman from Ender mobs, Zombie from zombies, Wolf from wolves, Wither Skeleton from skeletons, Snowman from everything, Turtle under 40% Health

Abilities for places that aren't in the game yet (the Crimson Isle, the Garden, Jerry's Workshop, the Glacite Tunnels, dungeons) and ones with their own mechanics (Golem's Last Stand, Guardian's Laserbeam, Horse's Stampede, Combat Wisdom towards a mob...) show their text but don't work yet.

Kat, the pet sitter at a stall in the Hub's market, takes a pet up one rarity. Her menu lists your pets with what their next rarity costs: coins, sometimes items (Honey Dippers for a Bee, Summoning Eyes for an Ender Dragon), and a wait (from a minute to weeks, in real time, even while you're offline). Click a pet to give it to her; she looks after one pet at a time. When it's ready you get a message; open her menu and click it to take it back at its new rarity (it keeps its XP; its level follows the new rarity's table). All 216 of Hypixel's upgrades are there.
Not yet: the abilities above that don't work yet, Kat Flowers and Bouquets (to skip the wait), and the pets that come from drops, shops and events rather than recipes.
The menu key, how to move around the menu and every page in it.

Press K and one window opens with everything the pack adds: the SkyBlock Menu, your character, skills, slayers, storage, the Bazaar and Auction House, collections and settings. It has a sidebar of pages on the left and a dark custom look instead of vanilla screens. This page explains how to use the menu and lists every page, in the order they appear.
K | Open the menu, on the page you last used (the SkyBlock Menu the first time). Press again to close.
Esc | Step back inside a page, for example clear a search. Closes the menu when there is nowhere left to go back.
Up and Down arrows | Previous or next page
1 to 9 | Jump to one of the first nine pages
Click a page in the sidebar | Go there
Scroll wheel over the page | Scroll the page
Scroll wheel over the sidebar | Scroll the list of pages, when they don't all fit
A page with a text field, such as the Auction House, Bazaar, Party or Settings, takes digits and letters first.
The window fits itself to your screen. Settings, Interface, Menu size lets you pick Auto, Compact or Large. See Settings.
On a small screen nothing is out of reach:

When the pages don't all fit down the sidebar, the list scrolls. A thin scrollbar and a fade show where it is cut off, and picking a page with the keys scrolls it into view.
A page taller than the window scrolls inside it, with a scrollbar on the right. Tiles and cards keep a readable size instead of being squashed.
The sidebar lists the pages in this order:
SkyBlock Menu | The first page: everything on one board. See SkyBlock Menu
Profile | Your character and a tile for each stat
Stats | The main stats, grouped, with where each bonus comes from
Skills | A card for each skill
Calendar and Events | The SkyBlock date and what is on. See Calendar and events
Storage | Ender Chest pages and the Wardrobe. See Storage and Wardrobe
Fast Travel | Warps to your island, the Hub and the islands you have visited. See SkyBlock Menu
Pets | Your pet and your pet storage (admin-given only for now)
Party | Your party: members, health, where they are, invites
Collections | Gathered items and their tiers
Brainrots | Your brainrot album (also on J)
Wiki | This wiki, inside the game
Auction House | Buy and sell items. See Auction House
Bazaar | Instant trades and orders. See Bazaar
SkyBlock Leveling | Your SkyBlock Level and what it unlocks. See SkyBlock Leveling
Recipe Book | Every crafting recipe. See Recipe Book
SkyBlock Items | Every SkyBlock item. See SkyBlock items
Profile Management | Your profiles and co-ops. See Profiles and islands
The survival game's pages for Talents, Contracts, the Journal, Mounts, Titles and Pay are switched off in SkyBlock and do not show.
Your character is on the left. On the right is a tile for each thing the mods register:

Purse, the coins you carry.
SkyBlock Level, shown in aqua, which is also the badge in chat.
Skill Average.
One tile for every stat: Health, Defense, Strength, Crit Chance and so on.

Tiles fill one to three columns, depending on the window, and scroll when there are more than fit. A number too long for its tile is shortened, such as 1.23B. Hover to see it in full. See SkyBlock Leveling and Coins and the bank.
The main stats as tiles, in four groups:
Combat | Health, Defense, Strength, Crit Chance, Crit Damage, Speed, Intelligence
Gathering | Mining Speed, Mining Fortune, Farming Fortune, Foraging Fortune, Fishing Speed, Sea Creature Chance, Fishing Fortune
Wisdom | Farming, Mining, Foraging, Combat and Fishing Wisdom

Hover a tile to see what the stat does and where your bonuses come from: skills, gear, slayer levels, pets and your SkyBlock Level. Hypixel's other stats are on item tooltips but have no tile yet. See Stats.
A card for every skill with your level, an animated progress bar and your XP. Hover for your perk, what you have earned and what the next level gives. See Skills overview.

The overview has a card for each slayer line with your level, an XP bar, your boss kills per tier and any quest you are running. Click a line to see its level track (what each level gives and unlocks), the tiers (the boss, cost, rewards, drops and odds) and your own stats. See Slayers.

A live 3D preview of the selected pet, with its rarity, name, level and XP bar, its stats and perks, and your pet storage. Buttons: Equip, Unequip and Take out. Pets are only given out by admins at the moment. See Pets.

Your party's members, each on a card with their face, a crown for the leader, online or offline, health and where they are. Click a member to set a waypoint to them. The leader can Promote and Kick. There are buttons for Party chat, Leave and Disband, a name field to Invite a player, and your pending invites with Accept and Deny. See Party.
Tabs for each collection group. Each row shows an item's icon, your count, your tier, a bar to the next tier and what that tier unlocks. Hover a row for all its tiers. See Collections.

Your brainrot album: a card for each of the fifteen, with the 3D model of the ones you have caught and a ? for the rest. Click a card to see it up close and hear it say its name. J opens this page straight away. Brainrots cannot be caught in SkyBlock today. See Brainrots.
Every option, grouped by category, with a search box. See Settings.
These open from NPCs and blocks rather than the menu, but use the same look:

NPC shops, by right-clicking a merchant. See NPC shops.
The crafting table, by right-clicking one or typing /craft. See Recipe Book.
The Blacksmith and the anvil, for reforges and potato books. See Reforging.
Ender chests and the Wardrobe, by /ec and /wardrobe. See Storage and Wardrobe.
Minions, by right-clicking one. See Minions.
Slayer quests, by right-clicking Maddox. See Slayers.
This wiki is also inside the game. Look for Wiki in the menu, or type /wiki. Hover an item in any inventory and press H to jump to its entry. See Controls and keys.
The menu remembers the last page you used. Press K twice to go back to where you were.
