The themed chat: level badges, name cards, emotes, stickers, pictures, showcase tokens, whispers, mentions and chat settings.

SkyRPG restyles chat. Every message shows the sender's level and a hover card, you can show off your gear in a message, and you can post stickers and pictures that appear right in the chat window. It also removes the "Not Secure" marks and report buttons from player chat. This page covers everything you can type and see.
A player's message looks like this:

The level badge is a star and a number in brackets, such as (* 42). The number is the sender's SkyBlock Level (see SkyBlock Leveling). The colour changes every 40 levels: grey, white, yellow, green, dark green, aqua, dark aqua, blue, pink, purple, gold, red, and dark red from level 480. Hover a badge to see what the next colour is.
Staff titles. An administrator can give a player a title, shown as a small pill before the name: an icon and a few letters in a colour. Players cannot earn or pick titles in SkyBlock.
The name has a hover card with the player's level, skills, purse, slayers, pet and held item. Click a name to start a /msg to them.
A stripe beside each message shows its kind: player chat, whispers, joins, deaths, SkyRPG notices and more. Hover a stripe for the time.
Joins, leaves, deaths and advancements have their own themed lines, with icons. A new player gets a welcome that tells them to press the menu key.
Game messages about coins, skills, slayers and events have an icon, a short bold tag in an accent colour, then the text, for example SKILL, COINS and EVENT.

Messages with more to say come as one panel instead of a pile of lines: a level up and its rewards, a collection tier and what it unlocks, a SkyBlock level up, a new unique minion, your pet's details. The panel has a band in its colour behind the first line, a light body behind the rest, an edge on top and at the bottom, and a thin rail down its side, so it reads as one card.
Type one of these tokens anywhere in a message. It turns into a hoverable link that shows the real item tooltip.
[item] or [hand] | What you hold in your main hand
[offhand] | What you hold in your offhand
[armor] or [armour] | Every piece of armour you wear
An item shows its name in its rarity colour, with a rarity gem and, for stacks, x16. Empty hands show a grey [nothing].
Type a code and it turns into an icon or symbol. /emotes lists them all, and you can click one to use it. Among the codes:
The pixel icons draw as small sprites, and each skill has one. The rarity ones (:common: to :mythic:) show the same gems used on items.
Stickers are small pixel-art pictures. Type [s:name] (or [sticker:name]) and it shows as a picture in chat, such as gg [s:gg]. /stickers lists them, and a click puts a token in your chat box.
coins | coins raining onto a pile
An unknown name stays as plain text.

Run /share screenshot to show your newest screenshot to everyone. /share screenshot <file> shows a named one. The picture is scaled to at most 640 pixels and sent to every player with the mod. You can share one picture every 30 seconds. Players without the mod see the line without the picture.

Paste a link to a PNG, JPEG or GIF and it shows as a picture. Known sites load by themselves: imgur, Discord, Reddit, Tenor, Giphy and GitHub. Pictures from other sites show a "click to load" line if you chose Any site in the settings. GIFs show only their first frame. Pictures are capped at 4 MB.
Loading a picture from a link tells that site your internet address. Set Images from links to Off in Settings if you do not want that.

Click a picture in the open chat to see it full size. Esc or a click closes it. A message can hold up to three pictures. While one downloads you see [loading image...], and [image unavailable] if it fails.
Your name, or @yourname, in someone's message is highlighted and gives a soft ding. Whispers have their own softer ding. Both can be turned down in Settings.
/r <text> or /reply <text> | Reply to the last person who whispered you
Whispers have an envelope icon, a "From" or "To" label in their own pink-violet colour, and appear in the Whispers tab.

Party members have their own chat. /pc <message> sends one message to your party, and /party chat switches everything you type to the party until you run it again. Party lines have a green PARTY tag and a shield icon, and a crown before the leader's name. They show in All and in the Party tab. See Party.

SkyHelper is the server's assistant. Start a chat line with @skyhelper (or @helper) and a question, and it answers everyone in a few seconds. Its answers glow violet and teal with a few sparkles, so you can tell the AI is talking, and every item it names is a hoverable [item]. /ask <question> asks privately. See SkyHelper.

On the open chat window you get five tabs: All, Chat, Whispers, Party and SkyRPG. A tab is just a view of the same history. Closing the chat goes back to All. The Party tab holds only your party's chat and party notices, such as joins, leaves and invites. See Party.
All these options live in the menu under Settings, Chat. See Settings.
Themed chat box | On | SkyRPG colours and a framed panel instead of plain black
Message stripes | On | A coloured stripe by message kind
Timestamps | Off | Off, 12:34 or 12:34:56 before each message
Compact repeats | On | The same message in a row shows once, with a grey (x3)
Message spacing | 4 px | A gap between messages, from Off to 8 px. The lines of one long message stay together
Highlight mentions | On | Highlight and ding for your name or @name
Ping volume | 70% | How loud mentions and whispers ding. 0% is silent
Ding on whispers | On | A softer ding on whispers
Chat tabs | On | The All, Chat, Whispers, Party and SkyRPG tabs
Show images | On | Pictures inline in chat. Off shows only text
Images from links | Known sites | Known sites, Any site (click to load), or Off
Max image height | 7 lines | 3 to 12 chat lines
Show stickers | On | Stickers as pictures. Off leaves the token as you typed it
Turn Timestamps on while you play with friends across timezones or when you are checking when something happened. Hover a stripe to see the time without them.

Every HUD box, the HUD editor, the minimap, the world map and the look-at and info boxes.

The SkyRPG HUD is a set of small boxes drawn over the game: your purse, your skill progress, health, mana and Defense, the SkyBlock sidebar, the minimap and more. Every box can be moved, resized or hidden, and each shows only when it has something to say. This page lists them all, explains the HUD editor, and covers the minimap, the world map and the info boxes.
Purse | Top left | The coin icon and your purse
Skill progress | Top left | Appears for about 8 seconds after you gain skill XP: the skill, the XP gained, your progress to the next level and the XP rate
Health bar | Bottom centre | Your health, in SkyRPG's units
Mana bar | Bottom centre | Your mana
Minimap | Top right | The area around you. See below
Info (coordinates, biome, time) | Top right, under the minimap | Position, biome, day and time. See below
Look-at info | Top centre | What you are looking at. See below
Waypoint compass | Top centre | A compass ribbon pointing to your tracked waypoint. Only shows while you track one. See Waypoints
Events | Top right | Running admin events with a countdown bar and the top five. Only shows during an event
SkyBlock Sidebar | Middle right | Hypixel's scoreboard in SkyRPG's look: the real date, the SkyBlock date and time, where you are (such as ⏣ Coal Mine or Your Island) and your purse
Sidebar | Middle right | The vanilla scoreboard sidebar in SkyRPG's look. It only shows boards from admin events and commands; in normal play the SkyBlock Sidebar is what you see
Slayer Quest | Top left | Your running slayer quest and its timer. See Slayers
Fishing Bait | Bottom centre, above the hotbar | While you hold a fishing rod: the bait that would be used with how many are left (or "No bait"), and the hotspot your bobber is in. See Fishing
Party | Middle left | A row for each other party member: face, name, health bar, a dimension tag, and Offline when they are logged off. Only shows while you are in a party. See Party
Brainrot catches | Top left | A card for a few seconds when anyone on the server catches a brainrot: the catcher and the brainrot turning in 3D. Nothing triggers it in SkyBlock today. See Brainrots
Combat tag | Top centre, under the other boxes | A red "In combat" box with the seconds left (it blinks in the last 3), only while you are in combat. See Combat basics
All of them are on by default. Boxes with nothing to show stay hidden even when switched on. The editor always shows them so you can place them.

Banners slide in at the top of the screen for big moments, such as a skill or SkyBlock level up. They queue up.
Mob nameplates show the level and health of hostile mobs near you.
The winner board shows a podium with confetti when an event ends.
The vanilla hearts and armour row are hidden while the health bar is on screen. Switch it off to bring them back.
The XP text that normally appears above the hotbar ("+4 Farming") is replaced by the Skill progress box.
All of these have switches in Settings under HUD.
Open the menu, then Settings, HUD, Edit HUD layout.
Scroll over a box | Resize it, from half size to double size, in steps of 0.1
Right-click a box | Hide it, or show it again
R with the mouse over a box | Reset that box
R with the mouse over nothing | Reset every box
Esc | Finish. Your layout is saved.
Boxes pin to the nearest third of the screen, so your layout keeps its shape when you resize the window. Each box also has its own on and off switch in Settings under HUD.
The minimap is a small map of your surroundings in the top right.

It shows the blocks around you, in the colour of their own textures, so paths, roofs and flowers are visible.
Other players are shown as their faces and you are an arrow.
NPCs and your waypoints appear as icons.
Zoom with = and -. There are five levels, from a quarter of a pixel per block to four pixels per block. The zoom is remembered for each dimension. In the Hub it starts zoomed in.
By default north is up. Turn the minimap with you makes the way you face point up.
Cave view: when you are underground, the minimap shows the floor around you instead of the surface, and gets darker the deeper you go.
Waypoints outside the view show as an arrow on the rim.
The minimap can be switched off in Settings under Map.
Press M to open the map of everything you have explored in this dimension (the Hub, your island and each public island are separate dimensions).
Hover an icon | See what it is
Right-click the map | Drop a waypoint
Click or right-click an icon | Track, share in chat, or remove it if it is your waypoint
Zoomed in, names show under the icons. Every NPC is on the map with their face, name and role, even when they are too far away to load.
Explored map is saved on your own computer in the skyrpg/maps/ folder of your game folder, for each server and dimension. See Waypoints.
A box at the top centre shows what you are looking at, up to 12 blocks away.

Blocks: the name, which mod it comes from, how grown a crop is, whether a mining node has regrown, and whether your tool can harvest it.
Mobs and players: their health, and a player's ping.
NPCs: their role.

Under the minimap. It shows your coordinates and the way you are facing, the biome, the day and the time on a 24-hour clock, and optionally the frames per second. Each line has its own switch in Settings under Info, and FPS is off by default.

Hold Tab for the SkyRPG player list: heads and ping on the left, info panels on the right. Every player's SkyBlock Level badge sits before their name, in the same tier colour as in chat, for everyone online, near or far. Names themselves are plain white. Switch the list back to vanilla in Settings under Interface.
If the HUD feels crowded, hide boxes you do not use in the editor rather than turning the whole HUD off. Everything you hide can be brought back there.
The whole HUD can be turned off with SkyRPG HUD in Settings under HUD.

Controls and keys
Named, coloured points on your maps and in the world: how to make, track and share them.

A waypoint is a named, coloured point that you save. It shows on your minimap and world map, and as a marker in the world, so you can find your way back to an island spot, a farm, a mine or a friend. You can track one to get a compass at the top of the screen that points the way. Waypoints are kept on your own computer, per server and per dimension. The Hub, the Private Islands and each public island are separate dimensions, so a waypoint only shows on the island where you made it.
/wp is a shortcut for /waypoint. Without coordinates the waypoint is placed where you stand. Put names with spaces in quotes, such as /wp add "My Base".

If you add a waypoint with a name you already have, it replaces the old one and keeps its colour. New ones take the next colour in a cycle of eight: gold, aqua, purple, green, red, blue, orange and white.
Press M, then right-click an empty spot on the map. A small dialog asks for a name and one of the eight colours. Click or right-click any existing icon for a menu.
When you die, a red waypoint called Last death is added where it happened. The next death replaces it.
/wp add <name> [x y z] | Save a waypoint
/wp list | List the waypoints in this dimension, with distance and clickable Track, Share and Remove buttons
/wp track <name> <x> <y> <z> | Track any spot, without saving it
On the world map, click an icon to open a popup with Track, Share in chat and, for your own waypoints, Remove.

On the minimap: a coloured marker. If a waypoint is off the edge, an arrow on the rim points to it. The tracked one is drawn larger.
In the world: a diamond with the name and distance, such as "Base 142m". It fades in as you get closer, from faint at 2 blocks to solid at 16. When it is off-screen or behind you, an arrow at the screen edge points to it.
On the world map: the same colour as everywhere else, with its name when you zoom in.
You can track one thing at a time. The tracked target:

Always shows in the world, with a white ring round its diamond.
Gets a compass ribbon at the top centre of the screen. It shows N, E, S and W, a diamond for the target, an arrow at the end when it is behind you, the name, the distance, and whether it is above or below you.
Is cleared when you get within 3 blocks of it, with a message "You've arrived at...", or when you leave the server.
Only shows in its own dimension.
/wp share <name>, or Share in chat on the map, posts this in chat:

Players with the mod see clickable Add and Track buttons next to it. The coordinates are taken to be in the dimension the reader is in, so only share a waypoint from the dimension you are both in. Names are shortened to 32 characters.
In the menu under Settings, Map, in the Waypoints section:
Waypoints in the world | On | The diamond with the name and distance. The tracked one always shows.
Waypoints on the minimap | On | The markers and the edge arrows
Waypoint distance | 2,000 blocks | How far away a waypoint still shows in the world and as an arrow. 100 to 5,000. The top setting is Unlimited
Waypoint marker size | 10 px | How big the diamond in the world is, 6 to 24
NPCs and waypoints, under the same category, turns the icons on both maps on or off. See Settings.
Make a waypoint at your island's best spots, at the mine or farm you use most and at anything rare you find. /wp list then works as a quick way back: click Track and follow the compass.

Parties of up to 8 players: they are saved, show each other's health on an overlay, share a chat tab and cannot hurt each other.

A party is a group of up to 8 players who play together. A party is saved: log out, come back tomorrow, and you are still in it. Party members see each other's health in a small overlay, talk in their own chat tab, can set a waypoint to each other and cannot hurt each other.

Type /party invite <player>, or open the Party page in the K menu, type their name and press Invite.
They get a line in chat with clickable [Accept] and [Deny]. An invite lasts 60 seconds.
When they accept, the party exists. You are its leader.
Anyone in the party can invite more people, up to 8 in all. You can only be in one party at a time. Joins, leaves, kicks, promotions and members logging in and out are announced to the whole party.
/party invite <player> | Invite a player (60 seconds to answer)
/party accept [player] | Accept an invite. Say the inviter's name if you have several
/party promote <player> | Make a member the leader (leader only)
/party disband | Break the party up for everyone (leader only)
/party list or /party | Show the members and who is online
/party chat <message> | Send one message to the party
/party chat | Switch your chat to party chat, and back

The party stays together while members are offline. An offline member keeps their seat and shows as Offline on the overlay, with the place they logged out. If the leader leaves, the member who has been in the party longest becomes the leader. If only one member would be left, the party disbands.
Party chat and the Party tab
Party chat and the Party tab

Messages to the party and party notices (joins, leaves, invites) appear in chat with a green PARTY tag and a shield icon. They are in All and in the Party tab of the chat window, between Whispers and SkyRPG. The tab gets a dot when a party line arrives while you are on another tab. See Chat.
Party chat and the Party tab
Run /party chat once and everything you type goes to the party until you run it again. It also switches off when you leave the party or log out.
A small box on the left of the screen shows every other member:

Their face, taken from their skin, and their name. The leader has a crown.
A health bar with the numbers, in SkyRPG's units (the same as your own health bar). It is green, turns gold under half and red and pulsing under a quarter.
A small tag naming where they are when it is not where you are: Hub, Islands (the Private Islands), Farming islands (The Barn and the Mushroom Desert), The park, Gold mine, Deep caverns or Spiders den.
Offline members are greyed out, and their bar says Offline.
It is a normal HUD box: move, resize or hide it in the HUD editor. See HUD and minimap. It only shows while you are in a party.

Open the menu and choose Party. Each member has a card with their face, crown, whether they are online, health, and where they are (place, coordinates and distance, or where they were last seen when offline).

Click a member to set a waypoint to them. See Waypoints.
The leader sees Promote and Kick on each member (Kick asks for a second click).
Party chat, Leave and, for the leader, Disband are buttons at the top. Leave and Disband ask for a second click.
Invite a player has a name field. Pending invites you have received show at the top with Accept and Deny.
Hold Tab. Party members have a green mark beside their face, and a Party panel lists everyone with their health.

Party members cannot hurt each other. The hit is cancelled, with no damage and no knockback. It covers melee, arrows and other projectiles (the shooter counts, not the arrow), thrown potions that hurt, abilities and area attacks, and a tamed animal hitting for its owner. You can still hurt yourself.
A few things are not stopped: poison or wither that keeps ticking after a thrown potion, fire, and TNT.

The Settings page: every category, every option and its default, and how to search and reset.

The Settings page in the menu holds every option the pack adds, in one place. Options are grouped into categories with a search box on top, and changes take effect straight away. Settings are saved on your own computer, in config/skyrpg/client.json in your game folder, so they belong to you, not the server.
Open the menu with K (or your own key), then Settings. It is the last page in the sidebar, and there is also a Settings tile in the SkyBlock Menu.

Categories are listed down the left, each with an icon. Click one to see its options on the right.
Search. Type in the search box at the top of the left side, and the page searches every category at once. It matches names, descriptions and keywords, so "ding" finds the mention sound.
Toggles switch on click. Choices step through their options. Sliders can be dragged. Buttons, such as Edit HUD layout, run an action.
Reset to defaults is a button above a category's list. It appears once you have changed something in that category, asks for a second click within 3 seconds, then resets the category.
Some options have sections, such as Look or Mentions in Chat, to keep long categories readable.
Tab and Shift+Tab | Move between the search box, the categories and the settings
Arrow keys | Move inside the pane that has focus
Enter or Space | Change a setting
Left and Right arrows | Adjust a choice or a slider
/ or Ctrl+F | Jump to the search box
Esc | Step back: clear the search, leave a pane, then close the menu

The page shows Interface, HUD and Gameplay first. The other categories follow: Chat, Map, Info, Effects, Builder and Brainrots. Builder and Brainrots belong to extras that cannot be reached in SkyBlock today, so they only matter if an admin gives you a Builder Station.
Menu size | Auto | How big the menu is. Auto fits it to your monitor. Compact and Large are the other choices
SkyRPG tab list | On | Players and your profile info when you hold Tab. Off brings back vanilla's list
SkyRPG sidebar | On | Draws the vanilla scoreboard sidebar (admin event boards) in the SkyRPG look. The SkyBlock sidebar is a HUD box, switched in the HUD category
SkyRPG theme for all screens | On | Restyles Minecraft's own menus, buttons and inventories to match SkyRPG
Classic stat symbols | Off | Shows stats with the original heart, star and similar symbols instead of SkyRPG's pixel icons
SkyRPG title screen | On | The SkyRPG start screen with the Play button instead of Minecraft's. Takes effect the next time the title screen opens. See First launch and setup
Show the setup again | Button | Opens the first-time setup: performance preset, shaders, resource packs, keys and the main settings

Detailed weapon art | On | Detailed, animated art for swords, pickaxes, spears, bows and shields. Off brings back the plain 16-pixel look. SkyBlock items get their Hypixel look from FurfSky Reborn, which has no setting; see SkyBlock items
The theme, symbol and weapon art options swap resource packs, so the game reloads its resources when you change them. It does not restart.
SkyRPG HUD | On | Master switch for the info boxes
Edit HUD layout | Button | Opens the HUD editor: drag, resize and hide every box
One switch per box | On | Show or hide each box. The boxes are listed on HUD and minimap
Big moment banners | On | A banner when you level up a skill or your SkyBlock Level, and at other milestones
Mob nameplates | On | The level and health over the mobs near you
Hide skill XP text | On | The Skill progress box replaces the "+4 Farming" text above the hotbar
Replace hearts with health bar | On | Hides vanilla's hearts and armour row. The health bar and the Defense box show them instead
Event winner board | On | The podium with confetti when an admin event ends

Thirteen options for the look of chat, mentions, tabs and pictures. They are explained on Chat.
Minimap | On | The small map in the top right

Players on the map | On | Other players' faces on both maps
NPCs and waypoints | On | Icons for NPCs, your waypoints and more on both maps

The last four are in a Waypoints section. See Waypoints.
Look-at info | On | What you are looking at, top centre

Effects quality | High | Particle effects on gear, mobs and pets. Choose Off, Low or High. Off saves the most frames

Catch announcements | Card and voice | When anyone catches a brainrot (nothing triggers it in SkyBlock today): a card with them and the brainrot in 3D plus its voice, the card only, or nothing. See Brainrots
On a slow computer, set Effects quality to Low or Off first. It is the biggest gain for the least loss. Then try turning off Weapon particles.
If the chat feels busy, turn off Message stripes and Show images. To stop the game loading pictures from outside sites at all, set Images from links to Off.
If your window is small, set Menu size to Compact. On a big monitor, Large gives the menu more room.
Where a setting says "Known sites", those are imgur, Discord, Reddit, Tenor, Giphy and GitHub.

The in-game assistant: ask it about SkyRPG SkyBlock in chat, and it answers from the wiki in a few seconds.

SkyHelper is SkyRPG's assistant. Ask it a question in chat and it answers within a few seconds, using what this wiki says: where to sell something, how to craft an item, where an island is, what a stat does, what to do next. It runs on the server's own computer as a small AI model, so it costs nothing and nothing you ask leaves the server.
@skyhelper <question> in chat | Everyone: your question and its answer
While it works, "✦ SkyHelper is thinking..." shows above your hotbar. The answer looks different from everything else in chat, so you always know the AI is talking:
SkyHelper lines show in the All and Chat tabs, with a light-blue stripe (see Chat). The glow needs the Themed chat box setting, which is on by default.
SkyHelper never runs commands itself. When a command would do what you asked, it offers it as a green [▶ /command] button:

@skyhelper invite PhilipSGamer to my party gives [▶ /party invite PhilipSGamer].
An operator asking @skyhelper make it day gets [▶ /time set day]. Anyone else is told only an operator can do that.

Clicking a button runs the command as you, with your own permissions, so a button can never do more than you could by typing it. Buttons only show to the player who asked, even when the answer is public, so nobody can get SkyHelper to put a button in front of someone else. Hover a button to see exactly what it runs.
SkyHelper sees what you are holding, what you carry and wear, where you are (the Hub, an island or the old survival world, and the biome), your health, mana, coins, skill levels and stats. So:

"this", "it" and "my item" mean the item in your hand. Hold a Aspect of the End and ask @skyhelper how do I reforge this?.
"What should I do next?" gets an answer for your levels and your gear.
It remembers your last three questions for 15 minutes, so you can follow up: "and where do I find that?"
It cannot give items or coins, or change the game itself; at most it offers a command button (see below).

Prices, NPC shops, the Bazaar and the Auction House.
Recipes: SkyBlock's crafting recipes, and vanilla recipes (pistons, furnaces, anything) read from the game itself.
Where things are: islands, areas, NPCs and warps.
How systems work: skills, stats, slayers, minions, collections, reforging, parties, profiles.
Plain Minecraft questions (redstone, brewing, mobs).
It is a small model, so it can still get something wrong. If an answer looks odd, click [Wiki] and check the page. The wiki is always the final word.

You can ask once every 8 seconds, and one question at a time.
Questions longer than 400 characters are cut.
If SkyHelper is offline you get "I'm asleep right now". Try again in a minute; the server starts it again on its own.

SkyHelper is the skyrpg_helper mod plus a small service, tools/skyhelper/helper.py, which asks a local Ollama model (qwen3.5:9b by default). The server starts the service when it starts and stops it when it stops. The service reads the in-game wiki files, so every wiki rebuild teaches SkyHelper the new content.
/skyhelper status | Whether the service and Ollama are running (operators)
/skyhelper start | Start the service if it is not running (operators)

Settings are in config/skyrpg/helper.json: enabled, url, cooldownSeconds, timeoutSeconds, autostart, python and script. Every question and answer is logged to run/skyhelper/log.jsonl, to find answers worth improving. python tools/skyhelper/eval.py asks a set of test questions and checks the answers.

Every enchantment, what it applies to and what it does at its top level.
Enchantments come from the enchanting table (up to the table level shown) or as tomes. Ultimate enchants are tome-only and an item can hold just one. The effect column shows the maximum level.
Bountiful | Hoe | V | While farming, a 0.7% chance per crop for a Bountiful harvest: +200 Farming Fortune for 15 seconds. Very rare find while farming.
Final Stand | Armor | V | Below 40% health, take 12% less damage (all pieces add up, to 60% at most). Very rare drop: the Broodmother (tier III+).
Heartwood Surge | Axe | V | While chopping, a 0.8% chance per log for a Heartwood Surge: +200 Foraging Fortune for 15 seconds. Very rare find while foraging.
Leviathan's Favor | Rod | V | Each catch has a 8% chance to win the Leviathan's favour: +20% Sea Creature Chance for 30 seconds. Very rare find while fishing.
Motherlode | Pickaxe | V | While mining, a 0.8% chance per ore to strike a Motherlode: +200 Mining Fortune for 15 seconds. Very rare find while mining.
Phoenix Ember | Chestplate | V | Once every 180 seconds, a killing blow sets you alight instead: you rise again with 40% health. Very rare drop: the world boss.
Rift Echo | Sword | V | Every fifth hit tears the air: a moment later the target is struck again for 80% of it. Very rare drop: the Void Stalker (tier III+).
Soulrend | Sword | V | Each kill binds a soul to you for 20 seconds (up to 10); every soul adds 3% damage. Very rare drop: the Grave Tyrant (tier III+).
Starshot | Bow | V | Every fourth arrow becomes a falling star, bursting for 150% of its damage on everything within 4 blocks. Very rare drop: the Bone Marshal (tier III+).
Titanbane | Sword | V | +45% damage to anything with more max health than you.
Unbreakable | Tool, Rod | I | The tool takes no durability damage, ever. Enchanting table (Enchanting 22), or a rare tome from slayer and world bosses.
